2.25.s:
2.121
rāma uvāca ..
narakādyānti tiryaktvaṃ tato mānuṣyameva ca ..
teṣāṃ cihnāni me brūhi mānuṣye varuṇātmaja ..1..
2.25.d:
2.121
राम उवाच ॥
नरकाद्यान्ति तिर्यक्त्वं ततो मानुष्यमेव च ॥
तेषां चिह्नानि मे ब्रूहि मानुष्ये वरुणात्मज ॥1॥
2.25.m: 2.121 / Rāma said: / From hell they enter animal existence, and from there human existence. / Tell me the signs of these [past sins] in human existence, O son of Varuṇa.

2.25.s:
puṣkara uvāca .. maṇimuktāpravālāni ratnāni vividhāni ca ..
apahṛtya naro rāma jāyate hemakartṛṣu .. 2 ..
2.25.d:
पुष्कर उवाच ॥ मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानि रत्नानि विविधानि च ॥
अपहृत्य नरो राम जायते हेमकर्तृषु ॥ 2 ॥
2.25.m: Puṣkara said: / Having stolen gems, pearls, corals, and various kinds of jewels, / a man is born among goldsmiths, O Rāma.

2.25.s:
yadvā tadvā paradravyamapahṛtya naro balāt ..
prāpnoti bhṛguśārdūla mānuṣye bhāravāhitām .. 3 ..
2.25.d:
यद्वा तद्वा परद्रव्यमपहृत्य नरो बलात् ॥
प्राप्नोति भृगुशार्दूल मानुष्ये भारवाहिताम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.25.m: Having forcibly seized another's property, whatever it may be, / a man attains the state of a load-carrier in human life, O tiger among the Bhṛgus.

2.25.s:
yaṃ kañcid ghātayitvāpi prāṇinaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
māṃsaṃ bhuktvā tu dharmajña bhavatīha gadāturaḥ .. 4 ..
2.25.d:
यं कञ्चिद् घातयित्वापि प्राणिनं भृगुनन्दन ॥
मांसं भुक्त्वा तु धर्मज्ञ भवतीह गदातुरः ॥ 4 ॥
2.25.m: Even having caused any living being whatsoever to be killed, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and eaten its flesh, O knower of dharma, he becomes afflicted with disease here.

2.25.s:
suvarṇacoraḥ kunakhī surāpaḥ śyāvadantakaḥ ..
brahmahā kṣayarogī syāhuścarmā gurutalpagaḥ .. 5 ..
2.25.d:
सुवर्णचोरः कुनखी सुरापः श्यावदन्तकः ॥
ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगी स्याहुश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 5 ॥
2.25.m: A thief of gold has deformed nails; a wine-drinker has dark teeth; / a slayer of a brahmin becomes consumptive; one who defiles his guru's bed gets bad skin;

2.25.s:
piśunaḥ pūtināsaḥ syātsūcakaḥ pūtivaktrakaḥ ..
dhānyacauroṅgahīnaḥ syādavyaṅgo miśrahṛdbhavet .. 6 ..
2.25.d:
पिशुनः पूतिनासः स्यात्सूचकः पूतिवक्त्रकः ॥
धान्यचौरोङ्गहीनः स्यादव्यङ्गो मिश्रहृद्भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.25.m: a slanderer has a foul-smelling nose; an informer has a foul mouth; / a thief of grain becomes deficient in limbs; one who mixes adulterants becomes whole-limbed [yet diseased];

2.25.s:
vyādhitaścānnahartā syānmūko vāgapahārakaḥ ..
vastrāpahārakaḥ śvitrī paṅguścāśvāpahārakaḥ .. 7 ..
2.25.d:
व्याधितश्चान्नहर्ता स्यान्मूको वागपहारकः ॥
वस्त्रापहारकः श्वित्री पङ्गुश्चाश्वापहारकः ॥ 7 ॥
2.25.m: a stealer of food becomes diseased; a stealer of speech becomes mute; / a stealer of clothes gets vitiligo; and a stealer of horses becomes lame.

2.25.s:
khalvāṭo matsarī rāma nāstiko vedanindakaḥ ..
bhūya eva samāpnoti tathā nāstikatāṃ dvija .. 8..
2.25.d:
खल्वाटो मत्सरी राम नास्तिको वेदनिन्दकः ॥
भूय एव समाप्नोति तथा नास्तिकतां द्विज ॥ 8॥
2.25.m: An envious man becomes bald, O Rāma; an atheist and reviler of the Vedas / repeatedly attains atheism again [in rebirth], O twice-born;

2.25.s:
andho dīpāpahārī syātkāṇo nirvāpakastathā ..
andho bhavati goghnastu ghāṇṭikastailikastathā .. 9 ..
2.25.d:
अन्धो दीपापहारी स्यात्काणो निर्वापकस्तथा ॥
अन्धो भवति गोघ्नस्तु घाण्टिकस्तैलिकस्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
2.25.m: a stealer of a lamp becomes blind; one who extinguishes [a lamp] becomes one-eyed; / and a cow-killer becomes blind, as does a bell-maker and an oil-presser;

2.25.s:
daridraḥ paravittaghno unmattaśca tathāgnidaḥ ..
pratikūlo guroryastu so'pasmārī prajāyate .. 2.121.10 ..
2.25.d:
दरिद्रः परवित्तघ्नो उन्मत्तश्च तथाग्निदः ॥
प्रतिकूलो गुरोर्यस्तु सोऽपस्मारी प्रजायते ॥ 2.121.10 ॥
2.25.m: one who destroys another's wealth becomes poor, and an arsonist becomes insane; / while he who is hostile to his guru is born epileptic.

2.25.s:
miṣṭāśyeko mahābhāga vātagulmī bhavennaraḥ ..
khagabhakṣyastu kuṇḍāśī dīrgharogī ca pīḍakaḥ .. 11 ..
2.25.d:
मिष्टाश्येको महाभाग वातगुल्मी भवेन्नरः ॥
खगभक्ष्यस्तु कुण्डाशी दीर्घरोगी च पीडकः ॥ 11 ॥
2.25.m: A man who eats sweets alone, O illustrious one, develops an abdominal swelling caused by wind; / an adulterer's parasite who eats food offered to him becomes food for birds; and an oppressor contracts a chronic disease.

2.25.s:
bhavatīha mṛgavyādhastvavikreyasya vikrayāt ..
ślīpadī cāvakīrṇī syānmūrkhaścākrośako bhavet ..12..
2.25.d:
भवतीह मृगव्याधस्त्वविक्रेयस्य विक्रयात् ॥
श्लीपदी चावकीर्णी स्यान्मूर्खश्चाक्रोशको भवेत् ॥12॥
2.25.m: A person becomes a hunter here by selling what should not be sold; / a celibate student who has broken his vow gets elephantiasis; and one who reviles [others] becomes a fool.

2.25.s:
uktāstu mukhyā hi mayā tiraścāṃ yā yonayo yāni ca lakṣaṇāni ..
śakyaṃ na kārtsyena mayā pravaktuṃ yā yātanāścaiva narādhamānām ..13..
2.122
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
etacchrutvā yaduśreṣṭha rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ ..
papāta bhuvi niśceṣṭaśchinnamūla iva drumaḥ .. .. 1 ..
taṃ visaṃjñaṃ mahābhāga pīnonnatapayodharāḥ ..
sacandanaiḥ śītajalaiḥ siṣicurdevayoṣitaḥ .. 2 ..
vāruṇerājñayā cānyāstālavṛntairmanoramaiḥ ..
vījayanti mahābhāga rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam .. 3 ..
labdhasaṃjñaṃ muhūrtena bhārgavaṃ cittavihvalam ..
āśvāsayāmāsa tadā vāruṇiḥ paravīrahā .. 4 .. .
samāśvastastato rāmaḥ papraccha varuṇātmajam ..
durgātitaraṇaṃ vīro rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .. 5 ..
rāma uvāca .. ..
kliśyamāneṣu bhūteṣu taistairbhāvaistatastataḥ ..
durgāṇyatitaredyena brūhi me varuṇātmaja .. 6 ..
2.25.d:
उक्तास्तु मुख्या हि मया तिरश्चां या योनयो यानि च लक्षणानि ॥
शक्यं न कार्त्स्येन मया प्रवक्तुं या यातनाश्चैव नराधमानाम् ॥13॥
2.122
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा यदुश्रेष्ठ रामो रतिकरः पितुः ॥
पपात भुवि निश्चेष्टश्छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
तं विसंज्ञं महाभाग पीनोन्नतपयोधराः ॥
सचन्दनैः शीतजलैः सिषिचुर्देवयोषितः ॥ 2 ॥
वारुणेराज्ञया चान्यास्तालवृन्तैर्मनोरमैः ॥
वीजयन्ति महाभाग रामं धर्मभृतां वरम् ॥ 3 ॥
लब्धसंज्ञं मुहूर्तेन भार्गवं चित्तविह्वलम् ॥
आश्वासयामास तदा वारुणिः परवीरहा ॥ 4 ॥ ।
समाश्वस्तस्ततो रामः पप्रच्छ वरुणात्मजम् ॥
दुर्गातितरणं वीरो रामो धर्मभृतां वरः ॥ 5 ॥
राम उवाच ॥ ॥
क्लिश्यमानेषु भूतेषु तैस्तैर्भावैस्ततस्ततः ॥
दुर्गाण्यतितरेद्येन ब्रूहि मे वरुणात्मज ॥ 6 ॥
2.25.m:
The principal animal wombs and their signs have indeed been spoken by me; / nor is it possible for me to declare in full the torments of the lowest of men.
2.122 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard this, O best of the Yadus, Rāma, who gave delight to his father, / fell lifeless to the ground like a tree cut down at the root.
Celestial maidens with full, raised breasts sprinkled him / who was unconscious, O illustrious one, with cool water mixed with sandalwood.
And by command of the son of Varuṇa, other [maidens] fanned / Rāma, the best of the upholders of dharma, with beautiful palm-leaf fans, O illustrious one.
When the descendant of Bhṛgu whose mind was distraught regained consciousness in a moment, / the son of Varuṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, comforted him then.
Then, being comforted, the heroic Rāma, the best of the upholders of dharma, / asked the son of Varuṇa about crossing over distresses.
Rāma said: / When living beings are afflicted everywhere by various states of mind, / tell me, O son of Varuṇa, that by which one may cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
puṣkara uvāca ..
āśrameṣu yathokteṣu yathoktaṃ te dvijātayaḥ ..
vartante saṃyatātmāno durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 7 ..
ye dambhānna jahatīha yeṣāṃ vṛttiśca saṃvṛtā ..
viṣayām̐śca na gṛhṇanti durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 8 ..
vāsayantyatithīnnityaṃ nityaṃ ye cānasūyakāḥ ..
nityaṃ svādhyāyaśīlāśca durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 9 ..
mātāpitrośca ye vṛttiṃ vartante dharmakovidāḥ ..
varjayanti divāsvāpaṃ durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 2.122.10 ..
sveṣu dāreṣu vartante nyāyavṛttimṛtāvṛtau ..
agnihotraparāḥ santo durgāṇyati taranti te .. 11 ..
āhaveṣu ca ye śūrāstyaktvā maraṇajaṃ bhayam ..
dharmeṇa jayamicchanti durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 12 ..
ye pāpāni na kurvanti karmaṇā manasā girā ..
nikṣiptadaṇḍā bhūtānāṃ durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 13 ..
2.25.d:
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आश्रमेषु यथोक्तेषु यथोक्तं ते द्विजातयः ॥
वर्तन्ते संयतात्मानो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 7 ॥
ये दम्भान्न जहतीह येषां वृत्तिश्च संवृता ॥
विषयाम्̐श्च न गृह्णन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 8 ॥
वासयन्त्यतिथीन्नित्यं नित्यं ये चानसूयकाः ॥
नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलाश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 9 ॥
मातापित्रोश्च ये वृत्तिं वर्तन्ते धर्मकोविदाः ॥
वर्जयन्ति दिवास्वापं दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 2.122.10 ॥
स्वेषु दारेषु वर्तन्ते न्यायवृत्तिमृतावृतौ ॥
अग्निहोत्रपराः सन्तो दुर्गाण्यति तरन्ति ते ॥ 11 ॥
आहवेषु च ये शूरास्त्यक्त्वा मरणजं भयम् ॥
धर्मेण जयमिच्छन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 12 ॥
ये पापानि न कुर्वन्ति कर्मणा मनसा गिरा ॥
निक्षिप्तदण्डा भूतानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 13 ॥
2.25.m:
Puṣkara said: / Those twice-born who abide properly in the prescribed stages of life, / self-restrained, cross over distresses.
Those who do not abandon [dharma] here out of hypocrisy, whose livelihood is concealed, / and who do not grasp sense-objects, cross over distresses.
Those who always lodge guests, who are always free from malice, / and who are constantly devoted to personal study of the Vedas, cross over distresses.
Those who, skilled in dharma, follow the conduct of their mother and father, / and avoid sleeping by day, cross over distresses.
Being devoted to the agnihotra, those who engage with their own wives / in lawful intercourse in every fertile period cross over distresses.
Those who, brave in battles, having abandoned the fear born of death, / desire victory through righteousness, cross over distresses.
Those who do not commit sins in deed, thought, or word, / and have laid down their staff against living beings, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
karmāṇyakuhakārthāni yeṣāṃ vācaśca sūnṛtāḥ ..
yeṣāmarthaśca sādhvartho durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 14 ..
2.25.d:
कर्माण्यकुहकार्थानि येषां वाचश्च सूनृताः ॥
येषामर्थश्च साध्वर्थो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 14 ॥
2.25.m: Those whose actions are devoid of deceit, whose words are pleasant and truthful, / and whose wealth is for the purpose of the virtuous, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
ye tapaśca tapasyanti kaumārabrahmacāriṇaḥ ..
vidyāvedavratasnātā durgāṇyatitaranti te .. 15 ..
2.25.d:
ये तपश्च तपस्यन्ति कौमारब्रह्मचारिणः ॥
विद्यावेदव्रतस्नाता दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥ 15 ॥
2.25.m: Those celibates from their youth who perform ascetic austerities, / and who have bathed at the completion of their vows and study of the Vedas, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
yeṣāṃ na kaścittrasati trasyanti na ca kasyacit ..
yeṣāmātmasamo loko durgāṇyatitaranti te..16..
2.25.d:
येषां न कश्चित्त्रसति त्रस्यन्ति न च कस्यचित् ॥
येषामात्मसमो लोको दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥16॥
2.25.m: Those from whom no one trembles in fear, and who fear no one, / to whom the world is equal to their own self, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
paraśriyā na tapyante santaḥ puruṣasattamāḥ ..
grāmyāsvāda nivṛttāśca durgāṇyatitaranti te..17..
2.25.d:
परश्रिया न तप्यन्ते सन्तः पुरुषसत्तमाः ॥
ग्राम्यास्वाद निवृत्ताश्च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥17॥
2.25.m: Those good men, the best of persons, who are not tormented by the prosperity of others / and have turned away from vulgar sensory pleasure, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
sarvāndevānnamasyanti sarvāndharmāṃśca śṛṇvate ..
ye śraddadhānāḥ puruṣā durgāṇyatitaranti te..18..
2.25.d:
सर्वान्देवान्नमस्यन्ति सर्वान्धर्मांश्च शृण्वते ॥
ये श्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥18॥
2.25.m: Those men of faith who bow to all the gods / and listen to all dharmas, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
ye na lobhānnayantyarthānrājāno rajasā vṛtāḥ ..
viṣayānparirakṣanto durgāṇyatitaranti te..19..
2.25.d:
ये न लोभान्नयन्त्यर्थान्राजानो रजसा वृताः ॥
विषयान्परिरक्षन्तो दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥19॥
2.25.m: Those kings who, [though] enveloped in passion, do not take wealth out of greed, / [and who succeed in] protecting their realms, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
ye na mānitumicchanti mānayanti ca ye narān ..
mānyamānānnamasyanti durgāṇyatitaranti te ..2.122.20..
2.25.d:
ये न मानितुमिच्छन्ति मानयन्ति च ये नरान् ॥
मान्यमानान्नमस्यन्ति दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥2.122.20॥
2.25.m: Those who do not desire to be honored, yet honor other men / and bow down to those who are being honored, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
ye ca śrāddhāni kurvanti tithyāṃtithyāṃ prajārthinaḥ ..
suviśuddhena manasā durgāṇyatitaranti te..21..
2.25.d:
ये च श्राद्धानि कुर्वन्ति तिथ्यांतिथ्यां प्रजार्थिनः ॥
सुविशुद्धेन मनसा दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥21॥
2.25.m: And those who, desiring offspring, perform ancestral rites on each lunar day / with a completely pure mind, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
ye krodhaṃ naiva kurvanti krodhārtaṃ śamayanti ca ..
na ca kupyanti bhṛtyānāṃ durgāṇyatitaranti te..22..
2.25.d:
ये क्रोधं नैव कुर्वन्ति क्रोधार्तं शमयन्ति च ॥
न च कुप्यन्ति भृत्यानां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥22॥
2.25.m: Those who do not give way to anger, who calm one afflicted by anger, / and do not become angry at their servants, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
madhu māṃsaṃ ca ye nityaṃ varjayantīha mānavāḥ..
janmaprabhṛti madyaṃ ca durgāṇyatitaranti te..23..
2.25.d:
मधु मांसं च ये नित्यं वर्जयन्तीह मानवाः॥
जन्मप्रभृति मद्यं च दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते॥23॥
2.25.m: Those men who here constantly avoid honey and meat, / as well as liquor from birth, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
yātrārthaṃ bhojanaṃ yeṣāṃ santānārthaṃ ca maithunam ..
vāk satyavacanārthāya durgāṇyatitaranti te ..24..
2.25.d:
यात्रार्थं भोजनं येषां सन्तानार्थं च मैथुनम् ॥
वाक् सत्यवचनार्थाय दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥24॥
2.25.m: Those whose eating is only for sustenance, intercourse is only for offspring, / and speech is only for speaking truth, cross over distresses.

2.25.s:
taḍāgārāmakartārastathānye vṛkṣaropakāḥ ..

2.123
राम उवाच ॥
भूय एव समाचक्ष्व कर्मणा येन मानवाः ॥
दुर्गाण्यतितरन्त्याशु सर्वधर्मभृतां वर ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
दुर्गाण्यतितरन्त्याशु ये नरा कृच्छ्रकारिणः ॥
प्राप्नुवन्ति तथा कामान्सर्वान्वै मनसेप्सितान् ॥ 2 ॥
राम उवाच ॥
कृच्छ्राणां श्रोतुमिच्छामि नामानि च विधींस्तथा ॥
एवं मे ब्रूहि धर्मज्ञ त्वं हि वेत्सि यथातथम् ॥ 3 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
कृच्छ्राण्येतानि कार्याणि राम वर्णत्रयेण च ॥
कृच्छ्रेष्वेतेषु शूद्रस्य नाधिकारो विधीयते ॥ 4 ॥
आदौ तु मुण्डनं कार्यं सर्वकृच्छ्रे भार्गव ॥
नित्यं त्रिषवणस्नानं केशवस्य च पूजनम् ॥ 5 ॥
2.25.m:
"From kings, thieves, serpents, fire, brahmins, bad dreams, wicked deeds, death, or rivals, / no fear arises among men who are devotees of the sole Master of the universe, the Enemy of Madhu."
2.123 / Rāma said: / Tell me further by what action men / quickly cross over difficulties, O best of all upholders of dharma.
Puṣkara said: / Men who perform penances quickly cross over difficulties, / and they obtain all desires cherished in the mind.
Rāma said: / I wish to hear the names and the procedures of the penances; / speak thus to me, O knower of dharma, for you know [them] as they truly are.
Puṣkara said: / These penances are to be performed, O Rāma, by the three castes; / for a śūdra, no eligibility is prescribed in these penances.
At the beginning, tonsure is to be performed in every penance, O Bhārgava, / bathing at the three junctures of the day constantly, and the worship of Keśava,

एतद्वीरासनं प्रोक्तं महापातकनाशनम् ॥ 2.123.10 ॥
आमिक्षया तु द्वौ मासौ पक्षं तु पयसा तथा ॥
अष्टरात्रं तथा दध्ना त्रिरात्रमथ सर्पिषा ॥ 11 ॥
निराहारस्त्रिरात्रं तु कुर्याद्वा तालकव्रतम् ॥
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वकामप्रदं तथा ॥ 12 ॥
2.25.m:
an oblation with purifying mantras, and recitation at the conclusion; / and one should avoid conversation with women, śūdras, and outcasts.
This is to be done in all penances without distinction; / and the hero's posture is to be observed, whether by desire or not.
A penance accompanied by the hero's posture becomes multiplied in virtue; / without the hero's posture, it is said to be deficient in procedure.
Rāma said: / I wish to hear about the hero's posture from you, O one of good vows, / since a penance accompanied by the hero's posture is multiplied in virtue.
Puṣkara said: / One should remain standing by day and seated at night; / this is declared to be the hero's posture, destroying great sins.
For two months on curd-mixture, a fortnight on milk, / eight nights on curds, and three nights on ghee,
and fasting without food for three nights, one should perform the vātālaka vow, / which pacifies all sins and grants all desires.

स्नपयेदात्मनोऽर्थाय पावकं भृगुनन्दन ॥
वह्नौ ततो'ऽनुजुहुयाद्दद्यादन्नञ्च कस्यचित् ॥ 13 ॥
ब्रह्मा देवेति मन्त्रेण साध्यमाने विचक्षणः ॥

श्रितं च श्राप्यमाणं च भाण्डे न्यस्त तथा पुनः ॥
अनेन राम मन्त्रेण नरस्त्रिरभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
यवोऽसि धान्यराजोऽसि वारुणो मधुसंयुतः ॥

मातुर्गुरोरशुश्रूषा सर्वं पुनीत मे यवाः ॥ 19 ॥
2.25.m:
One should bathe the fire for one's own sake, O descendant of Bhṛgu; / one should then offer into the fire and give food to someone.
While it is being prepared with the mantra 'brahmā devāḥ,' a wise man / should tie darbha grasses for protection; so is our traditional learning.
Over that which is boiled, being boiled, and placed in the vessel, / a man should consecrate it three times with this mantra, O Rāma:
"You are barley, you are the king of grains, sacred to Varuṇa, mixed with honey; / the dispeller of all sins, remembered by the sages as a purifier.
Ghee is barley, honey is barley, water indeed is nectar, barley; / purify all my sin, whatever misdeed has been done by me:
done by speech, done by action, a bad dream, an evil thought; / and destroy misfortune; purify all, O grains of barley!
What has been licked by a dog or a boar, and what is brought as leftovers, / non-attendance upon mother and teacher—purify all, O grains of barley!

2.25.m:
Food of a multitude, food of a courtesan, food of a śūdra, and of merchants, / food of a thief, a new funeral feast—purify all, O grains of barley!
Behavior [improper for] a child, adharma, and what is done [improperly] in the duties of a king, / theft of gold, non-vow observance, sacrificing for one unfit to sacrifice,
slander of brahmins—purify all, O grains of barley!" / This is the mantra over what has been placed in the vessel, and then he should proclaim:
("Those gods born of the mind, yoked by the mind, of great skill, whose fathers are skilled—may they protect us, may they help us; to them, svāhā!") / With this, O knower of dharma, one should always offer into oneself with restraint; / one should not overindulge; for this is the barley-gruel vow.
For three nights for one desiring intelligence; six nights for a great sinner; / seven nights is prescribed for one guilty of a secondary sin, O tamer of enemies;
and for one guilty of a great sin, twice six nights is handed down; / by twenty-one nights, he attains desired wishes;
by a month, he obtains liberation from all sins without doubt. / By performing this very [vow] with barley grains retrieved from cow dung,

māsena sākṣāttridaśānvedānvidyāśca paśyati .. 27 ..
varaśāpasamarthastu tathā bhavati bhārgava ..
śuklapakṣasamārambhādārabhetpratyahaṃ naraḥ .. 28 ..
ekaikavṛddhyā hyaśnīyātpiṇḍāñśrīkhaṇḍasaṃyutān ..
ekaikaṃ hrāsayetkṛṣṇe pratipatprabhṛti kramāt .. 29 ..
haviṣyasya mahābhāga nāśnīyāccandrasaṃkṣaye ..
etaccāndrāyaṇaṃ proktaṃ yavamadhyaṃ mahātmabhiḥ .. 2.123.30 ..
etadeva viparyastaṃ vajramadhyaṃ prakīrtitam ..
aṣṭabhiḥ pratyahaṃ grāsairyaticāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam .. 31 ..
prātaścaturbhiḥ sāyaṃ ca śiśucāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam ... .
yathākathaṃcitpiṇḍānāṃ catvāriṃśacchatadvayam .. 32 ..
māsena bhakṣayedetatsuracāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam ..
gokṣīraṃ saptarātraṃ tu pibetstanacatuṣṭayam .33.
2.25.d:
फलं प्राप्नोति धर्मज्ञ तथा दशगुणं ध्रुवम् ॥
मासेन साक्षात्त्रिदशान्वेदान्विद्याश्च पश्यति ॥ 27 ॥
वरशापसमर्थस्तु तथा भवति भार्गव ॥
शुक्लपक्षसमारम्भादारभेत्प्रत्यहं नरः ॥ 28 ॥
एकैकवृद्ध्या ह्यश्नीयात्पिण्डाञ्श्रीखण्डसंयुतान् ॥
एकैकं ह्रासयेत्कृष्णे प्रतिपत्प्रभृति क्रमात् ॥ 29 ॥
हविष्यस्य महाभाग नाश्नीयाच्चन्द्रसंक्षये ॥
एतच्चान्द्रायणं प्रोक्तं यवमध्यं महात्मभिः ॥ 2.123.30 ॥
एतदेव विपर्यस्तं वज्रमध्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
अष्टभिः प्रत्यहं ग्रासैर्यतिचान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥ 31 ॥
प्रातश्चतुर्भिः सायं च शिशुचान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥॥
यथाकथंचित्पिण्डानां चत्वारिंशच्छतद्वयम् ॥ 32 ॥
मासेन भक्षयेदेतत्सुरचान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥
गोक्षीरं सप्तरात्रं तु पिबेत्स्तनचतुष्टयम् .33.
2.25.m:
he certainly gains ten times the fruit, O knower of dharma; / in a month, he sees face-to-face the gods, the Vedas, and the sciences,
and he becomes capable of granting boons and curses, O Bhārgava. / Beginning from the start of the bright fortnight, a man should begin day by day:
He should eat balls [of food] mixed with sandalwood, increasing by one each day; / in the dark [fortnight], he should decrease [them] by one in succession, beginning from the first day.
On the disappearance of the moon, O fortunate one, he should eat nothing of sacrificial food; / this is declared by the great-souled ones as the barley-middle cāndrāyaṇa.
This very [vow] reversed is proclaimed as the thunderbolt-middle; / with eight morsels every day, it is handed down as the ascetic's cāndrāyaṇa.
With four in the morning and [four] in the evening, it is handed down as the child's cāndrāyaṇa; / in whatever manner, two hundred and forty balls [in all].
If one consumes this over a month, it is known as the suracāndrāyaṇa.
For seven nights, one should drink cow's milk from four teats;

2.25.s:
stanatrayātsaptarātraṃ saptarātraṃ stanadvayāt ..
stanāttathaiva ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātraṃ vāyubhugbhavet .. 34 ..
etatsomāyanaṃ nāma vrataṃ kalmaṣanāśanam ..
tryahaṃ pibedapastūṣṇāstryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pibet .. 35 ..
2.25.d:
स्तनत्रयात्सप्तरात्रं सप्तरात्रं स्तनद्वयात् ॥
स्तनात्तथैव षड्रात्रं त्रिरात्रं वायुभुग्भवेत् ॥ 34 ॥
एतत्सोमायनं नाम व्रतं कल्मषनाशनम् ॥
त्र्यहं पिबेदपस्तूष्णास्त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पिबेत् ॥ 35 ॥

2.25.s:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā vāyubhakṣyo bhavettrayaham ..
taptakṛcchramidaṃ proktaṃ śītaiḥ śītaṃ prakīrtitam .. 36 ..
2.25.d:
त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पीत्वा वायुभक्ष्यो भवेत्त्रयहम् ॥
तप्तकृच्छ्रमिदं प्रोक्तं शीतैः शीतं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.25.m:
having drunk warm ghee for three days, one should subsist on air for three days.
This is declared to be the taptakṛcchra; with cold [liquids] it is proclaimed as the śīta[kṛcchra].

2.25.s:
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatīn ..
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam .. 37 ..
2.25.d:
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतीन् ॥
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् ॥ 37 ॥
2.25.m:
The kṛcchrātikṛcchra is performed with milk for twenty-one days.
Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, water with kuśa grass,

2.25.s:
ekarātropavāsaśca kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ smṛtam ..
etacca pratyahābhyastaṃ mahāsāntapanaṃ smṛtam .. 38 ..
2.25.d:
एकरात्रोपवासश्च कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं स्मृतम् ॥
एतच्च प्रत्यहाभ्यस्तं महासान्तपनं स्मृतम् ॥ 38 ॥
2.25.m:
and fasting for a single night: this is known as the sāntapana kṛcchra.
And when this is practiced every day [in succession], it is known as the mahāsāntapana.

2.25.s:
kṛcchraṃ parākasaṃjñaṃ syāddvādaśāhamabhojanam ..
ekabhuktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca .. 39 ..
2.25.d:
कृच्छ्रं पराकसंज्ञं स्याद्द्वादशाहमभोजनम् ॥
एकभुक्तेन नक्तेन तथैवायाचितेन च ॥ 39 ॥
2.25.m:
Fasting for twelve days is the penance named parāka.
By eating once [a day], by [eating only] at night, and likewise by [eating only food] unasked-for,

2.25.s:
upavāsena caikena kṛcchrapādaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
etadeva trirabhyastaṃ śiśukṛcchraṃ prakīrtitam .. 2.123.40 ..
2.25.d:
उपवासेन चैकेन कृच्छ्रपादः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
एतदेव त्रिरभ्यस्तं शिशुकृच्छ्रं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 2.123.40 ॥
2.25.m:
and with a single fast, a kṛcchrapāda is proclaimed.
This very [practice] repeated three times is proclaimed as the śiśukṛcchra.

2.25.s:
tryahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahaṃ prātastryahamadyādayācitam ..
tryahaṃ paraṃ ca nāśnīyātprājāpatyaṃ carandvijaḥ .. 41 ..
2.25.d:
त्र्यहं सायं त्र्यहं प्रातस्त्र्यहमद्यादयाचितम् ॥
त्र्यहं परं च नाश्नीयात्प्राजापत्यं चरन्द्विजः ॥ 41 ॥
2.25.m:
For three days in the evening, for three days in the morning, for three days one may eat unasked-for [food],
and for three days beyond that one must not eat: [thus] a twice-born performs the prājāpatya.

2.25.s:
piṇyākācāmatakrāmbusaktūnāṃ prativāsaram ..
ekaikamupavāsaṃ ca saumyakṛcchaṃ prakīrtitam .. 42 ..
2.25.d:
पिण्याकाचामतक्राम्बुसक्तूनां प्रतिवासरम् ॥
एकैकमुपवासं च सौम्यकृच्छं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 42 ॥
2.25.m:
On each day, respectively: oil-cake, gruel, buttermilk-water, roasted barley meal,
and a single fast: this is proclaimed as the saumyakṛcchra.

2.25.s:
ambusiddhaistathā māsaḥ kevalairvāruṇaṃ samaiḥ ..
phalairmāsena kathitaṃ phalakṛcchraṃ manīṣibhiḥ .. 43 ..
2.25.d:
अम्बुसिद्धैस्तथा मासः केवलैर्वारुणं समैः ॥
फलैर्मासेन कथितं फलकृच्छ्रं मनीषिभिः ॥ 43 ॥
2.25.m:
Likewise, a month with [food] cooked in water, alone, in equal portions, is the vāruṇa [penance].
A month with fruits is declared by the wise as the phalakṛcchra.

2.25.s:
śrīkṛcchraṃ śrīphalaiḥ proktaṃ padmākṣairaparaṃ tathā ..
māsamāmalakaireva śrīkṛcchramaparaṃ smṛtam 44 ..
2.25.d:
श्रीकृच्छ्रं श्रीफलैः प्रोक्तं पद्माक्षैरपरं तथा ॥
मासमामलकैरेव श्रीकृच्छ्रमपरं स्मृतम् 44 ॥
2.25.m:
The śrīkṛcchra is proclaimed [to be performed] with bilva fruits; another [is performed] with lotus seeds;
and another śrīkṛcchra is remembered [to be performed] for a month with only myrobalan fruits.

2.25.s:
patrairmataṃ patrakṛcchraṃ puṣpaistatkṛcchramucyate ..
mūlakṛcchraṃ tathā mūlaistoyakṛcchraṃ jalena tu .. 45 ..
2.25.d:
पत्रैर्मतं पत्रकृच्छ्रं पुष्पैस्तत्कृच्छ्रमुच्यते ॥
मूलकृच्छ्रं तथा मूलैस्तोयकृच्छ्रं जलेन तु ॥ 45 ॥
2.25.m:
With leaves, it is considered the patrakṛcchra; with flowers, that penance is called [puṣpakṛcchra];
likewise, the mūlakṛcchra with roots, and the toyakṛcchra with water.

2.25.s:
dadhnā kṣīreṇa takreṇa piṇyākena kaṇaistathā ..
śākairmāsaṃ tu kāryāṇi sunāmāni vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 46 ..
2.25.d:
दध्ना क्षीरेण तक्रेण पिण्याकेन कणैस्तथा ॥
शाकैर्मासं तु कार्याणि सुनामानि विचक्षणैः ॥ 46 ॥
2.25.m:
With curd, with milk, with buttermilk, with oil-cake, and with grain-tips,
and with vegetables, for a month: auspiciously named [penances] should be performed by the discerning.

2.25.s:
sāyaṃ prātastu bhuñjāno naro yo nāntarā pibet ..
ṣaḍabhirvarṣairidaṃ proktaṃ kṛcchraṃ nityopavāsitā .. 47 ..
2.25.d:
सायं प्रातस्तु भुञ्जानो नरो यो नान्तरा पिबेत् ॥
षडभिर्वर्षैरिदं प्रोक्तं कृच्छ्रं नित्योपवासिता ॥ 47 ॥
2.25.m:
A man who, eating in the evening and the morning, does not drink in between:
this is declared to be the penance of perpetual fasting for six years.

2.25.s:
ekabhaktena māsena kathitaṃ caikabhaktakam ..
na tu kṛcchraṃ tu naktena mahatsaṃvatsarādbhavet .. 48 ..
2.25.d:
एकभक्तेन मासेन कथितं चैकभक्तकम् ॥
न तु कृच्छ्रं तु नक्तेन महत्संवत्सराद्भवेत् ॥ 48 ॥
2.25.m:
With a single meal [daily] for a month, it is declared as the aikabhaktika.
A great penance does not result from [eating only] at night except after a year.

2.25.s:
naktāśinastu dharmajña ekabhuktasya vā punaḥ ..
tryahaṃ vopavasedyuktaḥ snāyīta savanatrayam..49..
2.25.d:
नक्ताशिनस्तु धर्मज्ञ एकभुक्तस्य वा पुनः ॥
त्र्यहं वोपवसेद्युक्तः स्नायीत सवनत्रयम्॥49॥
2.25.m:
For one who eats at night, O knower of dharma, or again for one who eats once [a day],
or one who, disciplined, fasts for three days and bathes at the three ritual junctions,

2.25.s:
nimnavatsu tathaivāpsu triḥ paṭhedaghamarṣaṇam .. .
devatābhāvavṛttastu cchandaścaivāpyanuṣṭubham .. 2.123.50 ..
2.25.d:
निम्नवत्सु तथैवाप्सु त्रिः पठेदघमर्षणम् ॥ ।
देवताभाववृत्तस्तु च्छन्दश्चैवाप्यनुष्टुभम् ॥ 2.123.50 ॥
2.25.m:
one should recite the Aghamarṣaṇa [hymn] three times in flowing waters.
Adopting the state of the deity, with the anuṣṭubh meter,

2.25.s:
saṃsmarettasya ca tathā ṛṣiṃ caivāghamarṣaṇam ..
caturthe'hani dātavyā brāhmaṇāya tapasvine .. 51 ..
2.25.d:
संस्मरेत्तस्य च तथा ऋषिं चैवाघमर्षणम् ॥
चतुर्थेऽहनि दातव्या ब्राह्मणाय तपस्विने ॥ 51 ॥
2.25.m:
and one should also remember its seer, Aghamarṣaṇa.
On the fourth day, [a cow] should be given to an ascetic brahmin.

2.25.s:
tryahaṃ japedyathāśakti śuciścaivāghamarṣaṇam ..
bhāvavṛttastathā devastathā ca puruṣaḥ paraḥ .. 52 ..
2.25.d:
त्र्यहं जपेद्यथाशक्ति शुचिश्चैवाघमर्षणम् ॥
भाववृत्तस्तथा देवस्तथा च पुरुषः परः ॥ 52 ॥
2.25.m:
Purified, one should recite the Aghamarṣaṇa according to one's ability for three days.
Likewise, the deity is the Creator, and likewise the supreme Cosmic Person.

2.25.s:
taddaivatyaṃ vijānīyātsūktaṃ tadaghamarṣaṇam ..
yathāśvamedhaḥ kraturāṭ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ .. 53 ..
2.25.d:
तद्दैवत्यं विजानीयात्सूक्तं तदघमर्षणम् ॥
यथाश्वमेधः क्रतुराट् सर्वपापापनोदनः ॥ 53 ॥
2.25.m:
One should know that Aghamarṣaṇa hymn to have that deity.
Just as the horse-sacrifice is the king of sacrifices, dispelling all sins,

2.25.s:
tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
kṛṣṇājinaṃ vā kutapaṃ paridhāyātha valkalam..54..
2.25.d:
तथाघमर्षणं सूक्तं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
कृष्णाजिनं वा कुतपं परिधायाथ वल्कलम्॥54॥
2.25.m:
so the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn destroys all impurities.
Wearing a black antelope skin, or a woolen blanket, or bark garments,

2.25.s:
saṃvatsaraṃ vrataṃ kuryātsammitaṃ nāma bhārgava ..
gṛhaṃ na praviśettatra bhavedākāśaśāyakaḥ .. 55 ..
2.25.d:
संवत्सरं व्रतं कुर्यात्सम्मितं नाम भार्गव ॥
गृहं न प्रविशेत्तत्र भवेदाकाशशायकः ॥ 55 ॥
2.25.m:
one should observe for a year the vow named sammita, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
There he should not enter a house; he should sleep beneath the open sky.

2.25.s:
aśaktau vā bhavedrāma tathā śailaguhāśayaḥ ..
nityaṃ triṣavaṇasnāyī tathā syāddvijasattama..56..
2.25.d:
अशक्तौ वा भवेद्राम तथा शैलगुहाशयः ॥
नित्यं त्रिषवणस्नायी तथा स्याद्द्विजसत्तम॥56॥
2.25.m:
Or, in case of inability, O Rāma, he may sleep in a mountain cave.
He should constantly bathe at the three ritual junctions, O best of the twice-born.

2.25.s:
bhaikṣyaśākaphalāhāraḥ kāmaṃ syāddvijapuṅgava ..
vīrāsanaṃ tathā kuryātkāṣṭhamaunaṃ tathaiva ca..57..
2.25.d:
भैक्ष्यशाकफलाहारः कामं स्याद्द्विजपुङ्गव ॥
वीरासनं तथा कुर्यात्काष्ठमौनं तथैव च॥57॥
2.25.m:
His food may freely consist of alms, vegetables, and fruits, O bull among the twice-born;
and he should practice the hero's posture, and likewise absolute silence.

2.25.s:
sarvakāmapradaṃ hyetatsarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
vāyavyaṃ kṛcchramuktaṃ tu pāṇipūrānnabhojinaḥ .. 58 ..
2.25.d:
सर्वकामप्रदं ह्येतत्सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
वायव्यं कृच्छ्रमुक्तं तु पाणिपूरान्नभोजिनः ॥ 58 ॥
2.25.m:
For this grants all desires and destroys all impurities.
The vāyavya penance is declared for one who eats food filling [only] his palm,

2.25.s:
māsenaikena dharmajña sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
tilairdvādaśarātreṇa kṛcchramāgneyamucyate .. 59 ..
2.25.d:
मासेनैकेन धर्मज्ञ सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
तिलैर्द्वादशरात्रेण कृच्छ्रमाग्नेयमुच्यते ॥ 59 ॥
2.25.m:
over one month, O knower of dharma, destroying all impurities.
A penance with sesame seeds for twelve nights is called the āgneya.

2.25.s:
lājāprasṛtimapyekāṃ kanakena samanvitām ..
bhuñjānasya tathā māsaṃ kṛcchraṃ dhanadadaivatam .. 2.123.60 ..
2.25.d:
लाजाप्रसृतिमप्येकां कनकेन समन्विताम् ॥
भुञ्जानस्य तथा मासं कृच्छ्रं धनददैवतम् ॥ 2.123.60 ॥
2.25.m:
For one eating just a handful of fried grain mixed with gold
for a month, that is the penance whose deity is the Giver of Wealth.

2.25.s:
gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktairyavaiḥ saktūnsamantrataḥ ..
yāmyaṃ kṛcchraṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ māsena bhṛgunandana .. 61 ..
2.25.d:
गवां निर्हारनिर्मुक्तैर्यवैः सक्तून्समन्त्रतः ॥
याम्यं कृच्छ्रं विनिर्दिष्टं मासेन भृगुनन्दन ॥ 61 ॥
2.25.m:
With roasted barley flour [made from] barley passed through the dung of cows, accompanied by mantras,
the yāmya penance is prescribed for a month, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.25.s:
gomūtreṇa caretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ gomayamācaret ..
gavāṃ madhye sadā tiṣṭhedgopurīṣe ca saṃvaset..62..
2.25.d:
गोमूत्रेण चरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं गोमयमाचरेत् ॥
गवां मध्ये सदा तिष्ठेद्गोपुरीषे च संवसेत्॥62॥
2.25.m:
One should bathe with cow's urine; one should maintain one's livelihood with cow dung;
one should always stay in the midst of cows and reside among cow dung.

2.25.s:
goṣvatṛptāsu na pibedudakaṃ bhṛgunandana ..
abhuktāsu tu nāśrīyādutthitāsūtthito bhavet..63..
2.25.d:
गोष्वतृप्तासु न पिबेदुदकं भृगुनन्दन ॥
अभुक्तासु तु नाश्रीयादुत्थितासूत्थितो भवेत्॥63॥
2.25.m:
When the cows are not satisfied, he must not drink water, O descendant of Bhṛgu;
when they have not eaten, he must not eat; when they stand up, he should stand up;

2.25.s:
tathā caivopaviṣṭāsu sarvāsūpaviśennaraḥ ..
māsenaikena kathitaṃ gomūtraṃ kalmaṣāpaham .. 64 ..
2.25.d:
तथा चैवोपविष्टासु सर्वासूपविशेन्नरः ॥
मासेनैकेन कथितं गोमूत्रं कल्मषापहम् ॥ 64 ॥
2.25.m:
and when all of them sit down, the man should sit down.
Performed for one month, this [penance of] cow's urine is declared to remove impurities.

2.25.s:
ajākṛcchraṃ tathaivaitadajāmadhye tu vartataḥ ..
tṛṇānāṃ bhakṣaṇeneha samatulyaphale ubhe .. 65 ..
2.25.d:
अजाकृच्छ्रं तथैवैतदजामध्ये तु वर्ततः ॥
तृणानां भक्षणेनेह समतुल्यफले उभे ॥ 65 ॥
2.25.m:
Likewise, the ajākṛcchra is for one living in the midst of goats;
by eating grass here, both yield an equal fruit.

2.25.s:
dvādaśāhena kathitaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam ..
upoṣitaścaturdaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāmanantaram .. 66 ..
2.25.d:
द्वादशाहेन कथितं सर्वपातकनाशनम् ॥
उपोषितश्चतुर्दश्यां पञ्चदश्यामनन्तरम् ॥ 66 ॥
2.25.m:
It is declared to destroy all cardinal sins in twelve days.
Having fasted on the fourteenth day, immediately on the fifteenth

2.25.s:
pañcagavyaṃ samaśnīyāddhaviṣyāśī tvanantaram ..
brahmakūrcamidaṃ kuryāduktapraśamanāya vai .. 67 ..
2.25.d:
पञ्चगव्यं समश्नीयाद्धविष्याशी त्वनन्तरम् ॥
ब्रह्मकूर्चमिदं कुर्यादुक्तप्रशमनाय वै ॥ 67 ॥
2.25.m:
one should consume pañcagavya, and thereafter eat sacrificial food.
One should perform this brahmakūrca indeed for the pacification of what has been spoken of.

2.25.s:
pakṣānte tvatha vā kāryaṃ māsamadhye tu vā punaḥ ..
brahmakūrcaṃ naraḥ kuryātpaurṇamāseṣu yaḥ sadā ..68..
2.25.d:
पक्षान्ते त्वथ वा कार्यं मासमध्ये तु वा पुनः ॥
ब्रह्मकूर्चं नरः कुर्यात्पौर्णमासेषु यः सदा ॥68॥
2.25.m:
Or it should be done at the end of a fortnight, or again in the middle of the month.
A man who always performs the brahmakūrca on full moon days,

2.25.s:
tasya pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti durbhuktādi na saṃśayaḥ ..
māsābhyāṃ ca naraḥ kṛtvā brahmakūrcaṃ samāhitaḥ .. 69 ..
2.25.d:
तस्य पापं क्षयं याति दुर्भुक्तादि न संशयः ॥
मासाभ्यां च नरः कृत्वा ब्रह्मकूर्चं समाहितः ॥ 69 ॥
2.25.m:
his sin arising from eating forbidden food and the like is destroyed, without doubt.
And having performed the brahmakūrca for two months with a concentrated mind,

2.25.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto yatheṣṭāṃ gatimāpnuyāt ..
brahmabhūtamamāvasyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tathaiva ca .. 2.123.70 ..
2.25.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो यथेष्टां गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
ब्रह्मभूतममावस्यां पौर्णमास्यां तथैव च ॥ 2.123.70 ॥
2.25.m:
a man, completely freed from all sins, attains whatever destination he desires.
On the new moon day and likewise on the full moon day, having become one with Brahman,

2.25.s:
yogabhūtaṃ paricaretkeśavaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
evametāni kṛcchrāṇi kathitāni mayā tava ..71 ..
2.25.d:
योगभूतं परिचरेत्केशवं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
एवमेतानि कृच्छ्राणि कथितानि मया तव ॥71 ॥
2.25.m:
he should serve Keśava, absorbed in yoga; he shall attain greatness.
In this way, these penances have been told by me to you

2.25.s:
śāsanānīha pāpānāṃ duritānāṃ ca bhārgava ..
saṃvatsarasyaikamapi caretkṛcchraṃ dvijottamaḥ .. 72 ..
2.25.d:
शासनानीह पापानां दुरितानां च भार्गव ॥
संवत्सरस्यैकमपि चरेत्कृच्छ्रं द्विजोत्तमः ॥ 72 ॥
2.25.m:
as the punishments for sins and misdeeds here, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
A best of the twice-born should perform even a single penance each year,

2.25.s:
ajñātabhuktaśuddhyarthaṃ jñātasya tu viśeṣataḥ ..
ajñātaṃ yadi vā jñātaṃ kṛcchraṃ pāpaṃ viśodhayet .. 73 ..
2.25.d:
अज्ञातभुक्तशुद्ध्यर्थं ज्ञातस्य तु विशेषतः ॥
अज्ञातं यदि वा ज्ञातं कृच्छ्रं पापं विशोधयेत् ॥ 73 ॥
2.25.m:
for the purification of what was eaten unknowingly, and especially of what was known.
Whether unknown or known, a penance purifies the sin.

2.25.s:
kṛcchrasaṃśuddhapāpānāṃ narakaṃ na vidhīyate ..
śrīkāmaḥ puṣṭikāmaśca svargakāmastathaiva ca .. 74 ..
2.25.d:
कृच्छ्रसंशुद्धपापानां नरकं न विधीयते ॥
श्रीकामः पुष्टिकामश्च स्वर्गकामस्तथैव च ॥ 74 ॥
2.25.m:
Hell is not ordained for those whose sins are purified by penance.
One desiring prosperity, one desiring nourishment, and likewise one desiring heaven,

2.25.s:
devatārādhanaparastathā kṛcchraṃ samācaret ..
rasāyanāni mantrāśca tathā caivauṣadhāśca ye .. 75 ..
2.25.d:
देवताराधनपरस्तथा कृच्छ्रं समाचरेत् ॥
रसायनानि मन्त्राश्च तथा चैवौषधाश्च ये ॥ 75 ॥
2.25.m:
intent on worshipping deities, should likewise perform a penance.
Elixirs, mantras, and whatever medicines there are,

2.25.s:
tasya sarve hi sidhyanti yo naraḥ kṛcchrakṛdbhavet ..
vaidikāni ca karmāṇi yāni kāmyāni kānicit .. 76 ..
2.25.d:
तस्य सर्वे हि सिध्यन्ति यो नरः कृच्छ्रकृद्भवेत् ॥
वैदिकानि च कर्माणि यानि काम्यानि कानिचित् ॥ 76 ॥
2.25.m:
all of them indeed succeed for that man who performs penance,
as well as whatever Vedic rites are performed for desired results.

2.25.s:
sidhyanti sarvāṇi sadā kṛcchrakarturbhṛgūttama ..
tejasā tasya saṃyogo mahatā caiva jāyate .. 77 ..
2.25.d:
सिध्यन्ति सर्वाणि सदा कृच्छ्रकर्तुर्भृगूत्तम ॥
तेजसा तस्य संयोगो महता चैव जायते ॥ 77 ॥
2.25.m: always succeed for one who performs the kṛcchra penance, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / and he becomes united with great brilliance.

2.25.s:
vāñchitānmānasānkāmānsa cāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ ..
jñāto bhavati deveṣu tathā carṣigaṇeṣu ca ..
vipāpmā vitamaskaśca saṃśuddhaśca viśeṣataḥ ..78..
2.25.d:
वाञ्छितान्मानसान्कामान्स चाप्नोति न संशयः ॥
ज्ञातो भवति देवेषु तथा चर्षिगणेषु च ॥
विपाप्मा वितमस्कश्च संशुद्धश्च विशेषतः ॥78॥
2.25.m: And he attains the desired wishes of his mind, without doubt. / He becomes known among the gods and likewise among the hosts of sages, / freed from evil, freed from darkness, and exceedingly purified.

2.25.s:
ārādhanārthaṃ puruṣottamasya kṛcchrāṇi kṛtvā madhusūdanasya ..
surottamānāṃ samatītalabdhaṃ tallokamāpnoti janārdanasya .. 79 ..
2.124
.. rāma uvāca ..
vaidikāni samācakṣva karmāṇi surasattama ..
adhikārī bhavedyeṣāṃ kṛcchrakārī tvanantaram .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
śṛṇu kāmyāni karmāṇi puṣkalāni mamānagha ..
prativedaṃ mahābhāga gadato bhṛgunandana .. 2 ..

kāmaṃ karoti gāyatrī prāṇāyāmādviśeṣataḥ .. 3 ..

bahiḥ snātasya tatraiva sarvakalmaṣanāśanaḥ .. 4 ..
daśāyutāni japtvā ca haviṣyāśī susaṃyataḥ ..
vāyubhūtastadāpnoti yadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ..5..
parasya brahmaṇo rāma vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
puruṣasyāprameyasya sarvagasyāvināśinaḥ .. 6..
2.25.d:
आराधनार्थं पुरुषोत्तमस्य कृच्छ्राणि कृत्वा मधुसूदनस्य ॥
सुरोत्तमानां समतीतलब्धं तल्लोकमाप्नोति जनार्दनस्य ॥ 79 ॥
2.124
॥ राम उवाच ॥
वैदिकानि समाचक्ष्व कर्माणि सुरसत्तम ॥
अधिकारी भवेद्येषां कृच्छ्रकारी त्वनन्तरम् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शृणु काम्यानि कर्माणि पुष्कलानि ममानघ ॥
प्रतिवेदं महाभाग गदतो भृगुनन्दन ॥ 2 ॥
अन्तर्जले तथा होमे जपेच्च मानसेप्सितम् ॥
कामं करोति गायत्री प्राणायामाद्विशेषतः ॥ 3 ॥
गायत्र्या दशसाहस्रो जपो नक्ताशिनो द्विज ॥
बहिः स्नातस्य तत्रैव सर्वकल्मषनाशनः ॥ 4 ॥
दशायुतानि जप्त्वा च हविष्याशी सुसंयतः ॥
वायुभूतस्तदाप्नोति यद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥5॥
परस्य ब्रह्मणो राम वाचकः प्रणवः स्मृतः ॥
पुरुषस्याप्रमेयस्य सर्वगस्याविनाशिनः ॥ 6॥
2.25.m:
Having performed kṛcchra penances for the sake of worshiping Puruṣottama, Madhusūdana, / he attains that world of Janārdana, which surpasses [that] achieved by the best of the gods.
2.124
Rāma said: / Declare, O best of the gods, the Vedic rites / for which one who performs the kṛcchra penance becomes qualified immediately thereafter.
Puṣkara said: / Hear from me, O sinless one, the abundant desire-prompted rites / according to each Veda, O fortunate descendant of Bhṛgu, as I speak.
While inside water, or during an oblation, one should murmur [it] for the desire of one's heart; / the Gāyatrī fulfills one's desire, especially through breath control.
A recitation of ten thousand repetitions of the Gāyatrī by one eating only at night, O twice-born, / who has bathed outdoors right there, destroys all sins.
And having recited one hundred thousand [repetitions], eating sacrificial food and well-restrained, / having become like the wind, he attains that supreme step of Viṣṇu.
The praṇava is regarded as the signifier of the supreme Brahman, O Rāma, / of the immeasurable, all-pervading, imperishable Cosmic Person.

2.25.s:
tajjapeneha pūyante ye'pi duṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ ..
kārapūtaṃ salilaṃ nābhimātrodakasthitaḥ .. 7 ..

akāraścāpyukāraśca makāraśca bhṛgūttama .. 8 ..
yajurvedaḥ sāmaveda ṛgvedaśca vicakṣaṇaiḥ ..
kathitastu trimātraśca praṇavaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..9..
mātrātrayaṃ tu praṇavastrayo devāḥ sanātanāḥ ..
eta eva trayo lokāstrayaścaivāgnayastathā .. 2.124.10 ..
mahāvyāhṛtibhirhomātsarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
mahāvyāhṛtayo jñeyāḥ saptalokā vicakṣaṇaiḥ .. 11 ..
gāyatrī paramā japye home vyāhṛtayastathā ..
antarjale tathā rāma proktaścaivāghamarṣaṇaḥ .. 12 ..
agnimīḻe purohita sūkto'yaṃ vahnidevataḥ ..
śirasā dhārayedvahniṃ yo japetparivatsaram .. 13 ..
homaṃ triṣavaṇaṃ caiva tathā tena samācaret ..
anagnijvalanaṃ kuryādbhaikṣāhārastu vatsarān .. 14 ..
2.25.d:
तज्जपेनेह पूयन्ते येऽपि दुष्कृतकारिणः ॥
कारपूतं सलिलं नाभिमात्रोदकस्थितः ॥ 7 ॥
शतजप्तं पिबेद्यस्तु स पापैर्विप्रमुच्यते ॥
अकारश्चाप्युकारश्च मकारश्च भृगूत्तम ॥ 8 ॥
यजुर्वेदः सामवेद ऋग्वेदश्च विचक्षणैः ॥
कथितस्तु त्रिमात्रश्च प्रणवः परिकीर्तितः ॥9॥
मात्रात्रयं तु प्रणवस्त्रयो देवाः सनातनाः ॥
एत एव त्रयो लोकास्त्रयश्चैवाग्नयस्तथा ॥ 2.124.10 ॥
महाव्याहृतिभिर्होमात्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
महाव्याहृतयो ज्ञेयाः सप्तलोका विचक्षणैः ॥ 11 ॥
गायत्री परमा जप्ये होमे व्याहृतयस्तथा ॥
अन्तर्जले तथा राम प्रोक्तश्चैवाघमर्षणः ॥ 12 ॥
अग्निमीḻए पुरोहित सूक्तोऽयं वह्निदेवतः ॥
शिरसा धारयेद्वह्निं यो जपेत्परिवत्सरम् ॥ 13 ॥
होमं त्रिषवणं चैव तथा तेन समाचरेत् ॥
अनग्निज्वलनं कुर्याद्भैक्षाहारस्तु वत्सरान् ॥ 14 ॥
2.25.m:
By its recitation, even those who have committed evil deeds are purified in this world. / Standing in water reaching up to the navel, [having consecrated] water purified by the [praṇava] syllable,
he who drinks [it] over which [the praṇava] has been recited a hundred times is freed from sins. / The syllable 'a', the syllable 'u', and the syllable 'ma', O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
are stated by the wise to be the Yajurveda, Sāmaveda, and Ṛgveda, / and the praṇava is proclaimed to have three measures.
The three measures of the praṇava are the three eternal gods; / these very [measures] are the three worlds, and likewise the three fires.
From offering oblations with the Great Utterances, one is freed from all sins. / The Great Utterances are to be known by the wise as the seven worlds.
The Gāyatrī is supreme in recitation, and likewise the Utterances in oblations; / and inside water, O Rāma, the Aghamarṣaṇa is proclaimed.
'Agnim īḷe purohitam'—this hymn has Agni as its deity; / one who recites it for a year should bear fire upon his head.
He should perform oblations with it at the three junctures of the day; / he should keep a fire unignited [in himself] and subsist on begged food for years.

2.25.s:
ataḥ paramṛcaḥ sapta cāgneyyaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
tā japanprayato nityamiṣṭānkāmānsamaśnute .. 15 ..
medhākāmo japennityaṃ sadasatpadamityṛcam ..
ambayo yānti yāḥ proktā na bandhomṛtyunāśinī .. 16 ..
śunaḥśephamṛṣiṃ tadvatsaṃniruddho'tha vā japet ..
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo gadācāpagadī gadan .. 17 ..
yadīcchecchāśvataṃ kāmamindrātprāptaṃ purandarāt ..
ṛgbhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ stūyādindrameti dinedine .. 18 ..
hiraṇyastūpamityetajjapañśatrūnprabādhate ..
kṣemī bhavati cādhmāne ye te paktā japannaraḥ .. 19 ..
raudrībhiḥ ṣaḍbhirīśānaṃ stūyādyo vai dinedine ..
caruṃ vā kalpayedraudraṃ tasya śāntiḥ parā bhavet .. 2.124.20 ..
udityudyantamādityamupatiṣṭheddinedine ..
kṣipejjalāñjalīnsapta manoduḥkhavināśanam .. 21 ..
2.25.d:
अतः परमृचः सप्त चाग्नेय्यः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
ता जपन्प्रयतो नित्यमिष्टान्कामान्समश्नुते ॥ 15 ॥
मेधाकामो जपेन्नित्यं सदसत्पदमित्यृचम् ॥
अम्बयो यान्ति याः प्रोक्ता न बन्धोमृत्युनाशिनी ॥ 16 ॥
शुनःशेफमृषिं तद्वत्संनिरुद्धोऽथ वा जपेत् ॥
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो गदाचापगदी गदन् ॥ 17 ॥
यदीच्छेच्छाश्वतं काममिन्द्रात्प्राप्तं पुरन्दरात् ॥
ऋग्भिः षोडशभिः स्तूयादिन्द्रमेति दिनेदिने ॥ 18 ॥
हिरण्यस्तूपमित्येतज्जपञ्शत्रून्प्रबाधते ॥
क्षेमी भवति चाध्माने ये ते पक्ता जपन्नरः ॥ 19 ॥
रौद्रीभिः षड्भिरीशानं स्तूयाद्यो वै दिनेदिने ॥
चरुं वा कल्पयेद्रौद्रं तस्य शान्तिः परा भवेत् ॥ 2.124.20 ॥
उदित्युद्यन्तमादित्यमुपतिष्ठेद्दिनेदिने ॥
क्षिपेज्जलाञ्जलीन्सप्त मनोदुःखविनाशनम् ॥ 21 ॥
2.25.m:
Beyond this, seven verses are proclaimed as dedicated to Agni; / reciting them constantly with self-control, he attains his desired wishes.
Desiring intelligence, one should constantly recite the verse 'sadasatpadam'; / the [verses] proclaimed as 'ambayo yānti' [and] 'na bandhoḥ' destroy death.
Likewise, one who is imprisoned should recite [the hymns of] the sage Śunaḥśepha; / a sick man, reciting it, is freed from disease and all sins.
If he should desire an enduring wish obtained from Indra, Purandara, / he should praise Indra day after day with sixteen verses.
Reciting this [hymn], 'hiraṇyastūpam', he repels enemies; / and a man reciting 'ye te paktā' becomes secure when suffering from flatulence.
He who praises Īśāna day after day with the six verses to Rudra, / or prepares a sacrificial mush for Rudra, achieves supreme peace.
Reciting 'ud', he should attend upon the rising sun day after day; / he should cast seven handfuls of water, which destroys mental distress.

2.25.s:
dviṣantamityathānarcya dviṣyantaṃ ca japansmaret ..
agacchansaptarātreṇa vidveṣamadhigacchati..22..

uttamastasya cāvajapedvairavināśane .. 23 .. ..

2.25.d:
द्विषन्तमित्यथानर्च्य द्विष्यन्तं च जपन्स्मरेत् ॥
अगच्छन्सप्तरात्रेण विद्वेषमधिगच्छति॥22॥
आरोग्यकामो रोगी च प्रस्कन्नस्योत्तमं जपेत् ॥
उत्तमस्तस्य चावजपेद्वैरविनाशने ॥ 23 ॥ ॥
उदयत्यायुरक्षय्यं तेजोमध्यन्दिने जपेत् ॥
अस्तं व्रजति सूर्ये च द्विषन्तं प्रतिपादितम् ॥ ॥ 24 ॥
नवपद्येति सूक्तानि जपञ्शत्रून्नियच्छति ॥
एकादश सुवर्णस्य सर्वकामांस्तु निर्दिशेत् ॥ 25 ॥
आध्यात्मिकैः क इत्येतज्जपन्मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥
आसनो रुद्रमित्येतद्दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ॥ 26 ॥
त्वं सोमेति च सूक्तेन नवं पश्येन्निशाकरम् ॥
उपतिष्ठेत्समित्पाणिर्वासांस्याप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 27 ॥
आयुरिप्सन्निदमिति कौत्ससूक्तं यदाभ्यसेत् ॥
अप नः शोशुचदिति स्तुत्वा मध्ये दिवाकरम् ॥ 28 ॥
यथा मुञ्जादिवेषीका तथा पापं प्रमुञ्चति ॥
जातवेदस इत्येतज्जपेत्स्वस्त्ययनं पथि ॥ 29 ॥
2.25.m:
Then, having worshiped, reciting 'dviṣantam', he should remember his enemy; / within seven nights, without [the enemy] approaching, he brings about hostility [for him].
A diseased person desiring health should recite the best [verse] of 'praskannasya'; / and for the destruction of enmity he should recite the highest [verse] of it.
At sunrise, [he recites it for] inexhaustible lifespan; at midday, he should recite it for splendor; / and as the sun sets, 'dviṣantam' is prescribed.
Reciting the hymns beginning with 'navapadā', he restrains his enemies; / he should point out the eleven [verses] of Suvarṇa for all desires.
Reciting this [verse], 'kaḥ', with spiritual [intent], he would attain liberation; / with this [verse], 'āsano rudram', he would attain a long life.
And looking at the new moon with the hymn 'tvaṃ soma', / he should attend upon it with kindling wood in hand; he attains garments, without doubt.
Desiring life, when he practices this Kautsa hymn, 'idam'; / having praised the sun at midday with 'apa naḥ śośucad',
just as the reed [stalk is drawn] from the muñja grass, so he casts off sin; / he should recite this [verse], 'jātavedase', as an auspicious rite on a journey.

2.25.s:
bhayairvimucyate sarvaiḥ svastimānāpnuyādgṛham ..
vyuṣṭāyāṃ ca tathā rātrāvetadduḥsvapnanāśanam .. 2.124.30 ..
pramanditeti sūryasya japedgarbhavimocanam ..
japannindramiti snāto vaiśvadevaṃ tu saptakam .. 31 ..
muñcatyājyaṃ tathā juhvatsakalaṃ kilbiṣaṃ naraḥ ..

chitvā sarvānmṛtyupāśāñjīvedrogavivarjitaḥ ..

mānastoketi ca ṛcā śikhābandhe kṛte naraḥ ..

2.25.d:
भयैर्विमुच्यते सर्वैः स्वस्तिमानाप्नुयाद्गृहम् ॥
व्युष्टायां च तथा रात्रावेतद्दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् ॥ 2.124.30 ॥
प्रमन्दितेति सूर्यस्य जपेद्गर्भविमोचनम् ॥
जपन्निन्द्रमिति स्नातो वैश्वदेवं तु सप्तकम् ॥ 31 ॥
मुञ्चत्याज्यं तथा जुह्वत्सकलं किल्बिषं नरः ॥
इमामिति जपञ्शश्वत्कामानाप्नोत्यभीप्सितान् ॥ 32 ॥
मानस्तोक इति द्वाभ्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितः शुचि ॥
औदुम्बरीस्तु जुहुयाद्दधिमध्वाज्यसंस्कृताः ॥ 33 ॥
छित्वा सर्वान्मृत्युपाशाञ्जीवेद्रोगविवर्जितः ॥
ऊर्ध्वबाहुरनेनैव स्तुत्वा शस्त्रं तथैव च ॥ 34 ॥
मानस्तोकेति च ऋचा शिखाबन्धे कृते नरः ॥
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां जायते संशयं विना ॥ 35 ॥
चित्रमित्युपतिष्ठेत त्रिसन्ध्यं भास्करं तथा ॥
समित्पाणिर्नरो नित्यं प्राप्नुयात्तु धनायुषी ॥ 36 ॥
2.25.m:
He is freed from all fears and reaches home safely; / and at the dawn of the night, this destroys bad dreams.
He should recite the solar [hymn] 'pramanditā' for release from the womb; / having bathed, reciting 'indram', [or] the seven verses to the Viśvedevas,
and offering clarified butter [into the fire], a man is freed from all sin; / reciting 'imām' constantly, he attains his desired wishes.
Having fasted for three nights, pure, with the two [verses beginning with] 'mā nas toke', / he should offer [sticks of] udumbara wood prepared with curd, honey, and clarified butter.
Having severed all the nooses of death, he lives free from disease; / with uplifted arms, having praised the weapon with this very [hymn],
and when the tying of the topknot is done with the verse 'mā nas toke', a man / becomes invisible to all beings, without doubt.
With 'citram', a man with kindling wood in hand should regularly attend upon the sun / at the three junctures of the day; he would attain wealth and lifespan.

2.25.s:
etad duḥsvapnasyeti ca japanprātardinedine..
duḥsvapnaṃ dahate kṛtsnaṃ bhojanaṃ cāpnuyācchubham .. 37 ..
ubheṣunāmīti tathā rakṣā ca parikīrtitā ..
nirvartya pañcayajñāṃśca hutvā cāgniṃ kṛtāhnikaḥ .. 38 ..
devāsāviti devyedaṃ japankāmānavāpnuyāt ..
ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyāghrādikaṃ naraḥ .. 39 ..
na mā giranniti japaṃstebhya eva pramucyate ..
kayā śubheti ca japañjñātiśraiṣṭhyamavāpnuyāt .. 2.124.40 ..
imaṃ nu somamityetatsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..

2.25.d:
एतद् दुःस्वप्नस्येति च जपन्प्रातर्दिनेदिने॥
दुःस्वप्नं दहते कृत्स्नं भोजनं चाप्नुयाच्छुभम् ॥ 37 ॥
उभेषुनामीति तथा रक्षा च परिकीर्तिता ॥
निर्वर्त्य पञ्चयज्ञांश्च हुत्वा चाग्निं कृताह्निकः ॥ 38 ॥
देवासाविति देव्येदं जपन्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
आततायिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा व्याघ्रादिकं नरः ॥ 39 ॥
न मा गिरन्निति जपंस्तेभ्य एव प्रमुच्यते ॥
कया शुभेति च जपञ्ज्ञातिश्रैष्ठ्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 2.124.40 ॥
इमं नु सोममित्येतत्सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
पित्रन्त्वित्युपतिष्ठेत नित्यमन्नमुपस्थितम् ॥ 41 ॥
नास्य स्यादन्नतो व्याधिर्विषमप्यन्नतामियात् ॥
अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाद् घृतम् ॥ 42 ॥
पक्वान्नं प्रतिपद्येत कृत्वा चाकर्म गर्हितम् ॥
वीरान्वयं समाप्नोति सश्लोकं यो जपेत्सदा॥43॥
कं कता चेति सूक्तेन विघ्नान्सर्वानपोहति ॥
यो जात इति सूक्तेन सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्॥ 44॥
2.25.m:
And reciting 'etad duḥsvapnasya' in the morning day after day, / he burns away all bad dreams and obtains wholesome food.
And the [hymn] 'ubhe suṣumnā' is proclaimed as a protection; / having completed the five great sacrifices, offered oblation into the fire, and performed daily rites,
reciting this [verse] to the goddess, 'devāsau', he obtains his desires; / seeing an assailant approaching, such as a tiger, a man,
reciting 'na mā giran', is freed from them; / and reciting 'kayā śubhā', he attains preeminence among his kin.
With "[May I enjoy] this Soma now" [RV 6.47.1], he obtains all desires. / He should constantly worship cooked food that is served with "May they protect [our] father" [RV 6.52.15].
No illness arising from food will befall him, and even poison will turn into [harmless] food. / With the hymn "O Agni, lead [us]" [RV 1.189.1], he should offer clarified butter with each verse.
Even after doing a censured, prohibited deed, he will obtain cooked food. / Whoever constantly recites [the hymn] together with its stanza obtains a heroic lineage.
With the hymn "Which? By what means?" he ward off all obstacles. / With the hymn "He who as soon as born" [RV 2.12.1], he attains unsurpassed happiness.

2.25.s:
ye parājannitīmāṃ tu duḥsvapnaśamanāmṛcam ..
ekāmāhamitīyāṃ tu vijñeyā śrīkarī tathā .. 45 ..
caturdaśīmupoṣyaikāṃ kṛṣṇāsu juhuyād ghṛtam ..
āttasūktena raudreṇa vyādhimekaṃ vimuñcati .. 46..

āmiṣasyetayormohātkṛtvā vā karma garhitam ..47..

nāsti vidyāgamo yasya suyuktasyāpi bhārgava .. 51 ..
2.25.d:
ये पराजन्नितीमां तु दुःस्वप्नशमनामृचम् ॥
एकामाहमितीयां तु विज्ञेया श्रीकरी तथा ॥ 45 ॥
चतुर्दशीमुपोष्यैकां कृष्णासु जुहुयाद् घृतम् ॥
आत्तसूक्तेन रौद्रेण व्याधिमेकं विमुञ्चति ॥ 46॥
स्नात्वानश्नञ्जपेदप्सु शीतत्रयमतन्द्रितः ॥
आमिषस्येतयोर्मोहात्कृत्वा वा कर्म गर्हितम् ॥47॥
अध्वनि प्रस्थितो यस्तु पश्येच्छकुनमुत्थितम् ॥
अप्रशस्ते प्रशस्ते वा कनिक्रदमिदं जपेत् ॥ 48 ॥
अस्पृष्ट्वैव च जप्तव्यमेतत्तस्करमोहनम् ॥
ओंष्वित्यृचमपां मध्ये जपेद्यो वै नदीं तरेत् ॥49॥
उद्धौर्मिभिरितीमां तु जपेद्रथगतस्तरन् ॥ ।
अध्वानं प्रस्थितश्चैव मन्त्रैरिति च संस्मरेत् ॥ 2.124.50 ॥
सुदातारं सुपुष्ट्यर्थं सर्ववेदे स्थितं नरम् ॥
नास्ति विद्यागमो यस्य सुयुक्तस्यापि भार्गव ॥ 51 ॥
2.25.m:
The verse "They who fled" is to be known as pacifying bad dreams; / and that [verse] "I myself [rule] alone" [RV 10.159.1] brings prosperity.
Having fasted on one fourteenth lunar day of the dark fortnight, he should offer clarified butter; / by means of the hymn to Rudra that has been taken, he is released from each disease.
Having bathed and fasting, unwearied, he should recite the three cool [verses] in water; / or having performed a censured deed out of delusion through these two [forms] of meat,
when set out on a road, whoever sees an omen that has arisen, / whether inauspicious or auspicious, he should recite this [verse]: "Crying out repeatedly" [RV 2.42.1].
This [verse], which confounds thieves, is to be recited without touching [anything]. / Whoever would cross a river should recite in the midst of the waters the verse beginning with "Oṃṣu".
One mounted on a chariot while crossing should recite this [verse], "With high waves..."; / and set out on a journey, he should remember [them] with these mantras.
For abundant nourishment, [he should recite] "A generous giver" [RV 1.8.3], a man established in all the Vedas; / one who has no acquisition of learning, even when well-applied, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.25.s:
sa sarpīriti ca japanmāsāttaṃ pratipadyate ..
yānākṣaṃ samabhajyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā durge'dhvani dvija .. 52 ..
abhityavasyeti japedṛkṣamakṣabalaṃ dadhat ..
kṛṣṇapakṣacaturdaśyāṃ trirātropoṣitaḥ śuciḥ .. 53 ..
dakṣiṇāpravaṇe deśe śmaśānasthaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
raktoṣṇīṣyasipāṇiśca taulākībhyo'nilāśanaḥ .. 54 ..
saptāhaṃ juhuyāttailaṃ sārṣapaṃ lavaṇānvitam ..
samidho rājavṛkṣasya vasiṣṭhe dveṣiṇīḥ paṭhan .. 55 ..
yaṃ dviṣyāttasya kṛtvā tu śamyā kenāhṛtaṃ niśi ..
adhiṣṭhāya ca taṃ kuryādṛgbhiśca tisṛbhirdvijaḥ .. 56 ..
uddiśya rāma homo'yaṃ saptarātraṃ na jīvati ..
dvāviṃśakaṃ japansūktamadhyātmikamanuttamam .. 57 ..
parvasu prayato nityamiṣṭānkāmānupāśnute ..
bṛhaspatimajāśvaṃ ca satāraṃ babhrumeva ca .. 58 ..
