kṛṇuṣveti japansūktaṃ juhvadājyaṃ samāhitaḥ..59..
2.25.d:
स सर्पीरिति च जपन्मासात्तं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
यानाक्षं समभज्यन्तं दृष्ट्वा दुर्गेऽध्वनि द्विज ॥ 52 ॥
अभित्यवस्येति जपेदृक्षमक्षबलं दधत् ॥
कृष्णपक्षचतुर्दश्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितः शुचिः ॥ 53 ॥
दक्षिणाप्रवणे देशे श्मशानस्थः समाहितः ॥
रक्तोष्णीष्यसिपाणिश्च तौलाकीभ्योऽनिलाशनः ॥ 54 ॥
सप्ताहं जुहुयात्तैलं सार्षपं लवणान्वितम् ॥
समिधो राजवृक्षस्य वसिष्ठे द्वेषिणीः पठन् ॥ 55 ॥
यं द्विष्यात्तस्य कृत्वा तु शम्या केनाहृतं निशि ॥
अधिष्ठाय च तं कुर्यादृग्भिश्च तिसृभिर्द्विजः ॥ 56 ॥
उद्दिश्य राम होमोऽयं सप्तरात्रं न जीवति ॥
द्वाविंशकं जपन्सूक्तमध्यात्मिकमनुत्तमम् ॥ 57 ॥
पर्वसु प्रयतो नित्यमिष्टान्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥
बृहस्पतिमजाश्वं च सतारं बभ्रुमेव च ॥ 58 ॥
पञ्चर्चेन स्तुवन्नेतान्पञ्चकामानवाप्नुयात्॥
कृणुष्वेति जपन्सूक्तं जुह्वदाज्यं समाहितः॥59॥
2.25.m:
reciting "He [drinks] clarified butter" for a month, he acquires it. / Seeing the axle of a carriage breaking on a difficult road, O twice-born,
he should recite the verse "May you help us...", maintaining axle-strength. / Fasted for three nights, pure, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
in a place sloping toward the south, stationed in a cremation ground, concentrated in mind, / wearing a red turban, with a sword in hand, subsisting on air for the Taulāki [rites],
for seven days he should offer mustard oil mixed with salt / and fuel sticks of the rājavṛkṣa tree, reciting the [verses] hateful to Vasiṣṭha.
Having made [an effigy] of the one whom he hates, brought with a peg at night, / and stepping on it, the twice-born should perform [the rite] with three verses.
This oblation is directed [against him], O Rāma; he does not live for seven nights. / Reciting the twenty-second spiritual hymn, which is unsurpassed,
on the auspicious days, constantly restrained, he attains desired wishes. / To Bṛhaspati, and the goat-steeded [Pūṣan], and to [Indra] with the stars, and to the Brown One,
praising them with the five-verse hymn, he attains five desires. / Reciting the hymn "Make [power]" [RV 4.4.1], offering clarified butter, concentrated in mind,

2.25.s:
arātīnāṃ haretprāṇānrakṣāṃsyapi ca nāśayet..
upatiṣṭheta yo vahniṃ parītya ca dine dine..2.124.60..
taṃ rakṣati svayaṃ vahnirviśvato viśvatomukhaḥ..
ko adyeti ca sūktena vāsāṃsi labhate param..61..
kāyeti vāmadevena kuryātsvastyayanaṃ niśi...
haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityetacchucirīkṣandivākaram .. 62..
kṛṣiṃ prapadyamānastu sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi ..
juhuyātkṣetramadhye tu śunā vāhastu pañcabhiḥ..63...
indrāya ca marudbhyaśca parjanyāya bhagāya ca ..
yathāliṅgaṃ tu viharellāṅgalaṃ tu kṛṣīvalaḥ .. 64 ..
pūṣṇe dhānyāya sītāyai śunāsīramathottaram .. .
gandhamālyopahāraiśca yajedetāśca devatāḥ .. 65 ..
pravāpaṇe pralapane khalasītopahārayoḥ ..
amoghaṃ karma bhavati vardhate sarvadā kṛṣiḥ .. 66 ...
kṣetrasya patye tatkṣetraṃ sūryadṛgvindate bhuvam ..
ākhūtkareṣu caraṇau yajedetena mūṣikām .. 67 ..
2.25.d:
अरातीनां हरेत्प्राणान्रक्षांस्यपि च नाशयेत्॥
उपतिष्ठेत यो वह्निं परीत्य च दिने दिने॥2.124.60॥
तं रक्षति स्वयं वह्निर्विश्वतो विश्वतोमुखः॥
को अद्येति च सूक्तेन वासांसि लभते परम्॥61॥
कायेति वामदेवेन कुर्यात्स्वस्त्ययनं निशि॥।
हंसः शुचिषदित्येतच्छुचिरीक्षन्दिवाकरम् ॥ 62॥
कृषिं प्रपद्यमानस्तु स्थालीपाकं यथाविधि ॥
जुहुयात्क्षेत्रमध्ये तु शुना वाहस्तु पञ्चभिः॥63॥।
इन्द्राय च मरुद्भ्यश्च पर्जन्याय भगाय च ॥
यथालिङ्गं तु विहरेल्लाङ्गलं तु कृषीवलः ॥ 64 ॥
पूष्णे धान्याय सीतायै शुनासीरमथोत्तरम् ॥ ।
गन्धमाल्योपहारैश्च यजेदेताश्च देवताः ॥ 65 ॥
प्रवापणे प्रलपने खलसीतोपहारयोः ॥
अमोघं कर्म भवति वर्धते सर्वदा कृषिः ॥ 66 ॥।
क्षेत्रस्य पत्ये तत्क्षेत्रं सूर्यदृग्विन्दते भुवम् ॥
आखूत्करेषु चरणौ यजेदेतेन मूषिकाम् ॥ 67 ॥
2.25.m:
he takes away the lives of enemies and also destroys demons. / Whoever approaches the fire, having circumambulated it day after day,
him the fire itself protects on all sides, facing all directions. / And with the hymn "Who today..." [RV 1.84.1], he obtains excellent garments.
At night, he should perform an auspicious blessing with the [hymn] "By what..." composed by Vāmadeva. / [Reciting] the verse "The swan seated in purity" [RV 4.40.5], pure, looking at the sun,
one undertaking agriculture should offer a domestic cooked oblation according to rule / in the middle of the field with the five [verses beginning with] "May the plows...".
To Indra, and to the Maruts, and to Parjanya, and to Bhaga, / according to the characteristic mark [in the mantras], the cultivator should guide the plow.
To Pūṣan, to Grain, to Sītā, and then next to Śunāsīra; / and he should worship these deities with perfumes, garlands, and offerings.
At sowing, at weeding, and at offerings to the threshing-floor and the furrow, / his work becomes unfailing, and agriculture ever flourishes.
To the Lord of the Field—the sun-seer gains that field and earth. / In molehills he should worship the mouse's two feet with this [mantra].

2.25.s:
citrā indreti ca stūyānnāsya vṛṣṭibhayaṃ bhavet ...
vijyetiṣyeti jvalayedyatrecchejjātavedasam..68..
samudrāditi sūktena kāmānāpnoti pāvakāt..
viśvāni ca iti dvābhyāmṛgbhyāṃ yo vahnimarcati.. ..69..
sa taratyāpadaḥ sarvāḥ yaśaḥ prāpnoti cākṣayam ..
agne tvamiti ca stutvā dhanamāpnoti vāñchitam..2.124.70..
uroṣṭa iti(5.38.1) sūktena vittamāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
prajākāmo japennityaṃ varuṇādevasannayā .. 71 ..
svastyātreyaṃ japetprātaḥ sadā svastyayanaṃ japet ..
svastipanthāmiti prodya svastimānvrajate'dhvani ..72..
vijahīṣurvanasyānte śatrūṇāṃ bādhanaṃ bhavet ..
striyo garbhapramūḍhāyā garbhamokṣaṇamuttamam..73..
avacchāditi sūktena vṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet..
nirāhāraḥ klinnavāsā na cireṇa pravarṣati..74..
2.25.d:
चित्रा इन्द्रेति च स्तूयान्नास्य वृष्टिभयं भवेत् ॥।
विज्येतिष्येति ज्वलयेद्यत्रेच्छेज्जातवेदसम्॥68॥
समुद्रादिति सूक्तेन कामानाप्नोति पावकात्॥
विश्वानि च इति द्वाभ्यामृग्भ्यां यो वह्निमर्चति॥ ॥69॥
स तरत्यापदः सर्वाः यशः प्राप्नोति चाक्षयम् ॥
अग्ने त्वमिति च स्तुत्वा धनमाप्नोति वाञ्छितम्॥2.124.70॥
उरोष्ट इति(5.38.1) सूक्तेन वित्तमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
प्रजाकामो जपेन्नित्यं वरुणादेवसन्नया ॥ 71 ॥
स्वस्त्यात्रेयं जपेत्प्रातः सदा स्वस्त्ययनं जपेत् ॥
स्वस्तिपन्थामिति प्रोद्य स्वस्तिमान्व्रजतेऽध्वनि ॥72॥
विजहीषुर्वनस्यान्ते शत्रूणां बाधनं भवेत् ॥
स्त्रियो गर्भप्रमूढाया गर्भमोक्षणमुत्तमम्॥73॥
अवच्छादिति सूक्तेन वृष्टिकामः प्रयोजयेत्॥
निराहारः क्लिन्नवासा न चिरेण प्रवर्षति॥74॥
2.25.m:
He should praise with "Wondrous Indra..." [RV 8.21.1]; he will have no fear of excessive rain. / With "Untying the bowstring...", he should kindle Jātavedas wherever he desires.
With the hymn "From the ocean..." [RV 4.58.1], he obtains desires from the fire. / Whoever worships the fire with the two verses "All [evils]...",
he crosses over all misfortunes and attains imperishable fame. / And having praised with "O Agni, you...", he obtains desired wealth.
With the hymn "Wide-stepping..." [RV 5.38.1], he undoubtedly obtains wealth. / Desiring offspring, he should constantly recite [the verses] together with "From Varuṇa, the god...".
In the morning he should recite the Svastyātreya [hymn]; he should always recite an auspicious benediction. / Having proclaimed "A safe path...", he travels safely on the road.
Desiring to abandon [evils] at the edge of the forest, there will be harassment of his enemies. / For a woman whose embryo is confused, it is the best deliverance of the fetus.
With the hymn "From the covering...", one desiring rain should employ [the rite]; / without food, with wet clothes, it rains before long.

2.25.s:
śriyaḥ pañcadaśarcaṃ tu japañjuhuyād ghṛtena vā..
upaitu māṃ devasakha iti sarvauṣadhījalaiḥ ..75..
sadā snātaḥ śriyaṃ dīptāṃ kule prāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
manasaḥ kāma ityetāṃ paśukāmo naro japet ..76 ..
kardameneti ca snāyātprajākāmaḥ śuci vrataḥ..
aśvapūrvāmiti snāyādrājyakāmastu mānavaḥ..77..
rohite carmaṇi snāyādbrāhmaṇastu yathāvidhi ..
rājā carmaṇi vaiyāghre chāge vaiśyastathaiva ca ..78..
daśasāhasriko homaḥ pratyekaṃ parikīrtitaḥ ..
apsu vā juhuyādrāma padmānyayutaśo'gniṣu..79 ..
2.25.d:
श्रियः पञ्चदशर्चं तु जपञ्जुहुयाद् घृतेन वा॥
उपैतु मां देवसख इति सर्वौषधीजलैः ॥75॥
सदा स्नातः श्रियं दीप्तां कुले प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
मनसः काम इत्येतां पशुकामो नरो जपेत् ॥76 ॥
कर्दमेनेति च स्नायात्प्रजाकामः शुचि व्रतः॥
अश्वपूर्वामिति स्नायाद्राज्यकामस्तु मानवः॥77॥
रोहिते चर्मणि स्नायाद्ब्राह्मणस्तु यथाविधि ॥
राजा चर्मणि वैयाघ्रे छागे वैश्यस्तथैव च ॥78॥
दशसाहस्रिको होमः प्रत्येकं परिकीर्तितः ॥
अप्सु वा जुहुयाद्राम पद्मान्ययुतशोऽग्निषु॥79 ॥
2.25.m:
Reciting the fifteen-verse hymn of Śrī, he should also offer with clarified butter; / with "May the friend of the gods approach me..." [RV Khila 4.8.7] [and] with waters of all herbs,
constantly bathed, he undoubtedly obtains radiant prosperity in his family. / A man desiring cattle should recite this [verse], "The desire of the mind..." [RV Khila 4.8.10].
With "By Kardama..." [RV Khila 4.8.11], desiring offspring, pure, observing vows, he should bathe. / A man desiring kingship should bathe with "Preceded by horses..." [RV Khila 4.8.3].
A brahmin should bathe according to rule on a red hide; / a king on a tiger's skin, and likewise a vaiśya on a goat's [skin].
An oblation of ten thousand [offerings] is proclaimed for each. / Or he should offer lotuses into waters, O Rāma, by the tens of thousands into fires.

2.25.s:
iṣṭāna ityṛcā vahniṃ stuvañśatrūnvināśayet..
ācāra iti sūktena goṣṭhe gāṃ lokamātaram..2.124.80 ..
2.25.d:
इष्टान इत्यृचा वह्निं स्तुवञ्शत्रून्विनाशयेत्॥
आचार इति सूक्तेन गोष्ठे गां लोकमातरम्॥2.124.80 ॥
2.25.m: Praising the fire with the verse "[O Agni, burn] the desired [places of the enemies]...", he destroys enemies. / With the hymn "Conduct...", in a cow-pen, to the cow, mother of the world,

2.25.s:
upatiṣṭhedvrajeccaiva ya icchedgāḥ sadākṣayāḥ..
vāksiddhiṃ tu stuvañśakraṃ mahaddhanamavāpnuyāt .. 81 ..
2.25.d:
उपतिष्ठेद्व्रजेच्चैव य इच्छेद्गाः सदाक्षयाः॥
वाक्सिद्धिं तु स्तुवञ्शक्रं महद्धनमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 81 ॥
2.25.m: he should approach and go, he who desires ever-inexhaustible cows. / Praising Śakra with [prayers for] accomplishment of speech, he obtains great wealth.

2.25.s:
upaiteti mṛtī rājño dundubhīnabhimantrayet ..
tejo balaṃ ca prāpnoti śatrūṃścaiva niyacchati .. 82 ..
2.25.d:
उपैतेति मृती राज्ञो दुन्दुभीनभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
तेजो बलं च प्राप्नोति शत्रूंश्चैव नियच्छति ॥ 82 ॥
2.25.m: With "Approach...", he should consecrate the war drums of the king; / he obtains splendor and strength, and subdues his enemies.

2.25.s:
tṛṇapāṇirjapetsūktaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ dasyubhirvṛtaḥ ..
ye ke ca metyṛcaṃ japtvā dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt ..83..
2.25.d:
तृणपाणिर्जपेत्सूक्तं रक्षोघ्नं दस्युभिर्वृतः ॥
ये के च मेत्यृचं जप्त्वा दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ॥83॥
2.25.m: With grass in hand, surrounded by bandits, he should recite the demon-slaying hymn. / Having recited the verse "Whoever [has transgressed against] me...", he attains long life.

2.25.s:
yasya naṣṭaṃ bhaveddravya sampūjya sa japenniśi ..
saumāraudraṃ japansūktaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..84..
2.25.d:
यस्य नष्टं भवेद्द्रव्य सम्पूज्य स जपेन्निशि ॥
सौमारौद्रं जपन्सूक्तं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥84॥
2.25.m: One whose property is lost should, after worshiping, recite at night. / Reciting the hymn to Soma and Rudra, he is released from all sins.

2.25.s:
jīmūtasūktena tathā senāṅgānabhimantrayet ..
yathāliṅgaṃ tato rājā vinihanti raṇe ripūn .. 85 ..
2.25.d:
जीमूतसूक्तेन तथा सेनाङ्गानभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
यथालिङ्गं ततो राजा विनिहन्ति रणे रिपून् ॥ 85 ॥
2.25.m: Likewise, he should consecrate the divisions of the army with the Jīmūta hymn; / then, in accordance with the signs, the king slays his enemies in battle.

2.25.s:
agniṃ nareti sūktena stuvannagniṃ sukhī bhavet ..
prāṇapeti tribhiḥ sūktairdhanamāpnoti cākṣayam .. 86 ..
2.25.d:
अग्निं नरेति सूक्तेन स्तुवन्नग्निं सुखी भवेत् ॥
प्राणपेति त्रिभिः सूक्तैर्धनमाप्नोति चाक्षयम् ॥ 86 ॥
2.25.m: Praising Agni with the hymn beginning with 'agniṃ naraḥ', one becomes happy. / And with the three hymns beginning with 'prāṇāpa', one attains imperishable wealth.

2.25.s:
abhītayaḥ pragāthena stutvā śakraṃ dhanī bhavet ..
śaṃvatīḥ śanna indrāgnī japedvyādhivināśanam .. 87 ..
2.25.d:
अभीतयः प्रगाथेन स्तुत्वा शक्रं धनी भवेत् ॥
शंवतीः शन्न इन्द्राग्नी जपेद्व्याधिविनाशनम् ॥ 87 ॥
2.25.m: Having praised Śakra with the pragātha beginning with 'abhītayaḥ', one becomes wealthy. / One should mutter the śaṃvatī verses and 'śanna indrāgnī', which destroy disease.

2.25.s:
samudrajyeṣṭheti japetsūktametajjayāvaham .
vāstoṣpate pratītyetatsūktaṃ vātoṣpaterjapet .. 88 ..
2.25.d:
समुद्रज्येष्ठेति जपेत्सूक्तमेतज्जयावहम् ।
वास्तोष्पते प्रतीत्येतत्सूक्तं वातोष्पतेर्जपेत् ॥ 88 ॥
2.25.m: One should mutter this hymn beginning with 'samudrajyeṣṭhā', which brings victory. / One should mutter the hymn to Vāstoṣpati beginning with 'vāstoṣpate prati'.

2.25.s:
anīvaheti sūktena bhūtānniḥsvāpayenniśi ..
sambādhe viṣame durge bandhe vā nigaḍaiḥ kvacit .. 89 ..
2.25.d:
अनीवहेति सूक्तेन भूतान्निःस्वापयेन्निशि ॥
सम्बाधे विषमे दुर्गे बन्धे वा निगडैः क्वचित् ॥ 89 ॥
2.25.m: With the hymn beginning with 'anīvahan', one should put the spirits to sleep at night, / when trapped in a tight pass, in rough terrain, in a stronghold, or bound in chains somewhere.

2.25.s:
palāyitvā gṛhīto vā sūktametattathā japet ..
trirātraṃ niyatopoṣya śrapayetpāyasaṃ carum .. 2.124.90 ..
2.25.d:
पलायित्वा गृहीतो वा सूक्तमेतत्तथा जपेत् ॥
त्रिरात्रं नियतोपोष्य श्रपयेत्पायसं चरुम् ॥ 2.124.90 ॥
2.25.m: Or having fled and been captured, one should likewise mutter this hymn. / Having fasted with restraint for three nights, one should cook a caru of milk-rice.

2.25.s:
tenāyutaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ juhuyāttryambaketyṛcā ..
samuddiśya mahādevaṃ jīvedabdaśataṃ sukhī .. 91..
2.25.d:
तेनायुतशतं पूर्णं जुहुयात्त्र्यम्बकेत्यृचा ॥
समुद्दिश्य महादेवं जीवेदब्दशतं सुखी ॥ 91॥
2.25.m: With that, with the verse beginning with 'tryambakam', one should offer a full one hundred myriads [of oblations] / dedicated to Mahādeva, and live happily for a hundred years.

2.25.s:
taccakṣurityṛcā snāta upatiṣṭheddivākaram ..
udyantaṃ madhyamaṃ caiva dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ .. 92 ..
2.25.d:
तच्चक्षुरित्यृचा स्नात उपतिष्ठेद्दिवाकरम् ॥
उद्यन्तं मध्यमं चैव दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥ 92 ॥
2.25.m: Having bathed, desiring to live a long life, one should worship the sun / with the verse beginning with 'taccakṣuḥ' as it rises and at midday.

2.25.s:
vyuṣā ityupatiṣṭheta yaḥ prātaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ ..
prāpnuyātsahiraṇyādi nānārūpadharaṃ bahu .. 93 ..
2.25.d:
व्युषा इत्युपतिष्ठेत यः प्रातः प्रयतः शुचिः ॥
प्राप्नुयात्सहिरण्यादि नानारूपधरं बहु ॥ 93 ॥
2.25.m: Whoever, restrained and pure, worships [the sun] at dawn with [the verse beginning with] 'vyuṣāḥ', / will obtain abundant [wealth] taking various forms, such as gold.

2.25.s:
dhruvaṃ sandhyāsu kṣitiṣu japanbaddhaḥ pramucyate ..
idamāpaḥ pravahata yatkiṃcidduritaṃ punaḥ .. 94 ..
2.25.d:
ध्रुवं सन्ध्यासु क्षितिषु जपन्बद्धः प्रमुच्यते ॥
इदमापः प्रवहत यत्किंचिद्दुरितं पुनः ॥ 94 ॥
2.25.m: Muttening 'dhruvam' at the twilights while upon the earth, one who is bound is set free. / [With the verse beginning with] 'idamāpaḥ pravahata yat kiṃcid duritam', moreover,

2.25.s:
apaḥ praviśya tu japansarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
sūktābhyāṃ para etābhyāṃ hutābhyāṃ bhūtimāpnuyāt .. 95 ..
2.25.d:
अपः प्रविश्य तु जपन्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
सूक्ताभ्यां पर एताभ्यां हुताभ्यां भूतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 95 ॥
2.25.m: entering the waters and muttering, one is freed from all sins. / Beyond these, by offering oblations with these two hymns, one attains prosperity.

2.25.s:
sūktābhyāṃ tisra etābhyāmāsyadalpodakasthitaḥ ..
upatiṣṭhanraviṃ devaṃ pañcarātre gate naraḥ .. 96 ..
2.25.d:
सूक्ताभ्यां तिस्र एताभ्यामास्यदल्पोदकस्थितः ॥
उपतिष्ठन्रविं देवं पञ्चरात्रे गते नरः ॥ 96 ॥
2.25.m: Standing in water up to the mouth or shallow water, a man worshipping the divine sun / with these two hymns or these three [verses], after five nights have elapsed,

2.25.s:
anaśnanbhārgavaśreṣṭha mahaddharṣamavāpnuyāt ..
indrāsometi sūktaṃ tu kathitaṃ śatrunāśanam .. 97 ..
2.25.d:
अनश्नन्भार्गवश्रेष्ठ महद्धर्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥
इन्द्रासोमेति सूक्तं तु कथितं शत्रुनाशनम् ॥ 97 ॥
2.25.m: eating no food, O best of the Bhṛgus, attains great joy. / The hymn beginning with 'indrāsomā' is declared to destroy enemies.

2.25.s:
yasya lupyedvrataṃ mohādvātyairvā saṃsṛjetsaha ..
upoṣyājyasya juhuyāttvamagne vratapā iti.. 98 ..
2.25.d:
यस्य लुप्येद्व्रतं मोहाद्वात्यैर्वा संसृजेत्सह ॥
उपोष्याज्यस्य जुहुयात्त्वमग्ने व्रतपा इति॥ 98 ॥
2.25.m: One whose vow has failed through delusion or who has associated with outcastes / should fast and offer clarified butter with [the verse beginning with] 'tvamagne vratapāḥ'.

2.25.s:
ādityadṛkpramādraujaṃ japtvā vādī jayī bhavet ..
samagniragnibhiśceti prapadyedvāyubhāskarau .. 99 ..
2.25.d:
आदित्यदृक्प्रमाद्रौजं जप्त्वा वादी जयी भवेत् ॥
समग्निरग्निभिश्चेति प्रपद्येद्वायुभास्करौ ॥ 99 ॥
2.25.m: A litigant, having muttered the [hymn] seen by the Ādityas, 'pramādraujam', becomes victorious. / With 'samagniragnibhiḥ', one should take refuge in Vāyu and the Sun.

2.25.s:
agniṃ prathamataḥ stutvā mahatkaṣṭātpramucyate ..
na hīti ca catuṣkeṇa mucyate mahato bhayāt .. 2.124.100 ..
2.25.d:
अग्निं प्रथमतः स्तुत्वा महत्कष्टात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
न हीति च चतुष्केण मुच्यते महतो भयात् ॥ 2.124.100 ॥
2.25.m: Having first praised Agni, one is freed from great distress. / And with the four verses beginning with 'na hi', one is freed from great danger.

2.25.s:
ṛcaṃ japtvā ya ityetatsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
prāgbhojanamidaṃ brahma mānavānāṃ maharṣiṇām .. 101 ..
2.25.d:
ऋचं जप्त्वा य इत्येतत्सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
प्राग्भोजनमिदं ब्रह्म मानवानां महर्षिणाम् ॥ 101 ॥
2.25.m: Having muttered the verse beginning with 'yaḥ', one attains all desires. / This is the prayer for the morning meal of men and great sages.

2.25.s:
pūrvāhṇe japato nityaṃ tvarthasiddhiḥ parā bhavet ..
agninetyāśvinaṃ sūktaṃ mṛjākaramudāhṛtam .. 102 ..
2.25.d:
पूर्वाह्णे जपतो नित्यं त्वर्थसिद्धिः परा भवेत् ॥
अग्निनेत्याश्विनं सूक्तं मृजाकरमुदाहृतम् ॥ 102 ॥
2.25.m: For one who mutters it daily in the morning, the highest attainment of one's purpose takes place. / The hymn to the Aśvins beginning with 'agninā' is declared to effect purification.

2.25.s:
samidheti juhotyagnau prāpnuyātkīrtimuttamām ..
dvicatvāriṃśakaṃ caindraṃ japtvā nāśayate ripūn .. 103 ..
2.25.d:
समिधेति जुहोत्यग्नौ प्राप्नुयात्कीर्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥
द्विचत्वारिंशकं चैन्द्रं जप्त्वा नाशयते रिपून् ॥ 103 ॥
2.25.m: One who offers oblations into the fire with 'samidhā' attains supreme renown. / And having muttered the forty-second hymn to Indra, one destroys enemies.

2.25.s:
nāśaṃ mahīti japtvā ca prāpnotyārogyameva ca ..
duḥsvapnaghnāḥ parā japyā naraḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 104 ..
2.25.d:
नाशं महीति जप्त्वा च प्राप्नोत्यारोग्यमेव च ॥
दुःस्वप्नघ्नाः परा जप्या नरः पापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 104 ॥
2.25.m: And having muttered 'na aśaṃ mahī', one attains health. / The supreme verses that destroy bad dreams are to be muttered; a man is freed from sins.

2.25.s:
śanno bhaveti dvābhyāṃ tu bhuktvānnaṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ ...
hṛdayaṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā vyādhibhirnābhibhūyate .. 105 ..
2.25.d:
शन्नो भवेति द्वाभ्यां तु भुक्त्वान्नं प्रयतः शुचिः ॥।
हृदयं पाणिना स्पृष्ट्वा व्याधिभिर्नाभिभूयते ॥ 105 ॥
2.25.m: Restrained and pure, having eaten food, touching the heart with the hand / with the two verses beginning with 'śanno bhava', one is not overcome by diseases.

2.25.s:
ahorātroṣitaḥ snātvā śakraṃ sampūjya mānavaḥ ..
ita ityājyamutpūya juhuyādindramacaryet .. 106 ..
2.25.d:
अहोरात्रोषितः स्नात्वा शक्रं सम्पूज्य मानवः ॥
इत इत्याज्यमुत्पूय जुहुयादिन्द्रमचर्येत् ॥ 106 ॥
2.25.m: Having fasted for a day and night, bathed, and worshipped Śakra, a man, / having purified clarified butter with 'itaḥ', should offer oblations and worship Indra.

2.25.s:
ghṛtaṃ tilaṃ vā dharmajña bhayebhyo vipramucyate ..
tattvāmandamiti snāto hutvā śatrūnpramāpayet ..107..
2.25.d:
घृतं तिलं वा धर्मज्ञ भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ॥
तत्त्वामन्दमिति स्नातो हुत्वा शत्रून्प्रमापयेत् ॥107॥
2.25.m: [Offering] ghee or sesame, O knower of dharma, he is fully freed from fears. / Having bathed and offered oblations with 'tat tvā mandam', one slays one's enemies.

2.25.s:
tānvidyādityadaivatyaṃ japtvā mucyeta bandhanāt ..
yaddyāva iti japtvā ca sarvānkāmānsamaśnute .. 108 ..
2.25.d:
तान्विद्यादित्यदैवत्यं जप्त्वा मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥
यद्द्याव इति जप्त्वा च सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते ॥ 108 ॥
2.25.m: Having muttered 'tān vidyāt' dedicated to the Ādityas, one is freed from bondage. / And having muttered 'yad dyāvaḥ', one obtains all desires.

2.25.s:
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ tu pāvamānaṛcaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
vaikhānasaṛcastriṃśatpavitrāḥ paramāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 109 ..
2.25.d:
पवित्राणां पवित्रं तु पावमानऋचः स्मृताः ॥
वैखानसऋचस्त्रिंशत्पवित्राः परमाः स्मृताः ॥ 109 ॥
2.25.m: The verses addressed to Pavamāna are regarded as the purifier of purifiers. / The thirty verses seen by Vaikhānasa are regarded as supreme purifiers.

2.25.s:
ṛcāṃ dviṣaṣṭiḥ proktaṃ copavasedṛṣisattamaiḥ ..
sarvakalmaṣanāśāya pāvanāya śivāya ca .. 2.124.110 ..
2.25.d:
ऋचां द्विषष्टिः प्रोक्तं चोपवसेदृषिसत्तमैः ॥
सर्वकल्मषनाशाय पावनाय शिवाय च ॥ 2.124.110 ॥
2.25.m: A fast is also prescribed by the best of sages for [muttering] sixty-two verses, / for the destruction of all impurities, for purification, and for auspiciousness.

2.25.s:
svādiṣṭayeti sūktānāṃ saptaṣaṣṭirudāhatāḥ ..
daśottarā ṛcaścaitāḥ pāvamānyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ 111 ..
2.25.d:
स्वादिष्टयेति सूक्तानां सप्तषष्टिरुदाहताः ॥
दशोत्तरा ऋचश्चैताः पावमान्यः शतानि षट् 111 ॥
2.25.m: Sixty-seven hymns beginning with 'svādiṣṭhayā' are cited. / These verses addressed to Pavamāna are six hundred and ten [in number].

2.25.s:
etajjuhvañjapaṃścaiva ghoraṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ jayet ..
ādhyātmikaṃ pavitraṃ ca sūktaṃ japtvālpataḥ kvacit .. 112 ..
2.25.d:
एतज्जुह्वञ्जपंश्चैव घोरं मृत्युभयं जयेत् ॥
आध्यात्मिकं पवित्रं च सूक्तं जप्त्वाल्पतः क्वचित् ॥ 112 ॥
2.25.m: Offering oblations and muttering this, one overcomes terrible fear of death. / Having muttered the spiritual and purifying hymn even briefly somewhere,

2.25.s:
gatimiṣṭāmavāpnoti vindate mahatīṃ śriyam ..
āpohiṣṭheti mahataḥ prayuñjītodakasthitaḥ .. 113 ..
2.25.d:
गतिमिष्टामवाप्नोति विन्दते महतीं श्रियम् ॥
आपोहिष्ठेति महतः प्रयुञ्जीतोदकस्थितः ॥ 113 ॥
2.25.m: one attains a desired state and acquires great fortune. / Standing in water, one should employ the great [hymn] beginning with 'āpo hi ṣṭha'.

2.25.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktastvaśeṣaphalamaśnute ..
upatiṣṭheta rājānaṃ yamasūktena vai dvija .. .. 114 ..
2.25.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तस्त्वशेषफलमश्नुते ॥
उपतिष्ठेत राजानं यमसूक्तेन वै द्विज ॥ ॥ 114 ॥
2.25.m: Freed from all sins, one enjoys the entire fruit. / O twice-born, one should worship the King with the hymn to Yama.

2.25.s:
caturdaśyā tu kurvīta sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi ..
pareyivāṃsamityetatsūktamatra prayojayet .. 115 ..
2.25.d:
चतुर्दश्या तु कुर्वीत स्थालीपाकं यथाविधि ॥
परेयिवांसमित्येतत्सूक्तमत्र प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 115 ॥
2.25.m: On the fourteenth day, one should prepare the vessel-cooked food according to rule. / Here one should employ this hymn beginning with 'pareyivāṃsam'.

2.25.s:
purāyuṣaḥ pramīyeta na sa jātu kathañcana ..
mṛtyumeva prapadyeta paraṃ mṛtyoriva dvija .. 116 ..
2.25.d:
पुरायुषः प्रमीयेत न स जातु कथञ्चन ॥
मृत्युमेव प्रपद्येत परं मृत्योरिव द्विज ॥ 116 ॥
2.25.m: He will never, by any means, die before his full lifespan. / O twice-born, he would meet death only at the other end of death, as it were.

2.25.s:
vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu naktabhojī sadā naraḥ ..
purāyuṣaḥ pramīyeta na sa jātu kathañcana .. 117 ..
2.25.d:
वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु नक्तभोजी सदा नरः ॥
पुरायुषः प्रमीयेत न स जातु कथञ्चन ॥ 117 ॥
2.25.m: A man who continually eats only at night on the full moon day of Vaiśākha / will never, by any means, die before his full lifespan.

2.25.s:
phalāhāro jayenmṛtyuṃ tribhirvarṣaiḥ sadā naraḥ ..
daśākṣaraṃ tu śāntyarthaṃ bhadraṃ na iti saṃsmaran .. 118 ..
2.25.d:
फलाहारो जयेन्मृत्युं त्रिभिर्वर्षैः सदा नरः ॥
दशाक्षरं तु शान्त्यर्थं भद्रं न इति संस्मरन् ॥ 118 ॥
2.25.m: A man who continually lives on fruit for three years overcomes death. / Remembering the ten-syllable [mantra] 'bhadraṃ naḥ' for the sake of peace,

2.25.s:
phalāhāro bhavenmāsaṃ māsānmāsaṃ payaḥ pibet ..
vāyubhakṣyo bhavenmāsaṃ japannetatsahasraśaḥ .. 119 ..
2.25.d:
फलाहारो भवेन्मासं मासान्मासं पयः पिबेत् ॥
वायुभक्ष्यो भवेन्मासं जपन्नेतत्सहस्रशः ॥ 119 ॥
2.25.m: he should live on fruit for a month; from month to month he should drink milk; / he should feed on air for a month, muttering this [mantra] thousands of times.

2.25.s:
antardhānamavāpnoti siddhānpaśyati cāraṇān ..
pradevateti niyato japeta marudhanvasu .. 2.124.120 ..
2.25.d:
अन्तर्धानमवाप्नोति सिद्धान्पश्यति चारणान् ॥
प्रदेवतेति नियतो जपेत मरुधन्वसु ॥ 2.124.120 ॥
2.25.m: He attains invisibility and beholds the siddhas and cāraṇas. / Self-controlled, he should mutter [the hymn beginning with] 'pradevatā' in desert regions.

2.25.s:
prāṇāntike bhaye prāpte kṣipramāyustu vindati ..
vaibhītakāṃstu trīnakṣāngandhaiḥ samadhivāsayet .. 121 ..
2.25.d:
प्राणान्तिके भये प्राप्ते क्षिप्रमायुस्तु विन्दति ॥
वैभीतकांस्तु त्रीनक्षान्गन्धैः समधिवासयेत् ॥ 121 ॥
2.25.m: When a life-threatening danger has arrived, he quickly finds [full] life. / One should perfume three dice of vibhītaka wood with fragrances,

2.25.s:
puṣpairavakireccaiva sthāpayitvā vihāyasi ..
saṃhṛtya pādau tau tatra tiṣṭheddakṣastutiṃ japet .. 122 ..
2.25.d:
पुष्पैरवकिरेच्चैव स्थापयित्वा विहायसि ॥
संहृत्य पादौ तौ तत्र तिष्ठेद्दक्षस्तुतिं जपेत् ॥ 122 ॥
2.25.m: and scatter flowers over them, placing them in the open air. / Drawing up both feet, he should stand there and mutter the praise of Dakṣa.

2.25.s:
prāve māsetyṛcāmekāṃ japecca manasā niśi ..
vyuṣṭāyāmudite sūrye dyūte jayamavāpnuyāt .. 123 ..
2.25.d:
प्रावे मासेत्यृचामेकां जपेच्च मनसा निशि ॥
व्युष्टायामुदिते सूर्ये द्यूते जयमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 123 ॥
2.25.m: And he should mentally mutter the single verse beginning with 'prāve māsa' at night. / When dawn has broken and the sun has risen, he will win victory in gambling.

2.25.s:
abradhnamuṣasānaktetyetatsvastyayanaṃ japet ..
namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣuṣeti ca nityaśaḥ .. 124 ..
2.25.d:
अब्रध्नमुषसानक्तेत्येतत्स्वस्त्ययनं जपेत् ॥
नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षुषेति च नित्यशः ॥ 124 ॥
2.25.m: One should mutter 'abradhnam' and 'uṣasānaktā' as an auspicious rite, / and constantly [the verse beginning with] 'namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣuṣe'.

2.25.s:
tathājyaṃ juhuyānnityaṃ bhītibhyo vipramucyate ..
devasyarīti nityaṃ tu japeddevaṃ samaśnute .. 125 ..
2.25.d:
तथाज्यं जुहुयान्नित्यं भीतिभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ॥
देवस्यरीति नित्यं तु जपेद्देवं समश्नुते ॥ 125 ॥
2.25.m: One should likewise offer clarified butter daily; one is freed from fears. / One should constantly mutter [the verse beginning with] 'devasya rīti'; one attains the deity.

2.25.s:
mā pragāmīti mūḍhastu panthānaṃ pathi vindati ..
kṣīṇāyuriti manyeta yaṃ kacitsuhṛdaṃ priyam ..126..
2.25.d:
मा प्रगामीति मूढस्तु पन्थानं पथि विन्दति ॥
क्षीणायुरिति मन्येत यं कचित्सुहृदं प्रियम् ॥126॥
2.25.m: A bewildered person finds the way on the path with [the verse beginning with] 'mā pragāma'. / When one considers some dear friend to have his lifespan depleted,

2.25.s:
yatteyamiti tu snātastasya mūrdhānamālabhet ..
sahasrakṛtvā pañcāhaṃ tenāyurvindate punaḥ..127..
2.25.d:
यत्तेयमिति तु स्नातस्तस्य मूर्धानमालभेत् ॥
सहस्रकृत्वा पञ्चाहं तेनायुर्विन्दते पुनः॥127॥
2.25.m: having bathed, one should touch his head with [the verse beginning with] 'yat te iyam', / a thousand times for five days; by that, he regains his life.

2.25.s:
sruksruve daśamenaiva idhmamaudumbaraṃ bhavet ..
idamidhmeti juhuyād ghṛtaṃ prājñaḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 128..
2.25.d:
स्रुक्स्रुवे दशमेनैव इध्ममौदुम्बरं भवेत् ॥
इदमिध्मेति जुहुयाद् घृतं प्राज्ञः सहस्रशः ॥ 128॥
2.25.m: The wooden ladle and spoon should be made [as prescribed] by the tenth [rule]; the firewood should be of udumbara. / With 'idam idhmam', the wise man should offer clarified butter thousands of times.

2.25.s:
paśukāmo gavāṃ goṣṭhe annakāmaścatuṣpathe ..
pārāvataḥ svastyayanaṃ snātakasya vidhīyate .. 129 ..
2.25.d:
पशुकामो गवां गोष्ठे अन्नकामश्चतुष्पथे ॥
पारावतः स्वस्त्ययनं स्नातकस्य विधीयते ॥ 129 ॥
2.25.m: One desiring cattle [should offer] in a cowpen; one desiring food, at a crossroads. / Pārāvata is prescribed as an auspicious blessing for a snātaka.

2.25.s:
bṛhaspate prathamamiti jñānakāmasya bhārgava ..
vayaḥ suparṇamityetāṃ japanvai vindate śriyam ..2.124.130..
2.25.d:
बृहस्पते प्रथममिति ज्ञानकामस्य भार्गव ॥
वयः सुपर्णमित्येतां जपन्वै विन्दते श्रियम् ॥2.124.130॥
2.25.m: "O Bṛhaspati, first..." is for one who desires knowledge, O Bhārgava. / Reciting "The well-winged bird...", one indeed attains fortune.

2.25.s:
yaste manyo iti sadā mayatnaghnaṃ vidhīyate ..
haviṣmatīyamabhyasya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 131 ..
2.25.d:
यस्ते मन्यो इति सदा मयत्नघ्नं विधीयते ॥
हविष्मतीयमभ्यस्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 131 ॥
2.25.m: "Your wrath..." is always prescribed for destroying enemies. / Having practiced the Haviṣmatī hymn, one is freed from all sins.

2.25.s:
yā oṣadhīḥ svastyayanaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam .. .
tasya māyā vinaśyeta kāyāgnirvardhate tathā .. 132 ..
2.25.d:
या ओषधीः स्वस्त्ययनं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ॥ ।
तस्य माया विनश्येत कायाग्निर्वर्धते तथा ॥ 132 ॥
2.25.m: "The herbs..." is an auspicious blessing, destroying all sins. / His illusion would be destroyed, and bodily fire increases as well.

2.25.s:
bṛhaspatiḥ pratītyetad vṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet ..
sarvatra tu parā śaktirjñeyā pratirathā tathā .. .. 133 ..
2.25.d:
बृहस्पतिः प्रतीत्येतद् वृष्टिकामः प्रयोजयेत् ॥
सर्वत्र तु परा शक्तिर्ज्ञेया प्रतिरथा तथा ॥ ॥ 133 ॥
2.25.m: One desiring rain should employ "Bṛhaspati..." / But everywhere the Pratiratha hymn is to be known as supreme power.

2.25.s:
bhūtāṃśaṃ kāśyapaṃ nityaṃ prajākāmasya kīrtitam ..
ahaṃ rudrebhirityetadvāggmī bhavati mānavaḥ .. 134 ..
2.25.d:
भूतांशं काश्यपं नित्यं प्रजाकामस्य कीर्तितम् ॥
अहं रुद्रेभिरित्येतद्वाग्ग्मी भवति मानवः ॥ 134 ॥
2.25.m: The hymn to Bhūtāṃśa Kāśyapa is declared as constant for one desiring offspring. / Through "I with the Rudras...", a man becomes eloquent.

2.25.s:
na yonau jāyate vidvāṃñjapannatrīti rātriṣu ..
rātrisūktaṃ japanrātrau rātrikṣemī bhavennaraḥ .. 135 ..
2.25.d:
न योनौ जायते विद्वांञ्जपन्नत्रीति रात्रिषु ॥
रात्रिसूक्तं जपन्रात्रौ रात्रिक्षेमी भवेन्नरः ॥ 135 ॥
2.25.m: The wise man reciting "Atri..." at night is not reborn in a womb. / Reciting the Rātrisūkta at night, a man becomes secure at night.

2.25.s:
yā kalpayatīti japennityaṃ kṛtvā vināśanam ..
āyuṣyaṃ caiva varcasyaṃ sūktaṃ dākṣāyaṇaṃ mahat .. 136 ..
2.25.d:
या कल्पयतीति जपेन्नित्यं कृत्वा विनाशनम् ॥
आयुष्यं चैव वर्चस्यं सूक्तं दाक्षायणं महत् ॥ 136 ॥
2.25.m: Having made it a daily practice, one should recite "She who prepares..." for destruction [of evils]. / The great Dākṣāyaṇa hymn bestows longevity and luster.

2.25.s:
uta devā iti japedāmayaghnaṃ dhṛtavrataḥ ..
agne agnāva ityeddhanakāmaḥ prayojayet .. 137 ..
2.25.d:
उत देवा इति जपेदामयघ्नं धृतव्रतः ॥
अग्ने अग्नाव इत्येद्धनकामः प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 137 ॥
2.25.m: One observing vows should recite "Even the gods...", which destroys disease. / One desiring wealth should employ "Agni in Agni..."

2.25.s:
vaibhītake'bdaṃ hutvāgniṃ dviṣaddveṣaṃ tato japet ..
dviṣantu dhanvinaṃ hutvā dviṣato vindate dhanam .. 138 ..
2.25.d:
वैभीतकेऽब्दं हुत्वाग्निं द्विषद्द्वेषं ततो जपेत् ॥
द्विषन्तु धन्विनं हुत्वा द्विषतो विन्दते धनम् ॥ 138 ॥
2.25.m: Having offered into fire with bibhītaka wood for a year, one should then recite the Dviṣaddveṣa hymn. / Having offered against the hostile archer, he wins the enemy's wealth.

2.25.s:
ayamagne janiteti japedagniṃ bhaye sati ..
dvimārjanniti pāṭhaṃ tu japannutthāpayeddvijaḥ .. 139 ..
2.25.d:
अयमग्ने जनितेति जपेदग्निं भये सति ॥
द्विमार्जन्निति पाठं तु जपन्नुत्थापयेद्द्विजः ॥ 139 ॥
2.25.m: When there is fear, one should recite "This Agni is the producer..." over fire. / A twice-born, reciting the text "Wiping twofold...", should awaken [the fire].

2.25.s:
prātaśca pāṭhayedenaṃ saṃsadi brahmacāriṇām ..
imāmiti ca sūktena śatakṛtvo'bhimantritam .. 2.124.140 ..
2.25.d:
प्रातश्च पाठयेदेनं संसदि ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
इमामिति च सूक्तेन शतकृत्वोऽभिमन्त्रितम् ॥ 2.124.140 ॥
2.25.m: And in the morning he should have him recite it in the assembly of students. / And consecrated a hundred times with the hymn "This..."

2.25.s:
ghṛtena pītvā taṃ prātaḥ sapatnībhirvimucyate ..
araṇyānītyaraṇyeṣu japettadbhayanāśanam .. 141 ..
2.25.d:
घृतेन पीत्वा तं प्रातः सपत्नीभिर्विमुच्यते ॥
अरण्यानीत्यरण्येषु जपेत्तद्भयनाशनम् ॥ 141 ॥
2.25.m: Having drunk it with ghee in the morning, one is freed from co-wives. / One should recite "O Araṇyānī..." in forests; it destroys the fear of them.

2.25.s:
śraddhāsūktaṃ japennityaṃ śraddhākāmavivardhanam ..
brāhmī yadyasya sūkte dve japeta niyataḥ sadā .. 142..
2.25.d:
श्रद्धासूक्तं जपेन्नित्यं श्रद्धाकामविवर्धनम् ॥
ब्राह्मी यद्यस्य सूक्ते द्वे जपेत नियतः सदा ॥ 142॥
2.25.m: One should daily recite the Śraddhāsūkta, which increases faith and desire. / If restrained, he should always recite the two hymns to Brāhmī.

2.25.s:
śaṃkhapuṣpīṃ tu payasā brāhmīpuṣpāṇi sarpiṣā ..
śatāvarī tu payasā vacāmadbhirghṛtena vā .. 143 ..
2.25.d:
शंखपुष्पीं तु पयसा ब्राह्मीपुष्पाणि सर्पिषा ॥
शतावरी तु पयसा वचामद्भिर्घृतेन वा ॥ 143 ॥
2.25.m: śaṅkhapuṣpī with milk, brāhmī flowers with ghee, / śatāvarī with milk, or vacā with water or ghee:

2.25.s:
sūktābhyāṃ hyanumantrābhyāṃ caikaikaṃ tu tryahaṃ pibet ..
śraddhāṃ medhāṃ smṛtiṃ puṣṭiṃ varṇaṃ lakṣmīṃ ca vindati .. 144 ..
2.25.d:
सूक्ताभ्यां ह्यनुमन्त्राभ्यां चैकैकं तु त्र्यहं पिबेत् ॥
श्रद्धां मेधां स्मृतिं पुष्टिं वर्णं लक्ष्मीं च विन्दति ॥ 144 ॥
2.25.m: Consecrated by the two hymns, he should drink each one for three days. / He attains faith, intelligence, memory, strength, complexion, and fortune.

2.25.s:
śāsannarthāñjapannityaṃ saṃgrāme vijigīṣataḥ ..
gṛhītadakṣiṇādarbhāngṛhītvā saṃspṛśejjapet .. 145 ..
2.25.d:
शासन्नर्थाञ्जपन्नित्यं संग्रामे विजिगीषतः ॥
गृहीतदक्षिणादर्भान्गृहीत्वा संस्पृशेज्जपेत् ॥ 145 ॥
2.25.m: Reciting daily "Ordering the aims...", of those wishing to conquer in battle, / taking up darbha grass held in the right hand, touching it, one should recite.

2.25.s:
muñcāmi tvā haviṣeti yakṣmāṇamapakarṣati ..
brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃvidānaṃ garbhamṛtyuvināśanam .. 146 ..
2.25.d:
मुञ्चामि त्वा हविषेति यक्ष्माणमपकर्षति ॥
ब्रह्मणाग्निः संविदानं गर्भमृत्युविनाशनम् ॥ 146 ॥
2.25.m: "I release you with the oblation..." drives away consumption. / "Agni knowing along with prayer..." destroys the death of the embryo.

2.25.s:
apehīti japetsūktaṃ śucirduḥsvapnanāśanam ..
devāḥ kapota iti tu kapotasyopaveśane .. 147 ..
2.25.d:
अपेहीति जपेत्सूक्तं शुचिर्दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् ॥
देवाः कपोत इति तु कपोतस्योपवेशने ॥ 147 ॥
2.25.m: Pure, one should recite the hymn "Depart...", which destroys bad dreams. / And "The gods, the dove..." [is recited] upon the landing of a dove.

2.25.s:
kauśikasya japetsūktaṃ ghṛtena juhuyāttathā ..
sapatnaghnaṃ prayuñjīta ṛṣabhaṃ japahomayoḥ .. 148 ..
2.25.d:
कौशिकस्य जपेत्सूक्तं घृतेन जुहुयात्तथा ॥
सपत्नघ्नं प्रयुञ्जीत ऋषभं जपहोमयोः ॥ 148 ॥
2.25.m: One should recite the hymn of Kauśika and offer oblations with ghee. / One should employ the Ṛṣabha hymn, which destroys rivals, in recitation and homa.

2.25.s:
yenedamiti japtvā vai samādhiṃ vindate parām ..
mayobhūrvāta iti tu gavāṃ svastyayanaṃ param .. 149 ..
2.25.d:
येनेदमिति जप्त्वा वै समाधिं विन्दते पराम् ॥
मयोभूर्वात इति तु गवां स्वस्त्ययनं परम् ॥ 149 ॥
2.25.m: Having recited "By which this...", one indeed attains supreme absorption. / But "The wind bringing health..." is a supreme blessing for cattle.

2.25.s:
yavānāṃ ca ghṛtāktānāṃ gomayāgnau samāhitaḥ ..
juhuyādgoṣṭha madhye tu dadhimadhvājyasaṃskṛtam .. 2.124.150 ..
2.25.d:
यवानां च घृताक्तानां गोमयाग्नौ समाहितः ॥
जुहुयाद्गोष्ठ मध्ये तु दधिमध्वाज्यसंस्कृतम् ॥ 2.124.150 ॥
2.25.m: Concentrated, in the midst of a cowshed, in a fire of cow dung, / one should offer barley smeared with ghee, prepared with curds, honey, and clarified butter.

2.25.s:
patantamiti nityaṃ tu japeta vijane vane ..
śāmbarīmindrajālāṃ vā mālāmetena dhārayet .. 151 ..
2.25.d:
पतन्तमिति नित्यं तु जपेत विजने वने ॥
शाम्बरीमिन्द्रजालां वा मालामेतेन धारयेत् ॥ 151 ॥
2.25.m: One should always recite "The flying..." in an uninhabited forest. / By this one should wear a garland against Śambara's sorcery or jugglery.

2.25.s:
adṛśyānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ māyāmetena bādhate ..
na pratiṣṭheti svastyayanaṃ nārīgarbhavivardhanam .. 152 ..
2.25.d:
अदृश्यानां च सत्त्वानां मायामेतेन बाधते ॥
न प्रतिष्ठेति स्वस्त्ययनं नारीगर्भविवर्धनम् ॥ 152 ॥
2.25.m: And by this he counters the sorcery of invisible beings. / "No foundation..." is an auspicious blessing that promotes the womb of women.

2.25.s:
viṣṇurṇyānamitīmaṃ ca tathaivāparamucyate ..
mahityṛṇāṃ mavosviti parisvastyayanaṃ japet .. 153 .
2.25.d:
विष्णुर्ण्यानमितीमं च तथैवापरमुच्यते ॥
महित्यृणां मवोस्विति परिस्वस्त्ययनं जपेत् ॥ 153 ।
2.25.m: And likewise another is declared: "Viṣṇu's contemplation..." / One should recite "Of the great debts..." [and] "Protect well..." as a protective blessing.

2.25.s:
prāpayedvidviṣadveṣaṃ japecca ripunāśanam ..
āyaṅgauḥ saptarājñastu sarpānetaiḥ prasādhayet .. .. 154 ..
2.25.d:
प्रापयेद्विद्विषद्वेषं जपेच्च रिपुनाशनम् ॥
आयङ्गौः सप्तराज्ञस्तु सर्पानेतैः प्रसाधयेत् ॥ ॥ 154 ॥
2.25.m: He should direct hostility against enemies, and should recite for the destruction of adversaries. / With "This spotted bull..." and the Saptarājñī hymns, he should overcome serpents.

2.25.s:
saṃsamidyuvaseccaitatsaubhrātṛkaraṇaṃ mahata ..
tacchaṃyorāvṛṇīmahe japetsvastyayanaṃ sadā .. 155 ..
2.25.d:
संसमिद्युवसेच्चैतत्सौभ्रातृकरणं महत ॥
तच्छंयोरावृणीमहे जपेत्स्वस्त्ययनं सदा ॥ 155 ॥
2.25.m: "You unite fully..." is a great producer of good brotherhood. / One should always recite "That blessing and peace we choose..." as an auspicious blessing.

2.25.s:
pitṝṇāṃ saṃhitāṃ vidyātpitṝnprīṇāti vai tathā ..
vāstoṣpatena mantreṇa yajeta gṛhadevatām .. 156 ..
2.25.d:
पितॄणां संहितां विद्यात्पितॄन्प्रीणाति वै तथा ॥
वास्तोष्पतेन मन्त्रेण यजेत गृहदेवताम् ॥ 156 ॥
2.25.m: One should know the collection for the ancestors; he thus pleases the ancestors. / With the Vāstoṣpati mantra, he should worship the deity of the house.

2.25.s:
talliṅgairdevatāmantrairdevārādhanamucyate ..
japasyeṣa vidhiḥ prokto hute yajñe viśeṣataḥ .. ..157..
2.25.d:
तल्लिङ्गैर्देवतामन्त्रैर्देवाराधनमुच्यते ॥
जपस्येष विधिः प्रोक्तो हुते यज्ञे विशेषतः ॥ ॥157॥
2.25.m: Worship of the gods is declared through deity-mantras bearing their characteristic marks. / This rule of recitation has been stated, especially when sacrifice has been offered.

2.25.s:
homānte dakṣiṇā deyā yathāśaktyā ca bhārgava ..
hutena śamyate pāpaṃ hutamannena śamyate ..158..
2.25.d:
होमान्ते दक्षिणा देया यथाशक्त्या च भार्गव ॥
हुतेन शम्यते पापं हुतमन्नेन शम्यते ॥158॥
2.25.m: At the conclusion of the homa, a sacrificial fee is to be given according to one's ability, O Bhārgava. / Sin is pacified by what is offered; what is offered is pacified by food.

2.25.s:
annaṃ hiraṇyadānena amoghā brāhmaṇāśiṣaḥ..
siddhārthakā yavā dhānyaṃ payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā..159..
2.25.d:
अन्नं हिरण्यदानेन अमोघा ब्राह्मणाशिषः॥
सिद्धार्थका यवा धान्यं पयो दधि घृतं तथा॥159॥
2.25.m: Food [is pacified] by the gift of gold; the blessings of brahmins are unfailing. / White mustard, barley, grain, milk, curds, and ghee,

2.25.s:
kṣīravṛkṣāstathedhmāśca sarvakāmapradāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
samidhaḥ kaṇṭakinyaśca rājikā rudhiraṃ viṣam .. .. 2.124.160..
2.25.d:
क्षीरवृक्षास्तथेध्माश्च सर्वकामप्रदाः स्मृताः ॥
समिधः कण्टकिन्यश्च राजिका रुधिरं विषम् ॥ ॥ 2.124.160॥
2.25.m: milky trees and firewood are remembered as granting all desires. / Thorny firewood sticks, black mustard seeds, blood, poison,

2.25.s:
tailaṃ ca bhṛguśārdūla vijñeyamabhicārakam ..
saktavaḥ phalamūlāni śākāni vividhāni ca .. 161 ..
2.25.d:
तैलं च भृगुशार्दूल विज्ञेयमभिचारकम् ॥
सक्तवः फलमूलानि शाकानि विविधानि च ॥ 161 ॥
2.25.m: and oil, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, are to be known as used for sorcery. / Roasted barley meal, fruits and roots, various vegetables,

2.25.s:
payo dadhi suvarṇaṃ ca bhaikṣyaṃ nāśanamucyate ..
haviḥsnānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ sarvatra bhṛgusattama..162..
2.25.d:
पयो दधि सुवर्णं च भैक्ष्यं नाशनमुच्यते ॥
हविःस्नानं च कर्तव्यं सर्वत्र भृगुसत्तम॥162॥
2.25.m: milk, curds, gold, and alms are declared as an expiation. / And ablution with sacrificial offerings must be performed everywhere, O best of the Bhṛgus.

2.25.s:
ṛcāṃ vidhānaṃ kathitaṃ tavaitatsamāsataḥ karmakaraṃ dvijānām ..
tato vidhānaṃ yajuṣāṃ nibodha samāsato dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭha .. 163 ..
2.125
puṣkara uvāca ..
oṃkārapūrvikā nāma mahāvyāhatayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
sarvakalmaṣanāśinyaḥ sarvakarmapradāstathā..1..
ājyāhutisahasreṇa devamārādhayeddvija..
manasaḥ kāṃkṣitaṃ rāma manaseptitakāmadam .. 2 ..
śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryāttilaiḥ pāpāpanuttaye ..
dhānyaiḥ siddhārthakaiścaiva sarvakāmakaraṃ tathā .. 3 ..
audumbarībhiridhmābhiḥ paśukāmasya śasyate ..
daśa caivānnakāmasya payasā śāntimicchataḥ .. 4 ..
apāmārgasamidbhiśca kāmayankanakaṃ bahu ..
kanyākāmo ghṛtāktāni yugmaśo grathitāni ca..5..
jātīpuṣpāṇi juhuyādvāmārthī tilataṇḍulam ..
vaśīkarmaṇi śākhoṭavāśāpāmārgameva ca .. 6 ..
2.25.d:
ऋचां विधानं कथितं तवैतत्समासतः कर्मकरं द्विजानाम् ॥
ततो विधानं यजुषां निबोध समासतो धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठ ॥ 163 ॥
2.125
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
ओंकारपूर्विका नाम महाव्याहतयः स्मृताः ॥
सर्वकल्मषनाशिन्यः सर्वकर्मप्रदास्तथा॥1॥
आज्याहुतिसहस्रेण देवमाराधयेद्द्विज॥
मनसः कांक्षितं राम मनसेप्तितकामदम् ॥ 2 ॥
शान्तिकामो यवैः कुर्यात्तिलैः पापापनुत्तये ॥
धान्यैः सिद्धार्थकैश्चैव सर्वकामकरं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
औदुम्बरीभिरिध्माभिः पशुकामस्य शस्यते ॥
दश चैवान्नकामस्य पयसा शान्तिमिच्छतः ॥ 4 ॥
अपामार्गसमिद्भिश्च कामयन्कनकं बहु ॥
कन्याकामो घृताक्तानि युग्मशो ग्रथितानि च॥5॥
जातीपुष्पाणि जुहुयाद्वामार्थी तिलतण्डुलम् ॥
वशीकर्मणि शाखोटवाशापामार्गमेव च ॥ 6 ॥
2.25.m:
This rule of the Ṛgvedic verses has been told to you in brief, bringing ritual success for twice-borns. / Then learn the rule of the Yajurvedic formulas in brief, O best of the upholders of dharma.
2.125
Puṣkara said:
The great utterances, preceded by the syllable Om, are remembered / as destroying all impurities and granting [the fruit of] all rites.
With a thousand oblations of clarified butter, a twice-born should worship the god. / It grants the desire wished by the mind, O Rāma, fulfilling what is sought by the intellect.
Desiring pacification, one should perform it with barley; with sesame seeds for the dispelling of sins; / and with grains and white mustard seeds, it fulfills all desires.
With kindling sticks of udumbara wood it is praised for one desiring cattle; / and ten [oblations] for one desiring food; with milk for one wishing pacification;
and with kindling sticks of apāmārga for one desiring much gold; / one desiring a maiden [should offer] pairs tied together and smeared with ghee
of jasmine flowers; one seeking a beautiful woman should offer sesame and rice. / In a rite of subjugation, [he should offer] śākhoṭa, vāsā, and apāmārga.

2.25.d:
वसासृङ्मिश्रसमिधो व्याधिघातस्य भार्गव ॥
क्रुद्धस्तु जुहुयात्सम्यक् शत्रूणां वधकाम्यया ॥ 7 ॥
सर्वव्रीहिमयीं कृत्वा राज्ञः प्रतिकृतिं द्विजः ॥
सहस्रशस्तु जुहुयात्प्रजावशगतो भवेत् ॥ 8 ॥
वस्त्रकामस्य पुष्पाणि दूर्वा व्याधिविनाशनी ॥
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य वामाग्रं च विधीयते ॥ 9 ॥
प्रत्यङ्गिरेप्सुर्जुहुयात्तुषकण्टकभस्मभिः ॥
विद्वेषणे च पक्षाणि काककौशिकयोस्तथा ॥ 2.125.10 ॥
कापिलं तु घृतं हुत्वा तथा चन्द्रग्रहे द्विज ॥
वचाचूर्णेन संपीतांस्तानानीय च तां वचाम् ॥ 11 ॥
सहस्रमन्त्रितां भुक्त्वा मेधावी जायते नरः ॥
सूर्योदयेऽर्काभिमुखं पुत्रकामो जपेन्नरः ॥ 12॥
एकादश्यां गुग्गुलं लौहं बैल्वं खादिरमेव वा ॥
द्विषन्तन्त्वां बधानीति निखनेद्रिपुवेश्मनि ॥ 13 ॥
2.25.m:
Kindling sticks mixed with fat and blood are for the destruction of disease, O Bhārgava. / But when angered, one should offer properly with the desire to kill enemies.
Having made an effigy of a king out of all grains of rice, a twice-born / should offer into the fire by thousands; he would become one under whom the subjects fall.
Flowers are for one desiring garments; dūrvā grass destroys disease. / And for one desiring brahminical luster, the left tip is prescribed.
One desiring [to practice] counter-sorcery should sacrifice with chaff, thorns, and ashes; / and in causing hatred, likewise with the wings of a crow and an owl.
Having offered ghee from a brown cow, O twice-born, during a lunar eclipse, / and fetching those [roots of] vacā saturated with vacā powder,
and eating them consecrated a thousand times with mantras, a man becomes intelligent. / A man desiring a son should chant facing the sun at sunrise.
On the eleventh day, bdellium, iron, or [wood] of bilva or khadira, / [with the mantra,] 'I bind you who hate,' one should bury in the enemy's dwelling.

2.25.d:
उच्चाटनमिदं कर्म शत्रूणां कथितं तव ॥
शक्रं ध्रुवं भूपतये महाव्याहृतिभिर्भवेत् ॥ 14 ॥
सूर्यस्त्वेति तथा मन्त्रं ज्ञेया प्रत्यङ्गिरा परा ॥
एतेनौदुम्बरैरिध्मैर्देवं वर्षापयेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 15 ॥
अहोरात्रं जले जप्त्वा चक्षुष्मानित्ययं द्विज ॥
प्रणष्टचक्षुर्धर्मज्ञ योगमाप्नोति चक्षुषः ॥16 ॥
उपप्रयन्तमित्येतद्धुत्वा विप्रो महानसे ॥
अनुवाकं महाभाग नित्यसन्नेन युज्यते ॥ 17 ॥
तनूपाग्नेऽसि इति च दूर्वा हुत्वा रुजान्वितः ॥
व्याधिमोक्षमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 18 ॥
इहैव तेभ्यः पतितं गृहीत्वा गोमयं द्विज ॥
घृताज्यमधुसंयुक्तं हुत्वा धेनुं तु तां लभेत् ॥ 19 ॥
एष ते रुद्रभागेति हुत्वा राम गवेधुकाम् ॥
अर्धर्चेन तथाप्नोति धनं नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ 2.125.20 ॥
2.25.m:
This rite of eradication of enemies has been told to you. / A king will become firm like Śakra by means of the Mahāvyāhṛtis.
With the mantra 'Sūryas tvā', the supreme Pratyaṅgirā is to be understood. / With this and with firewood of udumbara, one will surely make the god rain.
Having chanted 'Cakṣuṣmān' in water for a day and night, O twice-born, / one who has lost his sight, O knower of dharma, obtains the use of his eyes.
A brahmin having offered the anuvāka beginning with 'Upaprayantam' in the kitchen, / O illustrious one, is constantly provided with food.
And one afflicted with sickness, having offered dūrvā grass with 'Tanūpāgne ’si,' / attains freedom from disease; no doubt should be entertained here.
Taking cow-dung fallen from them right here, O twice-born, / and offering it mixed with clarified butter and honey, he obtains that very milch cow.
Having offered gavedhukā grass with 'Eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ,' O Rāma, / he likewise obtains wealth through the half-verse; there is no doubt about this.

2.25.d:
अर्धर्चेन द्वितीयेन क्षेत्रमध्ये बलिं हरेत् ॥
मूषिकाशलभोत्पाते सुरामांसासवादिभिः॥21॥
भेषजमिति मन्त्रेण दध्याज्यमधुहोमकः ॥
चतुष्पदानां सर्वेषामुपसर्गं विनाशयेत् ॥ 22 ॥
त्र्यम्बकं यजामहेति होमः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥
कन्यानाम गृहीत्वा च कन्यालाभकरः परः ॥ 23 ॥
भयेषु च जपेन्नित्यं भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ॥
धत्तूरपुष्पं सघृतं तथा हुत्वा चतुष्पथे ॥ 24 ॥ ।
शून्ये शिवालये वापि शिवात्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
हुत्वा च गुग्गुलं राम स्वयं पश्यति शङ्करम् ॥ 25 ॥
अकृत्या इति चैवाष्टौ ऋचो हुत्वा घृतादिभिः ॥
अन्वहं त्वापदां नाशं स्वकुले कुरुते धुवम् ॥ 26 ॥
भवत्युत्तरवादी च जप्त्वा च विदसीत्यृचम् ॥
अग्नेस्तनोरिति तथा हुत्वा च तिल तण्डुलैः ॥ 27 ॥
सहस्रशस्तु धर्मज्ञ भवेत्सर्वातिथिर्नरः ॥
युञ्जते मन इत्येतदनुवाकं तु वैष्णवम् ॥ 28 ॥
2.25.m:
With the second half-verse, he should offer an oblation in the middle of the field / when an infestation of mice or locusts occurs, using liquor, meat, spirituous drinks, and the like.
One who sacrifices with curds, clarified butter, and honey using the mantra 'Bheṣajam' / destroys all afflictions of quadrupeds.
The homa with 'Tryambakaṃ yajāmahe' accomplishes all purposes, / and taking the name of a maiden, it is supreme in securing a maiden.
And in times of danger, one should recite it constantly; one is delivered from dangers. / Likewise, having offered dhattūra flowers with ghee at a crossroads,
or in an empty temple of Śiva, one obtains desires from Śiva; / and having offered bdellium, O Rāma, one sees Śaṅkara himself.
And having offered the eight verses beginning with 'Akṛtyai' with ghee and other substances, / he certainly brings about the destruction of misfortunes in his own family every day.
And having chanted the verse 'Vidāsi', he becomes victorious in debate. / And having offered sesame seeds and rice with 'Agnestanur',
thousands of times, O knower of dharma, a man becomes a host to all guests. / One should recite morning and evening this Vaiṣṇava anuvāka,

2.25.d:
सायं प्रातः समासीत दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ॥
दिवो वा विष्ण इत्यस्य कर्म व्याहृतिवद्भवेत् ॥ 29 ॥
विष्णोरराटमित्येतत्सर्वबाधाविनाशनम् ॥
रक्षोघ्नं च यशस्यं च तथैव विवर प्रदम्॥2.125.30॥
अयन्नो यज्ञ इत्येतत्संग्रामे विजयप्रदम् ॥
इदमापः प्रवहत स्नाने पापापनोदनम् ॥ 31 ॥
दैवांश इति दैवेतदभिचारेषु योजयेत् ॥
व्याधिघातः समिद्भिस्तु राजिकासृग्विषैस्तथा॥32॥
यक्ष्माहीति तथा हुत्वा बहिर्निर्गम्य मानवः॥
उपश्रुतिं तु गृह्णीयात्सा तस्यावितथा भवेत्॥33॥
अग्ने पवस्वेति हुतं ब्रह्मवर्चसकारकम् ॥
उदुत्यं चित्रमित्यस्य कर्म व्याहतिवद्भवेत् ॥ 34 ॥
यस्मान्नरादभ्यधिको नरो भवितुमिच्छति ॥
स्वस्ति नेन्द्रेति तु जपेत्तस्य नामान्तसंयुतम् ॥ 35 ॥
भवत्यभ्यधिकस्तस्माद्विद्यया यशसा श्रिया ॥
तथा होमादनेनैव दासलाभमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 36 ॥
2.25.m:
beginning with 'Yuñjate manaḥ'; he will attain a long life. / The ritual of 'Divo vā viṣṇo' should be performed like that of the vyāhṛtis.
This verse beginning with 'Viṣṇor arāṭam' destroys all obstacles; / it slays demons, brings renown, and likewise bestows an opening.
This [mantra] 'Ayaṃ no yajñaḥ' bestows victory in battle. / 'Idam āpaḥ pravahata' expels sin during bathing.
One should employ 'Daivāṃśaḥ' in rites of sorcery. / The destruction of disease [is effected] with firewood, black mustard, blood, and poison.
Having offered with 'Yakṣmāhi' and gone outside, a man / should listen for an omen of speech; it will not be false for him.
An offering with 'Agne pavasva' produces Vedic lustre. / The ritual of 'Ud u tyaṃ citram' should be performed like that of the vyāhṛtis.
A man who wishes to become superior to another man / should chant 'Svasti na indraḥ' joined with the other's name at the end.
He becomes superior to him in learning, renown, and fortune. / Likewise, through the homa with this very [mantra], he obtains servants.

2.25.d:

कन्याग्रे निखनेद्द्वारि ततस्सास्मै प्रदीयते ॥ 37 ॥
देवस्येति तरीतेन हुतेनैवान्नवान्भवेत् ॥
वाजस्यसति चैतेन हुत्वाज्यं सप्तभिर्द्विजः ॥ 38 ॥
यदेव जुहुयात्पश्चात्तदेवाक्षयमाप्नुयात् ॥

तिलैर्यवैश्च धर्मज्ञस्तथापामार्गतण्डुलैः ॥
सहस्रमन्त्रितां कृत्वा तथा गोरोचनां द्विजः ॥ 2.125.40 ॥
तिलकं च तथा कृत्वा जनस्य प्रियतां व्रजेत् ॥
पौर्णमास्यां तथा हुत्वा मेघं राजानमित्यपि ॥ 41 ॥
उपस्थानं तथा कृत्वा दत्त्वा चान्नं द्विजन्मने ॥
सोमयाजी भवेद्राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 42 ॥
एष ते निरृतेत्याभिरभिचारककर्मणा ॥
गृहान्नैरृत्यके भागे हुत्वा स्नात्वा नदीजले ॥ 43 ॥
2.25.m:
[Reciting] 'Viśvakarmā' over sacrificial food, he should bury an iron needle ten fingers long / before the maiden at the door; then she is given to him.
By offering with 'Devasya', one will become possessed of food. / And offering ghee seven times with 'Vājasya saṃprasawe', a twice-born,
whatever he sacrifices afterwards, that very thing he obtains imperishably. / Desiring wealth, the best of the twice-born should sacrifice with 'Agne accha',
with sesame seeds and barley, O knower of dharma, and likewise with apāmārga grains. / A twice-born having consecrated gorocanā a thousand times,
and making a mark on his forehead with it, will become dear to people. / Likewise, having sacrificed on the full-moon day with 'Meghaṃ rājānam',
and performing worship and giving food to a twice-born, / he will become a performer of Soma sacrifices, O Rāma; no doubt should be entertained here.
By means of an act of sorcery with the [verses] beginning with 'Eṣā te nirṛte', / having sacrificed in the south-western part of the house and bathed in river water,

manuṣyāṇāṃ narendrāṇāṃ bālānāṃ yoṣitāmapi .. 46 ..
grāmāṇāṃ nagarāṇāṃ ca deśānāmapi bhārgava ..
anidrutānāṃ dharmajña vyādhitānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 47 ..
maraṇe samanuprāpte ripuje ca tathā bhaye ..
rudrahomaḥ parā śāntiḥ pāyasena ghṛtena ca .. 48 ..
kūṣmāṇḍairghṛtahomena sarvānpāpānapohati ..
saktuyāvakabhaikṣyāśī naktaṃ manujasattama .. 49 ..
bahiḥ snānarato māsānmucyate brahmahatyayā ..
madhuvāteti mantreṇa hutvaivājyamatandritaḥ .. 2.125.50 ..
2.25.d:
कापिलाद्गोमयान्नित्यं पञ्चगव्याभिषेचितम् ॥
कृत्वा रुद्रांस्तथा जप्त्वा मैत्र्यमाप्नोति गुह्यकैः ॥ 44 ॥
रुद्राणां च तथा जप्यं सर्वाघविनिषूदनम् ॥
सर्वकर्मकरं होमं तथा सर्वत्र शान्तिदम् ॥ 45 ॥
अजाविकानामश्वानां कुञ्जराणां तथा गवाम् ॥
मनुष्याणां नरेन्द्राणां बालानां योषितामपि ॥ 46 ॥
ग्रामाणां नगराणां च देशानामपि भार्गव ॥
अनिद्रुतानां धर्मज्ञ व्याधितानां तथैव च ॥ 47 ॥
मरणे समनुप्राप्ते रिपुजे च तथा भये ॥
रुद्रहोमः परा शान्तिः पायसेन घृतेन च ॥ 48 ॥
कूष्माण्डैर्घृतहोमेन सर्वान्पापानपोहति ॥
सक्तुयावकभैक्ष्याशी नक्तं मनुजसत्तम ॥ 49 ॥
बहिः स्नानरतो मासान्मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
मधुवातेति मन्त्रेण हुत्वैवाज्यमतन्द्रितः ॥ 2.125.50 ॥
2.25.m:
[making] Rudras daily from the dung of a brown cow sprinkled with pañcagavya / and chanting [the Śatarudrīya], he attains friendship with the Guhyakas.
The recitation of the Rudras destroys all sins; / the homa accomplishes all deeds and brings pacification everywhere:
for goats, sheep, horses, elephants, and cows, / for men, kings, children, and women,
for villages, cities, and countries, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / for those who are unmolested and those who are diseased, O knower of dharma.
When death is imminent and when fear arising from enemies occurs, / the Rudra homa with milk-rice and ghee is the supreme pacification.
With a homa of ghee using the Kūṣmāṇḍa [mantras], he removes all sins, / eating barley meal, barley gruel, or begged food at night, O best of men.
Devoting himself to bathing outdoors, he is freed from the murder of a brahmin after a month. / Having unweariedly offered ghee with the mantra 'Madhu vātāḥ',

2.25.s:
sahasraśastu dharmajña dīrghamāpnoti jīvitam ..
hutvā dadhnā tathā putrānprāpnoti manasepsitān .. 51 ..
gugguloḥ kaṇikābhistu saubhāgyaṃ vindate dhruvam ..

2.25.d:
सहस्रशस्तु धर्मज्ञ दीर्घमाप्नोति जीवितम् ॥
हुत्वा दध्ना तथा पुत्रान्प्राप्नोति मनसेप्सितान् ॥ 51 ॥
गुग्गुलोः कणिकाभिस्तु सौभाग्यं विन्दते ध्रुवम् ॥
कृत्वाष्टपत्रं कमलं तन्मध्ये शशिनं लिखेत् ॥ 52 ॥
लवणेन ततस्तस्य पूजां कृत्वा यथाविधि ॥
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति मधुवातेति वै जपन् ॥53 ॥
जप्त्वा पुष्पवतीत्येवं मन्त्रं राम सहस्रशः ॥
देवतायै निवेद्यैव कुसुमानि शिवं भवेत् ॥ 54 ॥
जीमूतस्यैव भवति मन्त्रं जयकरं द्विज ॥
पयस्वतीति पयसा तथा हुत्वा सहस्रशः ॥ 55 ॥
ब्रह्मवर्चसमाप्नोति दध्ना वा भृगुनन्दन ॥
दधिक्राव्णेति हुत्वा तु पुत्रान्प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 56 ॥
तथा घृतवतीत्येतदायुष्यं स्याद् घृतेन तु ॥
बोधश्च मेति कथितं तथा स्वस्त्ययनं परम् ॥ 57 ॥
2.25.m:
thousands of times, O knower of dharma, he attains a long life. / Likewise, having offered with curd, he obtains sons desired in his mind.
With grains of bdellium he surely finds good fortune. / Having made an eight-petalled lotus, he should draw the moon in its centre.
Then, having worshipped it with salt according to rule / while chanting 'Madhu vātāḥ', he attains great good fortune.
Having chanted the mantra 'Puṣpavatī' thousands of times, O Rāma, / and offering flowers to the deity, auspiciousness will result.
The mantra "jīmūtasya" brings victory, O twice-born. / Likewise, having offered [oblations] a thousand times with milk, using "payasvatī",
or with curds, one attains the splendour of Brahman, O joy of the Bhṛgus. / And having offered with "dadhikrāvṇā", he obtains sons without a doubt.
Likewise, the [mantra] "ghṛtavatī" with clarified butter grants longevity. / "bodhaś ca me" has been declared as the supreme rite for welfare.

2.25.s:
svasti na indretyetaṃ ca sarvabādhāvināśanam ..
iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvamiti puṣṭivivardhanam .. 58 ..
sruveṇa devasya tveti hutvāpāmārgataṇḍulam ..

bahitvadanyadityetatkarma vyāhṛtivadbhavet ..
bhadrayante palāśasya samidbhiḥ kanakaṃ labhet ..2.125.60 ..
haṃsaḥ śuciṣadityetajjapaṃstoye'ghanāśanam ..

vasanteti ca hutvājyamādityāddhanamāpnuyāt ..

yāmyena iti caitacca taskarebhyo bhayāvaham ..
daṃṣṭrābhyāmiti caitacca vrīhibhirjuhuyānnaraḥ .. 64 ..
2.25.d:
स्वस्ति न इन्द्रेत्येतं च सर्वबाधाविनाशनम् ॥
इह गावः प्रजायध्वमिति पुष्टिविवर्धनम् ॥ 58 ॥
स्रुवेण देवस्य त्वेति हुत्वापामार्गतण्डुलम् ॥
मुच्यते विकृताच्छीघ्रमभिचारान्न संशयः ॥ 59 ॥
बहित्वदन्यदित्येतत्कर्म व्याहृतिवद्भवेत् ॥
भद्रयन्ते पलाशस्य समिद्भिः कनकं लभेत् ॥2.125.60 ॥
हंसः शुचिषदित्येतज्जपंस्तोयेऽघनाशनम् ॥
चत्वारि शृङ्गेत्येतच्च सर्वपापहरं जले ॥61 ॥
देव यज्ञेति जप्त्वा तु ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
जप्त्वा पितृभ्य इत्येतत्तृप्तिं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥ 62 ॥
वसन्तेति च हुत्वाज्यमादित्याद्धनमाप्नुयात् ॥
शिवो भवस्वाग्न्युत्पाते व्रीहिभिर्जुहुयान्नरः ॥ 63 ॥
याम्येन इति चैतच्च तस्करेभ्यो भयावहम् ॥
दंष्ट्राभ्यामिति चैतच्च व्रीहिभिर्जुहुयान्नरः ॥ 64 ॥
2.25.m:
And "svasti na indro" destroys all afflictions. / "iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam" promotes nourishment.
Having offered grains of apāmārga with a ladle using "devasya tvā", / he is quickly freed from distortion [caused by] black magic, there is no doubt.
The rite with "bahi te 'nyad" should be performed like the vyāhṛtis. / With kindling sticks of the palāśa tree using "bhadrayante", one obtains gold.
Muttering "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat" in water destroys sin; / and "catvāri śṛṅgā" in water removes all evil.
Having muttered "deva yajña", he is honoured in the world of Brahmā. / Having muttered "pitṛbhyaḥ", a man attains contentment.
And having offered clarified butter with "vasanta", he obtains wealth from the Sun. / When portents of fire appear, a man should offer with rice grains, [saying] "śivo bhava".
And "yāmyena" brings fear to thieves. / And with "daṃṣṭrābhyām", a man should offer with rice grains.

2.25.s:
yo asmabhyamarātīyānhutvā kṛṣṇatilairnaraḥ ..
sahasraśo'bhicārāttu mucyate vikṛtiṃ dvijaḥ .. 65 ..
annenānnapatetvetaddhutvā cānnamavāpnuyāt ..

etamevauṣadhīpāne sadā mantraṃ japeddvija ..

drupadā nāma sā devī yajurvede pratiṣṭhitā ..

2.25.d:
यो अस्मभ्यमरातीयान्हुत्वा कृष्णतिलैर्नरः ॥
सहस्रशोऽभिचारात्तु मुच्यते विकृतिं द्विजः ॥ 65 ॥
अन्नेनान्नपतेत्वेतद्धुत्वा चान्नमवाप्नुयात् ॥
सुपर्णोऽसीति दैत्यस्य कर्म व्याहृतिवद्भवेत् ॥ 66 ॥
मनः स्वतीति जप्त्वा च बन्धनान्मोक्षमाप्नुयात् ॥
रोपयेत वचां राजा चन्द्रे ग्रस्ते जलाशये ॥ 67 ॥
या ओषधय इत्येतज्जपंस्तामुद्धरेत्पुनः ॥
तिरात्रोपोषितः कूर्चां कृत्वा तां ताम्रभाजने ॥ 68 ॥
तेनैव मन्त्रितां चन्द्रं दृष्ट्वा मासं सदा जपेत् ॥
सकापिलघृतक्षीरे पीत्वा श्रुतिधरो भवेत् ॥ ॥ 69 ॥
एतमेवौषधीपाने सदा मन्त्रं जपेद्द्विज ॥
सिद्धा भवन्त्योषधयो मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रिताः ॥ 2.125.70 ॥
द्रुपदा नाम सा देवी यजुर्वेदे प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
अन्तर्जले त्रिरावृत्य मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥ 71 ॥
2.25.m:
Having offered with black sesame seeds a thousand times using "yo 'smabhyam arātīyān", / a twice-born is freed from black magic and distortion.
Having offered food with "annenānnapate", he obtains food. / The rite of the Daitya using "suparṇo 'si" should be performed like the vyāhṛtis.
And having muttered "manaḥsvatī", he obtains liberation from bondage. / When the moon is eclipsed, a king should plant vacā in a body of water;
muttering "yā oṣadhayaḥ", he should uproot it again. / Having fasted for three nights, making a brush of it in a copper vessel,
and consecrated with that very [mantra], looking at the moon, he should recite it constantly for a month. / Having drunk it with clarified butter and milk of a tawny cow, he becomes a bearer of the Veda.
When drinking this herbal preparation, O twice-born, he should constantly mutter this very mantra. / The herbs consecrated with this mantra become perfected.
She who is named Drupadā is established in the Yajurveda; / repeating it three times under water, one is freed from all sins.

2.25.d:
इह गावः प्रजायध्वं मन्त्रोऽयं पुष्टिवर्धनः ॥
हुतस्तु सर्पिषा दध्ना पयसा पायसेन वा ॥ 72 ॥
शतं व इति चैतेन हुत्वा पर्णफलानि वै ॥
आरोग्यं चिरमाप्नोति दीर्घमाप्नोति जीवितम् ॥ 73 ॥
ओषधीः प्रतिमोदध्वं जपेत्कर्मकवत्सदा ॥
लवने बीजवापे वा विशेषात्सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 74 ॥
सर्वौषधीः समानीय सर्वव्रीहियुतास्ततः ॥
क्षेत्रमध्ये द्विजो हुत्वा कृषिमाप्नोति पुष्टिदाम् ॥ 75 ॥
अपामार्गं यवं धान्यमोषधीरिति मातरः ॥
गोकामश्चाश्वकामो वा तं कामं शीघ्रमाप्नुयात् ॥ 76 ॥
ओषधीः समजन्तेति हुत्वा चाज्येन मानवः ॥
भयमाप्नोति नैवेह यातुधानभवं क्वचित् ॥ 77 ॥
ग्रन्थावतीति चैतेन पायसं जुहुयाद्द्विज ॥
सर्वत्र शान्तिमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 78 ॥
सीरां युञ्जति इत्येतद्धुत्वा कृषिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
उच्छुग्मा इति चैतेन बन्धनस्थो विमुच्यते ॥ 79 ॥
2.25.m:
This mantra "iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam" promotes nourishment / when offered with clarified butter, curds, milk, or pāyasa.
And having offered leaves and fruits with "śataṃ vaḥ", / he attains long-lasting health and achieves a long life.
One should constantly mutter "oṣadhīḥ pratimodadhvam" like a farmer; / especially at harvest or during sowing, one attains success.
Having brought all medicinal herbs together with all types of rice, / the twice-born, offering in the middle of the field, attains nourishing agriculture.
Offering apāmārga, barley, and grain with "oṣadhīr iti mātaraḥ", / one who desires cattle or horses quickly attains that desire.
And having offered clarified butter with "oṣadhīḥ samajanta", a man / never incurs any fear arising from Yātudhānas in this world.
And with "granthāvatī", a twice-born should offer pāyasa; / he attains pacification everywhere, there is no need to deliberate here.
Having offered with "sīrā yuñjanti", he obtains agriculture. / And with "ucchugmāḥ", one who is bound is set free.

2.25.d:
युवा सुवासा एतेन वासांस्याप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
यस्मिम्̐श्चापः स्थितः काष्ठे तद्गृहीत्वा विचक्षणः ॥ 2.125.80 ॥
सायं यक्ष्मेति मन्त्रेण शत्रोस्तु निखनेत्पदे ॥
कुष्ठी भवति चाषस्य पक्षं गृध्रस्य वा पुनः ॥ 81 ॥
सहस्रमन्त्रितं कृत्वा शत्रोः प्रतिकृतिं ततः ॥
तेन बद्ध्वा ततो मृत्युं शत्रुः प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 82 ॥
शत्रुं तु नाशयत्याशु सर्वातङ्कविनाशनम् ॥
प्रपतन्तीति च ऋचा जुहुयादोषधीर्द्विज ॥ 83 ॥
मिष्टान्नभागी भवति भाण्डानां चैव रक्षिता ॥
मा मा हिंसीति चाज्येन हुतं रिपुविनाशनम् ॥ 84 ॥
कान्तारमध्वरस्येति मधुसैन्धवसंयुताम् ॥
सौभाग्यकामो जुहुयात्स्त्रियो वा पुरुषस्य वा ॥ 85 ॥
होमो द्रप्सश्च स्कन्देति वश्यकामस्य शस्यते ॥
नमोस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति पायसं सघृतं नरः ॥ 86 ॥
2.25.m:
With "yuvā suvāsāḥ", he obtains clothes without a doubt. / Taking the piece of wood upon which water stood, a wise man,
with the mantra "sāyaṃ yakṣmā", should bury it in the enemy's footprint; / [the enemy] becomes afflicted with leprosy. Or again, with a feather of a blue jay or vulture,
having consecrated it a thousand times, then binding an image of the enemy / with it, the enemy attains death without a doubt.
It quickly destroys an enemy and destroys all illness. / With the verse "prapatanti", O twice-born, he should offer herbs.
He partakes of sweet food and becomes a guardian of vessels. / And offered with clarified butter, "mā mā hiṃsīḥ" destroys enemies.
With "kāntāram adhvarasya", one desiring good fortune should offer [oblations] / mixed with honey and rock-salt, for the sake of a woman or a man.
A burnt offering with "drapsaś ca skanda" is commended for one desiring subjugation. / With "namo 'stu sarpebhyaḥ", a man [offering] pāyasa with clarified butter,

अग्ने तिष्ठेति जुहुयाद्द्रव्याः खल्वभिचारकाः ॥

ग्रामे जनपदे वापि मरकं तु शमं नयेत् ॥ 89 ॥
रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगात्तथा दुःखात्तु दुःखितः ॥
औदुम्बर्यस्तु समिधो मधुमान्नो वनस्पतिः ॥ 2.125.90 ॥
हुत्वा सहस्रशो राम धनमाप्नोति मानवः ॥
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति व्यवहारे तथा जयम् ॥ 91 ॥
योगादिति तथा हुत्वा देवं वर्षापयेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
अपः पिबन्निति तथा हुत्वा दधिघृतं मधु ॥ 92 ॥
प्रवर्तयति धर्मज्ञ महावृष्टिमनन्तरम् ॥
अग्निर्देवतेति तथा यवमुष्ट्ययुतं द्विज ॥ 93 ॥
हुत्वा श्रद्धेयवाक्यस्तु सर्वत्रैवाभिजायते ॥
अयं पुरेति जुहुयादनुवाकेन मानवः ॥ 94 ॥
2.25.m:
should offer [saying] "nāgasthāna"; he obtains abundant gold. / "kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ" destroys black magic.
Substances used in black magic should indeed be offered with "agne tiṣṭha". / Having uttered the name of the enemy, he then brings the enemy under control.
Having offered ten thousand stalks of dūrvā grass with the mantra "kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt", / he puts an end to a pestilence in a village or country.
One afflicted with disease is freed from disease, and one suffering from grief [is freed] from grief. / Kindling sticks of udumbara wood [offered with] "madhumān no vanaspatiḥ",
having offered a thousand times, O Rāma, a man obtains wealth; / he attains great good fortune and likewise victory in legal disputes.
Having likewise offered with "yogāt", he certainly causes the rain-god to rain. / Likewise, having offered curds, clarified butter, and honey with "apaḥ piban",
O knower of dharma, he immediately brings about a great downpour. / Likewise with "agnir devatā", O twice-born, having offered ten thousand handfuls of barley,
his words become trustworthy everywhere. / A man should offer with the anuvāka "ayaṃ puraḥ",

घृतपूर्णानि पद्मानि सहस्रं भृगुनन्दन ॥
कन्यां तां समवाप्नोति यामसौ मनसेप्सति ॥ 95॥
श्रियमाप्नोति च तथा धनमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
नमस्ते रुद्र इत्येतत्सर्वोपद्रवनाशनम् ॥ 96 ॥
सर्वशान्तिकरं प्रोक्तं महापातकनाशनम् ॥
रक्षोघ्नं च यशस्यं च श्रीरायुःपुष्टिवर्धनम् ॥ 97 ॥
अभ्यवोचदित्यनेन रक्षा स्याद्व्याधितस्य तु ॥
सिद्धार्थकानां क्षेपेण पथि चैतत्सदा पठेत् ॥ 98 ॥
क्षेमेण स्वगृहानेति सर्वबाधाविवर्जितः ॥
असौ यस्ताम्र इत्येतत्पठेन्नित्यं दिवाकरम् ॥ 99 ॥
उपतिष्ठेत धर्मज्ञ सायंप्रातरतन्द्रितः ॥
अन्नमक्षय्यमाप्नोति दीर्घमायुश्च विन्दति ॥ 2.125.100 ॥
प्रमुञ्चन्तो न इत्येतत्षड्भिरायुधमन्त्रणम् ॥
रिपूणां भङ्गदं युद्धे नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 101 ॥
2.25.m:
a thousand lotuses filled with clarified butter, O joy of the Bhṛgus; / he attains that maiden whom he desires in his mind,
and likewise he attains prosperity and unsurpassable wealth. / "namas te rudra" destroys all calamities;
it is declared to bring all peace and destroy major sins; / it slays demons, bestows fame, and increases prosperity, life, and strength.
With "adhyavocat", protection is secured for a sick person / by throwing white mustard seeds, and on a journey one should always recite it.
He arrives safely at his own home, free from all afflictions. / One should daily recite "asau yas tāmraḥ" [facing] the sun.
One should worship [the sun] evening and morning without sloth, O knower of dharma; / one obtains inexhaustible food and attains long life.
With 'pramuñcanto naḥ', consecration of weapons with six [verses] / brings about the rout of enemies in battle; there should be no doubt about this.

2.25.d:
मानो महान्त इत्येतद्बालानां शान्तिकारकम् ॥
नमो हिरण्यबाहवे इत्यनुवाक् हर्षकारकम् ॥
राजिकां तिलतैलाक्तां जुहुयाच्छत्रुनाशनम् ॥ 102 ॥॥।
नमो वः किरिकेभ्यश्च पद्मलक्षे हुते नरः ॥
राजलक्ष्मीमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
बिल्वानां च तथा हुत्वा कनकं बहु विन्दति ॥1 03 ।
इमा रुद्रायेति तिलैः कृत्वा होमं विचक्षणः ॥
शीघ्रमेव महाभाग धनमाप्नोति चिन्तितम् ॥ 104 ॥
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण दूर्वाहोमेन मानवः ॥
सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो भयान्सर्वान्व्यपोहति ॥ 105 ॥
वरारोहेण इध्मानां याते रुद्रशिवा-तनूः ॥
हुत्वाऽयुतं तु धर्मज्ञं पुत्रमाप्नोत्यभीप्सितम् ॥ 106 ॥
असंख्याताः सहस्राणि मन्त्रैस्तदभिचारकम् ॥
नमोऽस्तु रुद्रेभ्य इति प्रोक्ता प्रत्यङ्गिरा परा ॥ 1 07॥
रक्तोष्णीषो रक्तवासा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥
अनेनैव श्मशाने तु लोहशङ्कुं नरोत्तम ॥1 08॥
2.25.m:
The verse 'mā no mahāntam' brings peace to children; / the anuvāka 'namo hiraṇyabāhave' brings joy. / One should offer black mustard smeared with sesame oil to destroy enemies.
When a hundred thousand lotuses are offered with 'namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ', a man / attains royal fortune; there should be no doubt about this. / Likewise, having offered [fruits] of bilva, he obtains abundant gold. / Having performed an oblation of sesame seeds with 'imā rudrāya', a wise man / quickly attains desired wealth, O fortunate one.
By this very mantra, through an oblation of dūrvā grass, a man / is freed from all diseases and wards off all fears.
With kindling-sticks of varāroha, having offered ten thousand [oblations] / with 'yā te rudra śivā tanūḥ', one obtains the desired son, O knower of dharma.
The mantras 'asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi' are for sorcery. / 'namo 'stu rudrebhyaḥ' is declared to be the supreme Pratyaṅgirā [mantra].
Wearing a red turban, red garments, red garlands, and red unguent, / with this very [mantra], in a cremation ground, O best of men,

प्रादेशमात्रं जुहुयात्सहस्रं भृगुनन्दन ॥
कृत्यामुत्थापयेज्जातां रक्तकुम्भेन पूजयेत् ॥1 09॥
पूर्णपात्रेण च तथा सर्वकर्मकरो भवेत ॥
आशुः शिशान इत्येतदायुधानां च रक्षणम् ॥2.125.110॥
संग्रामे कथितं राम सर्वशत्रुविनाशनम् ॥
इमं सोममित्येतन्नदीं गत्वा समुद्रगाम् ॥ 111 ॥
स्नातस्तोयेऽयुतं जप्त्वा हुत्वा दशशतं ततः ॥
साष्टं मनुजशार्दूल ग्राममाप्नोत्यभीप्सितम् ॥112॥
वाजश्च मेति जुहुयात्सहस्रं पञ्चभिर्द्विज ॥
आज्याहुतीनां धर्मज्ञ चक्षुरोगाद्विमुच्यते ॥ 113 ॥
मनोभवस्वेति गृहे तथा हुत्वा विचक्षणः ॥
वास्तुदोषांस्ततः सर्वान्क्षिप्रमेव व्यपोहति ॥ 114 ॥
अग्न आयूंषि चैतेन हुत्वेवाज्यमतन्द्रितः ॥
सहस्रशस्तु धर्मज्ञ वशं नाप्नोति केनचित्॥115॥
अपाम्फेनेति लाजाभिर्हुताभिर्जयमाप्नुयात् ॥
भद्रा इतीन्द्रियैर्हीनो जपन्स्यात्सकलेन्द्रियः ॥ 116 ॥
2.25.m:
one should offer an iron spike measuring a span a thousand times, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / One raises an arisen Kṛtyā, and should worship her with a red jar
and likewise with a full vessel; she becomes the doer of all deeds. / 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ' is for the protection of weapons.
In battle, O Rāma, it is taught to destroy all enemies. / With 'imaṃ somam', having gone to a river flowing to the sea,
having bathed in the water and recited it ten thousand times, then having offered a thousand and eight [oblations], / one attains the desired village, O tiger among men.
With 'vājaś ca me', a twice-born should offer a thousand oblations of ghee / with five [verses], O knower of dharma; he is freed from eye disease.
Likewise, having offered [oblations] in the house with 'manobhavasva', the wise man / then quickly removes all architectural defects of the site.
And with this 'agne āyūṃṣi', having offered ghee without sloth / a thousand times, O knower of dharma, one never comes under anyone's subjugation.
With 'apām phenena', by offering parched grain, one attains victory. / One who is deprived of sense organs, reciting 'bhadrāḥ', becomes possessed of all sense organs.

2.25.d:
अग्निश्च पृथिवी चेति वशीकरणमुत्तमम् ॥
अध्वनीति जपन्मन्त्रं व्यवहारे जयी भवेत् ॥ 117 ॥
ब्रह्मराजभ्यामिति च कर्मारम्भेषु वै जपेत् ॥
सर्वेषु सर्वधर्मज्ञ तेषां सिद्धिमुपाश्नुते ॥ 118 ॥
नूनपादोसुर इति न्यग्रोधे द्विजसत्तम ॥
अशोकपुष्पान्सघृताञ्जुहुयाल्लक्षसंमितान् ॥119 ॥
ततो दानवकन्यां तु स्वयमेवेह पश्यति ॥
अनुवाकस्य शेषेण तस्यान्नं विनिवेदयेत् ॥ 2.125.120 ॥
ददाति सा ततो रुक्मं तूष्णीं तत्रेच्छया भवेत् ॥
अनुगच्छेत्ततस्तूष्णीं पाणौ सङ्गृह्य सा नरम् ॥ 121 ॥
बिलं प्रवेशयेद्राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
शून्यायतनमासाद्य माषमिश्रमथौदनम् ॥ 122 ॥
कया नश्चित्र इत्येतज्जपंस्तु जुहुयान्नरः ॥
हुते शतसहस्रे तु तस्य विद्याधरः स्वकाम् ॥ 123 ॥
सुवर्णराशिं धर्मज्ञ शीघ्रमेव प्रयच्छति ॥
संवत्सरोशीत्यनया घृतं हुत्वा विचक्षणः ॥ 124 ॥
2.25.m:
'agniś ca pṛthivī ca' is supreme subjugation. / Reciting the mantra 'adhvani', one becomes victorious in legal affairs.
And one should recite 'brahmarājābhyām' at the commencement of deeds; / in all of them, O knower of all dharma, one attains their success.
With 'nū na pāt [asuro]', under a banyan tree, O best of twice-born, / one should offer a hundred thousand aśoka flowers mixed with ghee.
Then one sees a daughter of the Dānavas right there with one's own eyes. / With the remainder of the anuvāka, one should present food to her.
Then she gives gold; one should remain silent there at will. / Then, taking the man by the hand, she silently follows him;
she leads him into a cave, O Rāma; there should be no doubt about this. / Having approached an abandoned shrine, [offering] boiled rice mixed with māṣa beans,
a man reciting and offering with 'kayā naś citraḥ'— / when a hundred thousand [oblations] are offered, a Vidyādhara
quickly gives him his own heap of gold, O knower of dharma. / With 'saṃvatsaro 'si', a wise man having offered ghee,

2.25.d:
यावज्जीवमरोगी स्याल्लक्षहोमेन पण्डितः ॥
केतुं कृण्वन्नित्येतत्संग्रामे जयवर्धनम् ॥125॥
ऐन्द्राग्नं वर्म इत्येतद्रणे सन्नाहबन्धनम् ॥
धननागेति मन्त्रश्च धनुर्ग्रहणिकः परः ॥ 126 ॥
वक्ष्यन्तीति तथा मन्त्रो विज्ञेयो ज्याभिमन्त्रणे ॥
मन्त्रश्चाहिरिवेत्येतत्तृणमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 127 ॥
युञ्जतीति तथाश्वानां योजने मन्त्र उच्यते ॥
आशुः शिशान इत्येतद्गात्रालम्भनमुच्यते ॥ 128 ॥
विष्णोः क्रमेण मन्त्रश्च रथारोहणिकः परः ॥
आजंघन्तीति चाश्वानां ताडनीय उदाहृतः ॥ 129 ॥
यः सेना अभीत्वरीति परसैन्यमुखो जपेत् ॥
डुण्डुभ इति वाप्येतड् डुण्डुभीताडने भवेत् ॥2.125.130 ॥
एतैः पूर्वहुतैर्मन्त्रैः कृत्वैवं विजयो भवेत् ॥
यमेन दत्तमित्यस्य कोटिहोमाद्विचक्षणः ॥ 131 ॥
2.25.m:
a learned man becomes free from disease for as long as he lives by a hundred thousand oblations. / 'ketuṃ kṛṇvan' increases victory in battle.
'aindrāgnaṃ varma' is for binding armor in battle. / And the mantra 'dhanvanāgā' is supreme for taking up the bow.
The mantra 'vakṣyantī' is to be known for consecrating the bowstring. / And the mantra 'ahir iva' is declared to be the mantra for the archer's arm-guard.
Likewise, 'yuñjanti' is called the mantra for yoking the horses. / 'āśuḥ śiśānaḥ' is said to be for touching the limbs [of the chariot].
And the mantra 'viṣṇoḥ krameṇa' is supreme for mounting the chariot. / 'ājaṅghanti' is taught for striking the horses.
Facing the enemy's army, one should recite 'yāḥ senā abhītvarīḥ'. / Or this 'ḍuṇḍubhaḥ' is for striking the kettle-drum.
With these mantras offered beforehand, victory is achieved in this way. / From ten million oblations of this 'yamena dattam', a wise man

2.25.d:
रथमुत्पादयेच्छ्रीघ्रं संग्रामे विजयप्रदम् ॥
आकृष्णेति तथैतस्य कर्म व्याहतिवद्भवेत् ॥ 132 ॥
युवं च्यवानमेतच्च भयेषु भयनाशनम् ॥
घृताहुतिसहस्रेण नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥133॥
मित्रं हुवेत इत्येतन्मेधाकामस्य शस्यते ॥
स राज इति चैतेन देवताराधनं नरः ॥ 134 ॥
कुयाद्भार्गव सर्वत्र होमजप्यैर्यथेप्सितम् ॥
शिवसङ्कल्पजप्येन समाधिं मनसो लभेत्॥135॥
पञ्च नद्य इत्यनेन पद्मलक्षं घृताप्लुतम्॥
हुत्वा शीघ्रमवाप्नोति श्रियं ते पद्ममालिनीम् ॥136॥
उभावपि त इत्येतद्रूपकामस्य शस्यते ॥
यदाबध्नन्दाक्षायणा मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितम् ॥137 ॥
सहस्रकृत्वः कनकं धारयेद्रिपुनाशनम्॥
गुह्यकानां च सर्वेषां तथा निर्वहणं परम् ॥ 138 ॥
इमं जीवेभ्य इति च सीतालोष्टं चतुर्दिशम् ॥
क्षिपेद्गृहे तदा तस्य न स्याच्चोरभयं निशि ॥ 139 ॥
2.25.m:
quickly produces a chariot that bestows victory in battle. / And the rite of 'ā kṛṣṇena' is like that of the Vyāhṛtis.
'yuvaṃ cyavānam' destroys danger in times of danger / through a thousand oblations of ghee; there should be no doubt about this.
'mitraṃ huve' is commended for one desiring intelligence. / And with 'sa rājā', a man performs the propitiation of deities,
O Bhārgava, everywhere according to desire through homas and recitations. / By recitation of the Śivasaṅkalpa [hymn], one attains concentration of the mind.
Having offered a hundred thousand lotuses steeped in ghee with 'pañca nadyaḥ', / one quickly obtains royal fortune wearing a lotus garland.
'ubhāv api te' is commended for one desiring beauty. / With 'yad ābadhnan dākṣāyaṇāḥ', consecrated by this mantra,
one should wear gold [consecrated] a thousand times; it destroys enemies / and is the supreme defense against all Guhyakas.
And with 'imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ', one should throw clods from a furrow in all four directions / of the house; then there is no fear of thieves at night.

2.25.d:
परी मे गामनेषतेति वशीकरणमुत्तमम् ॥
हर्तुमप्यागतस्तस्य वशीभवति मानवः॥2.125.140॥
भक्ष्यताम्बूलपुष्पाद्यं मन्त्रितं तु प्रयच्छति ॥
यस्य धर्मस्य वशगः सोऽस्य शीघ्रं भविष्यति ॥ 141 ॥
शन्नोमिति त इत्येतत्सदा सर्वत्र शान्तिदम् ॥
मनसः काममाकूतिः पुष्टिकामस्य शस्यते ॥ 142 ॥
चमषट्कं च धर्मज्ञ सर्वकामकरं स्मृतम् ॥
षट्केन च तथा होमः सर्वदेवप्रसादनः ॥ 143 ॥
औदार्येणोदकं स्पृष्ट्वा तद्दोषाद्विप्रमुच्यते ॥
विवृतं चैतदाज्येन हुतं शूलापहं भवेत् ॥ 144 ॥
गणानां त्वा गणपतिं होम कृत्वा चतुष्पथे ॥
वशे कुर्याज्जगत्सर्वं सर्वधान्यैरसंशयम् ॥ 145 ॥
वैकङ्कतेध्महोमे च समास्त्वाग्न इतीत्यपि ॥
यशसा योगमाप्नोति विपुलं नात्र संशयः ॥ 146 ॥
2.25.m:
'parīme gām aneṣata' is supreme subjugation. / A man, even if come to plunder, comes under his power.
One gives edible things, betel, flowers, and the like, consecrated [with it]; / whomever one seeks to subject to one's purpose, that person will quickly become subservient.
'śaṃ no mit [raḥ]' brings peace always and everywhere. / 'manasaḥ kāmam ākūtim' is commended for one desiring prosperity.
The Camaka six [sections], O knower of dharma, are taught to fulfill all desires. / And oblation with the six propitiates all gods.
Having touched water with generosity, one is freed from that fault. / And this [homa] performed with clarified butter, uncovered, removes colic.
Having performed a homa at a crossroads with the verse “Gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatim” / using all kinds of grain, one surely brings the whole world under one's control.
And when offering a homa with firewood of Vikāṅkata wood with the verse “Samās tvāgne,” / one attains immense glory; there is no doubt about this.

2.25.d:
अग्निर्मूर्धेतिमन्त्रेण हुत्वैवाज्यं हुताशने ॥
तत्प्रसादमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥147॥
एवं हि देवतालिङ्गैस्तथा राम यथा स्वकैः ॥
हुतैः प्रसादयेदिष्टां देवतां नात्र सशयः ॥ 148 ॥
हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयो मन्त्रोऽयमभिषेचने ॥
शन्न आपश्च धन्वन्याः सर्वपापहराः स्मृताः ॥ 149 ॥
शन्नो देवीरभिष्टये चेति शान्तिकरः परः ॥
एकचक्रेति मन्त्रेण हुतेनाज्येन भार्गव ॥ 2.125.150 ॥
ग्रहेभ्यः शीघ्रमाप्नोति प्रसादं नात्र संशयः ॥
याज्यानुवाकौ वृक्षाणां समाग्ने वर्च इत्यपि॥151॥
तत्प्रसादमवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
गावो भग इति द्वाभ्यां हुत्वैवाज्यं सहस्रशः ॥ 152 ॥
गाः समाप्नोति धर्मज्ञ नात्त्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
उदुत्तमं वरुण इति जुहुयाद्भृगुनन्दन ॥ 153 ॥
2.25.m:
Having offered clarified butter into the fire with the mantra “Agnir mūrdhā,” / one obtains his grace; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus, indeed, through the marks of the deities, O Rāma, according to their respective [mantras], / one should propitiate the chosen deity by means of oblations; there is no doubt about this.
The mantra “Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ” is traditionally used for consecration, / and “Śan na āpaś ca dhanvanyāḥ” is regarded as removing all sins.
The verse “Śan no devīr abhiṣṭaye” is supremely pacifying. / By offering clarified butter with the mantra “Ekacakra,” O Bhārgava,
one swiftly receives grace from the planets; there is no doubt about this. / With the two offering verses for trees, and likewise “Samāgne varcaḥ,”
one obtains their grace; no doubt should be entertained here. / Having offered clarified butter thousands of times with the two [mantras beginning] “Gāvo bhagaḥ,”
one obtains cows, O knower of dharma; no doubt should be entertained here. / One should offer with “Ud uttamaṃ varuṇa,” O delight of the Bhṛgus,

2.25.d:
नदीवाहतडागेषु सुकृतेषु द्विजोत्तम ॥
संवदत्तां हिरण्यकोशं रूपं कृत्वा तथैव च ॥ 154॥
प्रवादसां सेति चैव गृहे यज्ञो विधीयते ॥
देवेभ्यो वनस्पत इति ब्रह्मयज्ञो विधीयते॥155॥
रात्रीयख्य इति द्वाभ्यां रात्रियज्ञाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
शमे शमीकं शम्याकामश्वत्थं प्लक्षमेव च॥156॥
उदुम्बरं च न्यग्रोधमपामार्गं च गोमयम्॥
यां कुर्याद्दर्भपिंजूलां दूर्वां प्राचीनगामिनीम् ॥157॥
सीतां लोष्टं सुवर्णं च तथा वल्मीकमृत्तिकाम् ॥
सं वः सृजामीति द्वाभ्यां बीजान्यप्सु विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ 158 ॥
या ओषधय इत्येतदनुवाकं ततो जपेत् ॥
अपामिवेद्विति ततः प्रोक्षणं तु विधीयते॥159॥
इन्नोभयमितीत्येतच्चाष्टर्चं जुहुयाद्द्विजः ॥
यद्देवा देवहेडनमृचस्तिस्रस्तथैव च ॥ 2.125.160 ॥ ।
2.25.m:
at rivers, streams, and ponds, when they are well-constructed, O best of the twice-born. / Likewise, having formed a shape [with the mantra] “Saṃvadattāṃ hiraṇyakośam,”
a sacrifice is prescribed in the house with “Pravādasāṃ sā.” / The sacrifice to Brahman is prescribed with “Devebhyo vanaspate.”
The night-sacrifices are proclaimed with the two [mantras] called Rātrīya. / In a pacification [ritual]: śamī, śamyāka, aśvattha, and plakṣa,
udumbara, nyagrodha, apāmārga, and cow dung. / One should make a tuft of darbha grass and eastward-spreading dūrvā grass,
furrow-earth, a clod, gold, and also ant-hill clay. / With the two verses “Saṃ vaḥ sṛjāmi,” one should cast seeds into the waters.
Then one should recite the anuvāka “Yā oṣadhayaḥ.” / After that, sprinkling is prescribed with “Apām ivedu.”
A twice-born should offer the eight-verse hymn “Inno bhayam,” / and likewise the three verses “Yad devā devaheḍanam.”
