2.25.d:
हुत्वा सम्प्रोक्षणं कुर्याद्भूयः सर्वत्र मानवः ॥
सर्वोत्पातप्रशमनं कर्मैतत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 161 ॥
गायत्री वैष्णवी ज्ञेया तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
सर्वपापप्रशमनी सर्वकर्मकरी तथा ॥ 162 ॥
एतावदुक्तं यजुषां विधानं मया हि किञ्चित्तव धर्मनिष्ठ ॥
अतः परं वच्मि नृवीर साम्नां तन्मे शृणुष्वायतलोहिताक्ष ॥163 ॥
2.25.m:
Having offered, a man should once again perform sprinkling everywhere. / This rite is proclaimed to pacify all portents.
The Vaiṣṇavī Gāyatrī is known to be “Tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam”; / it pacifies all sins and accomplishes all rites.
This much of the procedure of Yajur[-veda mantras] has been briefly declared by me to you, O you who are devoted to dharma. / Beyond this, I shall speak of the Sāmans, O hero among men; listen to that from me, O you with wide, reddish eyes.

2.26.s:
2.126
puṣkara uvāca ..
saṃhitāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ japtvā viṣṇuṃ prīṇāti mānavaḥ ..
sarvakāmamavāpnoti tathā hutvā ca bhārgava ..1..
2.26.d:
2.126
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
संहितां वैष्णवीं जप्त्वा विष्णुं प्रीणाति मानवः ॥
सर्वकाममवाप्नोति तथा हुत्वा च भार्गव ॥1॥
2.26.m: Puṣkara said: / Having recited the Vaiṣṇavī Saṃhitā, a man pleases Viṣṇu; / and having offered oblations [with it], O Bhārgava, he attains all desires.

2.26.s:
skandasya saṃhitāṃ japtvā skandātkāmānupāśnute ..
āsyadaghne jale tiṣṭhannaghenākīrṇamānasaḥ ..2 ..
2.26.d:
स्कन्दस्य संहितां जप्त्वा स्कन्दात्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥
आस्यदघ्ने जले तिष्ठन्नघेनाकीर्णमानसः ॥2 ॥
2.26.m: Having recited the Saṃhitā of Skanda, one attains desires from Skanda. / Standing in neck-deep water, with his mind overwhelmed by sin,

2.26.s:
triḥsaptakṛtvo japtvā ca sarvānkāmānupāśnute .. ..
tathā ca saṃhitāṃ pitryāṃ tatprasādamupāśnute .. 3 ..
2.26.d:
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो जप्त्वा च सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥ ॥
तथा च संहितां पित्र्यां तत्प्रसादमुपाश्नुते ॥ 3 ॥
2.26.m: and having recited it thrice-seven times, one attains all desires. / And likewise, [having recited] the ancestral Saṃhitā, he obtains their favor.

2.26.s:
gurugobrāhmaṇādīnāmuktvā nāma priyaṃ naraḥ ..
sopavāso japettoye tvidaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame .. 4 ..
2.26.d:
गुरुगोब्राह्मणादीनामुक्त्वा नाम प्रियं नरः ॥
सोपवासो जपेत्तोये त्विदं विष्णुर्विचक्रमे ॥ 4 ॥
2.26.m: Having uttered the dear name of his guru, cows, brahmins, and others, / a man, fasting, should recite in the water: “Idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame.”

2.26.s:
sadā gāvaśca śucayaḥ prayājyayajane japet ..
amedhyadarśane jāpoḥ panthā ame divaḥ .. 5 ..
2.26.d:
सदा गावश्च शुचयः प्रयाज्ययजने जपेत् ॥
अमेध्यदर्शने जापोः पन्था अमे दिवः ॥ 5 ॥
2.26.m: At an animal sacrifice, one should always recite: “Gāvaś ca śucayaḥ.” / Upon seeing something impure, the recitation is: “Panthā ame divaḥ.”

2.26.s:
etadindrastavāmīti sarvapāpaharaṃ japet ..
śukraṃ te'nyadyajataṃ japtvā steyādvimucyate .. 6 ..
2.26.d:
एतदिन्द्रस्तवामीति सर्वपापहरं जपेत् ॥
शुक्रं तेऽन्यद्यजतं जप्त्वा स्तेयाद्विमुच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
2.26.m: One should recite this “Indrastavāmīti,” which removes all sins. / Having recited “Śukraṃ te 'nyad yajatam,” one is freed from [the guilt of] theft.

2.26.s:
cakrāniti tathā japtvā pārayāyī vimucyate ..
sahantaḥ somamityetajjaptvā mucyetpratigrahāt .. 7 ..
2.26.d:
चक्रानिति तथा जप्त्वा पारयायी विमुच्यते ॥
सहन्तः सोममित्येतज्जप्त्वा मुच्येत्प्रतिग्रहात् ॥ 7 ॥
2.26.m: Having recited “Cakrān,” one is freed from transgressions of order. / Having recited “Sahantaḥ somam,” one is freed from [the fault of] accepting improper gifts.

2.26.s:
yattatsoma indra iti hiṃsādoṣavināśanam ..
agnerbhayātpramucyeta agnistigmeti vai japan .. 8 ..
2.26.d:
यत्तत्सोम इन्द्र इति हिंसादोषविनाशनम् ॥
अग्नेर्भयात्प्रमुच्येत अग्निस्तिग्मेति वै जपन् ॥ 8 ॥
2.26.m: “Yat tat soma indraḥ” destroys the fault of injury. / One is freed from the fear of fire by reciting “Agniḥ stigmena.”

2.26.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ jñeyaṃ parito ṣiñcatāmiti ..
parvāsusometi japejjīvituṃ tu sukarmaṇā .. 9 ..
2.26.d:
सर्वपापहरं ज्ञेयं परितो षिञ्चतामिति ॥
पर्वासुसोमेति जपेज्जीवितुं तु सुकर्मणा ॥ 9 ॥
2.26.m: The verse “Parito ṣiñcatām” should be known as removing all sins. / One should recite “Parvāsu soma” in order to live by good deeds.

2.26.s:
avikreyaṃ ca vikreyaṃ japedghṛtavatītviti ..
apyānī devasavito jñeyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam .. 2.126.10 ..
2.26.d:
अविक्रेयं च विक्रेयं जपेद्घृतवतीत्विति ॥
अप्यानी देवसवितो ज्ञेयं दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् ॥ 2.126.10 ॥
2.26.m: Whether for what is not to be sold or what is to be sold, one should recite “Ghṛtavatī tu.” / “Apyānī deva savitar” is known to destroy bad dreams.

2.26.s:
trātāramindramityeva mahi trīṇāmavostviti ..
uduttamaṃ varuṇapāśetyāyuṣyāṇi japetsadā .. 11 ..
2.26.d:
त्रातारमिन्द्रमित्येव महि त्रीणामवोस्त्विति ॥
उदुत्तमं वरुणपाशेत्यायुष्याणि जपेत्सदा ॥ 11 ॥
2.26.m: One should constantly recite the longevity-granting verses: “Trātāram indram,” / “Mahi trīṇām avostu,” and “Ud uttamaṃ varuṇapāśam.”

2.26.s:
śukracandreti jāpyena pūto bhavati mānavaḥ ..
śuddhāśuddhīyametacca taṃ vacosūktameva ca .. 12 ..
2.26.d:
शुक्रचन्द्रेति जाप्येन पूतो भवति मानवः ॥
शुद्धाशुद्धीयमेतच्च तं वचोसूक्तमेव च ॥ 12 ॥
2.26.m: A man becomes purified by the recitation “Śukracandra.” / And this Śuddhāśuddhīya [sāman] and the Taṃvaco hymn [also purify].

2.26.s:
nyagrodhaśṛṅgamādāya śaramūlaṃ tathaiva ca ..
trivṛtaṃ tu maṇiṃ kṛtvā juhuyācca sahasraśaḥ .. 13 ..
2.26.d:
न्यग्रोधशृङ्गमादाय शरमूलं तथैव च ॥
त्रिवृतं तु मणिं कृत्वा जुहुयाच्च सहस्रशः ॥ 13 ॥
2.26.m: Taking a shoot of nyagrodha and the root of śara grass, / and fashioning a threefold amulet, one should make offerings thousands of times,

2.26.s:
bodhyāsiriti mantreṇa ghṛtaṃ rāma yathāvidhi ..
abhyajya ghṛtaśeṣeṇa mekhalābandha iṣyate .. 14 ..
2.26.d:
बोध्यासिरिति मन्त्रेण घृतं राम यथाविधि ॥
अभ्यज्य घृतशेषेण मेखलाबन्ध इष्यते ॥ 14 ॥
2.26.m: with the mantra “Bodhyāsir,” offering clarified butter according to rule, O Rāma. / Having anointed it with the residue of clarified butter, tying a girdle is prescribed.

2.26.s:
strīṇāṃ yāsāṃ tu garbhāṇi patanti bhṛgusattama ..
vaṇigjātasya bālasya badhnīyāttadanantaram .. 15 ..
2.26.d:
स्त्रीणां यासां तु गर्भाणि पतन्ति भृगुसत्तम ॥
वणिग्जातस्य बालस्य बध्नीयात्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.26.m: For women whose embryos miscarry, O best of the Bhṛgus, / and for a child born of a merchant, one should tie it thereafter.

2.26.s:
gorvai svarūpavatsāyāḥ śuklāyā juhuyādghṛtam ..
ugrapriyā tu śaraṇaṃ maṃtreṇānena mantravit .. 16 ..
2.26.d:
गोर्वै स्वरूपवत्सायाः शुक्लाया जुहुयाद्घृतम् ॥
उग्रप्रिया तु शरणं मंत्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ॥ 16 ॥
2.26.m: One who knows mantras should offer clarified butter from a white cow / whose calf is identical in colour, with this mantra: “Ugrapriyā tu śaraṇam.”

2.26.s:
rakṣasā mucyate janturmaṇiṃ śirasi dhārayet ..
kautsyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tu prāśnīyānnityameva vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 17 ..
2.26.d:
रक्षसा मुच्यते जन्तुर्मणिं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥
कौत्स्यं घृतं तु प्राश्नीयान्नित्यमेव विचक्षणः ॥ 17 ॥
2.26.m: A creature is freed from a rākṣasa; he should wear the amulet on his head. / A wise man should constantly consume Kautsa clarified butter.

2.26.s:
viśvāpṛtanniti mantreṇa vyādhibhirvipramucyate ..
carṣaṇīvṛtametena ghṛtaṃ hutvā yathāvidhi .. 18 ..
2.26.d:
विश्वापृतन्निति मन्त्रेण व्याधिभिर्विप्रमुच्यते ॥
चर्षणीवृतमेतेन घृतं हुत्वा यथाविधि ॥ 18 ॥
2.26.m: With the mantra “Viśvā pṛtanāḥ,” one is freed from diseases. / Having offered clarified butter according to rule with this “Carṣaṇīvṛtam,”

2.26.s:
śatāyārimaṇiṃ baddhvā na sarpaiḥ paribhūyate ..
samatyāyantīti japenna mriyeta pipāsayā .. 19 ..
2.26.d:
शतायारिमणिं बद्ध्वा न सर्पैः परिभूयते ॥
समत्यायन्तीति जपेन्न म्रियेत पिपासया ॥ 19 ॥
2.26.m: and having bound a hundred-lifespan-warding amulet, one is not overcome by serpents. / Reciting “Samatyāyanti,” one will not die of thirst.

2.26.s:
iṣṭyāhotritayaṃ japtvā salile nāpnuyādbhayam ..
tvamemā oṣadhītvetajjaptvā vyādhiṃ na cāpnuyāt .. 2.126.20 ..
2.26.d:
इष्ट्याहोत्रितयं जप्त्वा सलिले नाप्नुयाद्भयम् ॥
त्वमेमा ओषधीत्वेतज्जप्त्वा व्याधिं न चाप्नुयात् ॥ 2.126.20 ॥
2.26.m: Having recited the three Iṣṭyāhotṛ [verses], one experiences no fear in water. / Having recited “Tvam emā oṣadhīḥ,” one is not afflicted by disease.

2.26.s:
yatte payāṃsi pūrveṇa grāsaṃ vai prakṣipenmukhe ..
nigireduttareṇaitannityamārogyamāpnuyāt .. 21 ..
2.26.d:
यत्ते पयांसि पूर्वेण ग्रासं वै प्रक्षिपेन्मुखे ॥
निगिरेदुत्तरेणैतन्नित्यमारोग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥ 21 ॥
2.26.m: With the first [verse of] “Yat te payāṃsi,” one should put a morsel into the mouth; / with the subsequent one, he should swallow it; he will attain constant health.

2.26.s:
devavratena hutvājyamuccheṣeṇa vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
karavīrakamabhyajya daṇḍahastagatena tu .. 22 ..
2.26.d:
देवव्रतेन हुत्वाज्यमुच्छेषेण विचक्षणः ॥
करवीरकमभ्यज्य दण्डहस्तगतेन तु ॥ 22 ॥
2.26.m: Having offered clarified butter with the Devavrata [mantra], a wise man, with the residue / having anointed a karavīraka [staff] held in his hand with a staff,

2.26.s:
svastimāṃstena bhavati yatra kvacana gacchati ..
pathi devavrataṃ japtvā bhayebhyo vipramucyate .. 23 ..
2.26.d:
स्वस्तिमांस्तेन भवति यत्र क्वचन गच्छति ॥
पथि देवव्रतं जप्त्वा भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ॥ 23 ॥
2.26.m: becomes prosperous wherever he goes. / Having recited the Devavrata on the road, one is freed from fears.

2.26.s:
yadindro anayatveti hutaṃ saubhāgyavardhanam ..
bhadrānno agniriti ca dantakāṣṭhaṃ ca bhakṣayet .. 24 ..
2.26.d:
यदिन्द्रो अनयत्वेति हुतं सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥
भद्रान्नो अग्निरिति च दन्तकाष्ठं च भक्षयेत् ॥ 24 ॥
2.26.m: An oblation made with "May Indra bring [it] here" increases good fortune. / And one should chew a tooth-stick with "Agni from the auspicious."

2.26.s:
saṃvatsaramaniṣṭhīvanmadhvājyasahitaṃ sadā ..
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti yatra kvacana gacchati .. 25 ..
2.26.d:
संवत्सरमनिष्ठीवन्मध्वाज्यसहितं सदा ॥
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति यत्र क्वचन गच्छति ॥ 25 ॥
2.26.m: Always accompanied by honey and clarified butter, not spitting for a year, / one obtains great good fortune wherever one goes.

2.26.s:
bhago na citra etena netrayorañjanaṃ smṛtam ..
saubhāgyavardhanaṃ rāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 26 ..
2.26.d:
भगो न चित्र एतेन नेत्रयोरञ्जनं स्मृतम् ॥
सौभाग्यवर्धनं राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 26 ॥
2.26.m: With "Bhaga not wondrous," collyrium for the eyes is prescribed; / it increases good fortune, O Rāma, of this there is no doubt.

2.26.s:
japannindreti vargaṃ ca tathā saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
karipriyo divaḥ kaviḥ kāmyāṃ saṃśrāvayetstriyam .. 27 ..
2.26.d:
जपन्निन्द्रेति वर्गं च तथा सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
करिप्रियो दिवः कविः काम्यां संश्रावयेत्स्त्रियम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.26.m: And repeating the group of verses beginning with "Indra," one obtains good fortune in the same way. / An elephant-loving poet of heaven should cause a desired woman to hear it;

2.26.s:
sā taṃ kāmayate rāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
rathantaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ brahmavarcasavardhanam .. 28 ..
2.26.d:
सा तं कामयते राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
रथन्तरं वामदेव्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसवर्धनम् ॥ 28 ॥
2.26.m: she will love him, O Rāma, of this there is no doubt. / The Rathantara and Vāmadevya [sāmans] increase spiritual lustre.

2.26.s:
yaśasāmeti juhuyātpuṣpeṇa tu priyaṅgukam ..
yaśasā yogamāpnoti karmaṇānena mānavaḥ .. 29 ..
2.26.d:
यशसामेति जुहुयात्पुष्पेण तु प्रियङ्गुकम् ॥
यशसा योगमाप्नोति कर्मणानेन मानवः ॥ 29 ॥
2.26.m: One should offer priyaṅgu with a flower [chanting] "Of fame"; / through this rite a man attains union with fame.

2.26.s:
prāśayedbālakaṃ nityaṃ vacācūrṇaṃ ghṛtāplutam ..
indramidgāthinaṃ japtvā bhavecchrutidharastvasau .. 2.126.30 ..
2.26.d:
प्राशयेद्बालकं नित्यं वचाचूर्णं घृताप्लुतम् ॥
इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनं जप्त्वा भवेच्छ्रुतिधरस्त्वसौ ॥ 2.126.30 ॥
2.26.m: One should daily feed a boy powdered calamus immersed in clarified butter / after chanting "Indra indeed, the singer"; he will become one who retains what he hears.

2.26.s:
hutvā rathantaraṃ japtvā putramāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
gīrvāṇaḥ pāhi satataṃ japtaṃ syādaghatārakam .. 31 ..
2.26.d:
हुत्वा रथन्तरं जप्त्वा पुत्रमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
गीर्वाणः पाहि सततं जप्तं स्यादघतारकम् ॥ 31 ॥
2.26.m: Having offered oblations while chanting the Rathantara, one undoubtedly obtains a son. / "O deity, protect always" recited delivers from sin.

2.26.s:
mayi śrīriti mantreṇa japtavyaṃ śrīvivardhanam ..
dānāviśati devo'pi mantreṇānena dharmavit .. 32 ..
2.26.d:
मयि श्रीरिति मन्त्रेण जप्तव्यं श्रीविवर्धनम् ॥
दानाविशति देवोऽपि मन्त्रेणानेन धर्मवित् ॥ 32 ॥
2.26.m: "In me be glory" is the mantra to be recited for increasing prosperity. / Through this mantra even a god, knower of dharma, enters into gifts.

2.26.s:
krītvā ghṛtaṃ tu puṣpeṇa suṣumāṇītyataḥ pibet ..
alakṣmīnāśanaṃ karma mayaitatte prakīrtitam .. 33 ..
2.26.d:
क्रीत्वा घृतं तु पुष्पेण सुषुमाणीत्यतः पिबेत् ॥
अलक्ष्मीनाशनं कर्म मयैतत्ते प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 33 ॥
2.26.m: Having bought clarified butter with a flower, one should then drink it [reciting] "Suṣumāṇi." / This rite destroying misfortune has been proclaimed by me to you.

2.26.s:
puṣpeṇa sarṣapāngaurāṃścūrṇayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
indrehimatsyaṃ dharmeti kuryādutsādanaṃ budhaḥ .. 34 ..
2.26.d:
पुष्पेण सर्षपान्गौरांश्चूर्णयित्वा विचक्षणः ॥
इन्द्रेहिमत्स्यं धर्मेति कुर्यादुत्सादनं बुधः ॥ 34 ॥
2.26.m: A wise man, having crushed white mustard seeds with a flower, / should perform anointment, O wise one, with "Indra, come fish, dharma."

2.26.s:
ghṛtasnānaṃ budhaḥ kṛtvā sarṣapāñjuhuyāttataḥ ..
adyetvīḍāvindriyeti mantreṇānena mantritam .. 35 ..
2.26.d:
घृतस्नानं बुधः कृत्वा सर्षपाञ्जुहुयात्ततः ॥
अद्येत्वीडाविन्द्रियेति मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.26.m: The wise man, having bathed in clarified butter, should then offer mustard seeds / consecrated with this mantra: "Today let Iḍā, through the sense-power."

2.26.s:
puṣṭidaṃ karma kathitaṃ mayaitattava bhārgava ..
miśrānvrīhi yavānagnau hutvā bhṛgukulodbhava .. 36 ..
2.26.d:
पुष्टिदं कर्म कथितं मयैतत्तव भार्गव ॥
मिश्रान्व्रीहि यवानग्नौ हुत्वा भृगुकुलोद्भव ॥ 36 ॥
2.26.m: This rite bestowing nourishment has been declared by me to you, O Bhārgava. / Having offered mixed rice and barley into the fire, O scion of the Bhṛgu race,

2.26.s:
munīśo dhāma etena dhānyabhāgī bhavetsadā ..
madhvājyadadhimiśrāṇi viprāṇīti juhoti yaḥ .. 37 ..
2.26.d:
मुनीशो धाम एतेन धान्यभागी भवेत्सदा ॥
मध्वाज्यदधिमिश्राणि विप्राणीति जुहोति यः ॥ 37 ॥
2.26.m: with "The lord of sages, the abode," he will always be a possessor of grain. / He who offers [substances] mixed with honey, clarified butter, and curd [reciting] "The sages,"

2.26.s:
sāṣṭaṃ sahasraṃ dharmajña śrāvayantīha mānavāḥ ..
māsopavāsī labhate kanakaṃ bahu bhārgava .. 38 ..
2.26.d:
साष्टं सहस्रं धर्मज्ञ श्रावयन्तीह मानवाः ॥
मासोपवासी लभते कनकं बहु भार्गव ॥ 38 ॥
2.26.m: a thousand and eight times, O knower of dharma—men proclaim this here— / fasting for a month, obtains much gold, O Bhārgava.

2.26.s:
gavyeṣuṇeti ca dvābhyāṃ yastu saṃvatsaraṃ naraḥ ..
nyagrodhajapaniṣṭhīvaṃ bhakṣayeddantadhāvanam .. 39 ..
2.26.d:
गव्येषुणेति च द्वाभ्यां यस्तु संवत्सरं नरः ॥
न्यग्रोधजपनिष्ठीवं भक्षयेद्दन्तधावनम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.26.m: The man who, for a year, with the two [mantras] beginning with "With the bovine wish," / chews a banyan tooth-stick, reciting it without spitting,

2.26.s:
sahasrasaṅkhyaṃ sa dhanaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
bhadro na agna ityetattathā hutvā sahasraśaḥ .. 2.126.40 ..
2.26.d:
सहस्रसङ्ख्यं स धनं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
भद्रो न अग्न इत्येतत्तथा हुत्वा सहस्रशः ॥ 2.126.40 ॥
2.26.m: obtains wealth numbered in the thousands, there is no doubt here. / Likewise, having offered [oblations] by the thousands with "Auspicious to us, O Agni,"

2.26.s:
audumbaredhmahomena mantreṇānena gāṃ labhet ..
hutvā vrīhiyavānagnau dhānyamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 41 ..
2.26.d:
औदुम्बरेध्महोमेन मन्त्रेणानेन गां लभेत् ॥
हुत्वा व्रीहियवानग्नौ धान्यमाप्नोति मानवः ॥ 41 ॥
2.26.m: through an oblation with kindling of udumbara wood, with this mantra he obtains a cow. / Having offered rice and barley into the fire, a man obtains grain.

2.26.s:
evāsi vīreyuriti dvādaśāhamupoṣitaḥ ..
sarpiṣā tvayutaṃ hutvā grāmamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 42 ..
2.26.d:
एवासि वीरेयुरिति द्वादशाहमुपोषितः ॥
सर्पिषा त्वयुतं हुत्वा ग्राममाप्नोति मानवः ॥ 42 ॥
2.26.m: Having fasted for twelve days [chanting] "Thus you are heroically," / and having offered ten thousand [oblations] of clarified butter, a man obtains a village.

2.26.s:
vairūpāṣṭakavannityaṃ prayuñjānaḥ śriyaṃ labhet ..
śrāntāṣṭakaṃ prayuñjānaḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 43 ..
2.26.d:
वैरूपाष्टकवन्नित्यं प्रयुञ्जानः श्रियं लभेत् ॥
श्रान्ताष्टकं प्रयुञ्जानः सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥ 43 ॥
2.26.m: Constantly employing [the mantra] like the Vairūpa octet, one obtains prosperity. / Employing the Śrānta octet, one attains all desires.

2.26.s:
gavyeṣuṇeti yo nityaṃ sāyaṃ prātaratandritaḥ ..
upasthānaṃ gavāṃ kuryāttasya syustāḥ sadā gṛhe .. 44 ..
2.26.d:
गव्येषुणेति यो नित्यं सायं प्रातरतन्द्रितः ॥
उपस्थानं गवां कुर्यात्तस्य स्युस्ताः सदा गृहे ॥ 44 ॥
2.26.m: He who constantly, evening and morning, unwearied, attends upon cows / with "With the bovine wish," they will always remain in his house.

2.26.s:
agne vivasvaduṣasā mantreṇānena mantravit ..
bhājanasyopanītasya yastvagraṃ juhuyātsadā .. 45 ..
2.26.d:
अग्ने विवस्वदुषसा मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ॥
भाजनस्योपनीतस्य यस्त्वग्रं जुहुयात्सदा ॥ 45 ॥
2.26.m: With this mantra, "O Agni, radiant with the dawn," the knower of mantras / who always offers the top portion of the vessel brought forward,

2.26.s:
uttareṇa baliṃ dattvā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
kṣīraikavṛkṣamāsādya maṇibhadrāya mānavaḥ .. 46 ..
2.26.d:
उत्तरेण बलिं दत्त्वा सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
क्षीरैकवृक्षमासाद्य मणिभद्राय मानवः ॥ 46 ॥
2.26.m: and gives an offering with the subsequent [verse], attains all desires. / A man, having approached a solitary milk-tree, for Maṇibhadra,

2.26.s:
aṣṭarātroṣitaḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā dadyāttato balim ..
susaṃskṛtena māṃsena kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ kṣapedbudhaḥ .. 47 ..
2.26.d:
अष्टरात्रोषितः पूजां कृत्वा दद्यात्ततो बलिम् ॥
सुसंस्कृतेन मांसेन कृष्णपक्षं क्षपेद्बुधः ॥ 47 ॥
2.26.m: having fasted for eight nights, having performed worship, should then offer an oblation. / With well-prepared meat, the wise man should pass the dark fortnight.

2.26.s:
eṣasyateti madhumannindra etena bhārgava ..
suvarṇamāpnoti naro yāvadicchati śatruhan .. 48 ..
2.26.d:
एषस्यतेति मधुमन्निन्द्र एतेन भार्गव ॥
सुवर्णमाप्नोति नरो यावदिच्छति शत्रुहन् ॥ 48 ॥
2.26.m: With "He speeds," [and] "O sweet Indra," with this, O Bhārgava, / a man obtains gold as much as he desires, O slayer of foes.

2.26.s:
śuklapakṣacaturdaśyāṃ trirātropoṣito naraḥ ..
maunaṃ māsaṃ pāyasaṃ ca rasatraya samanvitam .. 49 ..
2.26.d:
शुक्लपक्षचतुर्दश्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितो नरः ॥
मौनं मासं पायसं च रसत्रय समन्वितम् ॥ 49 ॥
2.26.m: On the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, a man who has fasted for three nights, / in silence, for a month, [offers] milk-rice endowed with the three essences;

2.26.s:
saptadhenavo duduhurmantreṇānena mantravit ..
kṛṣṇapakṣacaturdaśyāṃ trirātropoṣitastathā .. 2.126.50 ..
2.26.d:
सप्तधेनवो दुदुहुर्मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ॥
कृष्णपक्षचतुर्दश्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितस्तथा ॥ 2.126.50 ॥
2.26.m: the knower of mantras, with the mantra "Seven milk-cows milked," / and likewise having fasted for three nights on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,

2.26.s:
matsyānupaharedrātrāvāsurīmāpnuyācchriyam ..
balayuktaśca bhavati dīptatejāstathaiva ca .. 21 ..
2.26.d:
मत्स्यानुपहरेद्रात्रावासुरीमाप्नुयाच्छ्रियम् ॥
बलयुक्तश्च भवति दीप्ततेजास्तथैव च ॥ 21 ॥
2.26.m: should offer fishes at night; he obtains demonic prosperity, / and he becomes endowed with strength and likewise with radiant splendor.

2.26.s:
dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇaṃ mantreṇānena pāyasam ..
hutvā digaṣṭake dadyāddikpālānāṃ tato balim .. 52 ..
2.26.d:
धानावन्तं करम्भिणं मन्त्रेणानेन पायसम् ॥
हुत्वा दिगष्टके दद्याद्दिक्पालानां ततो बलिम् ॥ 52 ॥
2.26.m: Having offered milk-rice with this mantra, "Possessing grain, possessing porridge," / he should then present an oblation to the guardians of the directions in the eight directions.

2.26.s:
vāstudoṣaharaṃ karma mayaitatparikīrtitam ..
rājā samācaretsnānaṃ puṣyeṇa śravaṇena ca .. 53 ..
2.26.d:
वास्तुदोषहरं कर्म मयैतत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥
राजा समाचरेत्स्नानं पुष्येण श्रवणेन च ॥ 53 ॥
2.26.m: This rite removing defects of the dwelling has been proclaimed by me. / A king should perform a bath under Puṣya and under Śravaṇa;

2.26.s:
āprātṛvya iti sadā rahasyaṃ snānamācaret ..
svecchāpatitajīvantīgavāṃ śṛṅgasamudbhavaiḥ .. 54 ..
2.26.d:
आप्रातृव्य इति सदा रहस्यं स्नानमाचरेत् ॥
स्वेच्छापतितजीवन्तीगवां शृङ्गसमुद्भवैः ॥ 54 ॥
2.26.m: with "O rival," he should constantly perform a secret bath / with the horn-receptacles of living cows that have fallen naturally,

2.26.s:
kāśairmadhvājyasampūrṇairdadhikṣīrayutaistathā ..
niḥsapatnamavāpnoti rājyaṃ nirgatakaṇṭakam .. 55 ..
2.26.d:
काशैर्मध्वाज्यसम्पूर्णैर्दधिक्षीरयुतैस्तथा ॥
निःसपत्नमवाप्नोति राज्यं निर्गतकण्टकम् ॥ 55 ॥
2.26.m: which are filled with honey and clarified butter and endowed with curd and milk; / he attains a kingdom without rivals and free from thorns.

2.26.s:
ghṛtāktaṃ tu yavadroṇaṃ vāta āvatabheṣajam ..
anena hutvā vidhivatsarvāndoṣānvyapohati ..56..
2.26.d:
घृताक्तं तु यवद्रोणं वात आवतभेषजम् ॥
अनेन हुत्वा विधिवत्सर्वान्दोषान्व्यपोहति ॥56॥
2.26.m: A droṇa of barley anointed with clarified butter, with "O wind, blow medicine"— / having offered this according to rule, he dispels all defects.

2.26.s:
prādevo dāsa etena kṛṣṇānhutvā tathā tilān ..
kṛtvā karmāṇi tīrthodaiḥ stainyātkṣipraṃ vimucyate ..57 ..
2.26.d:
प्रादेवो दास एतेन कृष्णान्हुत्वा तथा तिलान् ॥
कृत्वा कर्माणि तीर्थोदैः स्तैन्यात्क्षिप्रं विमुच्यते ॥57 ॥
2.26.m: With this [mantra], "The god is a servant," having offered black sesame seeds / and performed rites with waters of sacred fords, he is quickly released from theft.

2.26.s:
abhi tvā pūrvapītaṃ ye vaṣaṭkārasamanvitam ..
bādhakedhmasahasraṃ tu hutaṃ yuddhe jayapradam .. 58 ..
2.26.d:
अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतं ये वषट्कारसमन्वितम् ॥
बाधकेध्मसहस्रं तु हुतं युद्धे जयप्रदम् ॥ 58 ॥
2.26.m: With "Unto you, drunk of old," accompanied by the exclamation vaṣaṭ, / a thousand kindling sticks of bādhaka offered grant victory in battle.

2.26.s:
hastyaśvapuruṣānkuryādbudhaḥ piṣṭamayāñchubhān ..
parakīyānathoddiśya pradhānapuruṣām̐stathā .. 59..
2.26.d:
हस्त्यश्वपुरुषान्कुर्याद्बुधः पिष्टमयाञ्छुभान् ॥
परकीयानथोद्दिश्य प्रधानपुरुषाम्̐स्तथा ॥ 59॥
2.26.m: The wise man should make auspicious figures of elephants, horses, and men out of flour, / and then designating the enemy's leading men,

2.26.s:
svastyannāpiṣṭapacane kṣureṇotkṛtya bhāgaśaḥ ..
abhitvā śūra no numo mantreṇānena mantravit .. 2.126.60 ..
2.26.d:
स्वस्त्यन्नापिष्टपचने क्षुरेणोत्कृत्य भागशः ॥
अभित्वा शूर नो नुमो मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् ॥ 2.126.60 ॥
2.26.m: cutting them up piece by piece with a blade on the flour-baking pan of the meal of blessing, / the knower of mantras, with this mantra, "Unto you, O hero, we praise,"

2.26.s:
kṛtvā sarṣapatailāktānkrodhena juhuyāttataḥ ..
etatkṛtvā budhaḥ karma saṃgrāme jayamāpnuyāt .. 61 ..
2.26.d:
कृत्वा सर्षपतैलाक्तान्क्रोधेन जुहुयात्ततः ॥
एतत्कृत्वा बुधः कर्म संग्रामे जयमाप्नुयात् ॥ 61 ॥
2.26.m: having smeared them with mustard oil, should then offer them with wrath. / Having performed this rite, the wise man attains victory in battle.

2.26.s:
āṣāḍhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu sopavāso vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
sāyaṃ dhānyāni vastrāṇi sasyāni tolayeda budhaḥ ..62 ..
2.26.d:
आषाढ्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु सोपवासो विचक्षणः ॥
सायं धान्यानि वस्त्राणि सस्यानि तोलयेद बुधः ॥62 ॥
2.26.m: On the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, the skilled one, having fasted, / in the evening, the wise man should weigh grains, garments, and crops.

2.26.s:
idhmamiddevatāmanne mantreṇāmantrayettu tām ..
pūjitāṃ vāsayedrātrau deśe paramapūjite .. 63 ..
2.26.d:
इध्ममिद्देवतामन्ने मन्त्रेणामन्त्रयेत्तु ताम् ॥
पूजितां वासयेद्रात्रौ देशे परमपूजिते ॥ 63 ॥
2.26.m: He should consecrate that deity with the mantra "The kindling indeed in food"; / worshipped, he should lodge it at night in a most revered place.

2.26.s:
deśānāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ tathā devacatuṣpadām ..
mṛnmayānāṃ tu kartavyaṃ tathā rātryādhivāsanam .. 64 ..
2.26.d:
देशानां भूमिपालानां तथा देवचतुष्पदाम् ॥
मृन्मयानां तु कर्तव्यं तथा रात्र्याधिवासनम् ॥ 64 ॥
2.26.m: A night-consecration of clay [images] representing realms, / earth-rulers, gods, and quadrupeds should likewise be performed.

2.26.s:
tulitānāṃ dvitīyehni tattadvṛddhi pravardhane ..
hīnasya kṣayamādeśyaṃ samasya samatā tathā..65..
2.26.d:
तुलितानां द्वितीयेह्नि तत्तद्वृद्धि प्रवर्धने ॥
हीनस्य क्षयमादेश्यं समस्य समता तथा॥65॥
2.26.m: Of those weighed, on the second day, [any] increase indicates prosperity; / of that which has decreased, decay is to be predicted; of that which is equal, stability likewise.

2.26.s:
govrataṃ tu budhaḥ kuryādādau māsacatuṣṭayam ..
tatastvaraṇyaṃ praviśettatra kuryājjapaṃ śubham ..66..
2.26.d:
गोव्रतं तु बुधः कुर्यादादौ मासचतुष्टयम् ॥
ततस्त्वरण्यं प्रविशेत्तत्र कुर्याज्जपं शुभम् ॥66॥
2.26.m: The wise man should first perform the vow of the cow for four months; / then he should enter the forest, and there he should perform auspicious recitation.

2.26.s:
tapaḥ sadṛśamāsādya jāptvaitaditi vai sadā ..
sahasrakṛtvastu japetsaptarātratraye gate..67..
2.26.d:
तपः सदृशमासाद्य जाप्त्वैतदिति वै सदा ॥
सहस्रकृत्वस्तु जपेत्सप्तरात्रत्रये गते॥67॥
2.26.m: Having attained a penance suited to it, constantly reciting "Having recited this," / he should recite it a thousand times when three periods of seven nights have passed.

2.26.s:
manasā kāṃkṣitānkāmāndhruvamāpnoti mānavaḥ..
antarikṣeṇa vā yāti rūpānyatvaṃ karoti vā ..68..
2.26.d:
मनसा कांक्षितान्कामान्ध्रुवमाप्नोति मानवः॥
अन्तरिक्षेण वा याति रूपान्यत्वं करोति वा ॥68॥
2.26.m: A man surely obtains the desires wished for in his mind; / or he travels through the atmosphere, or changes his form.

2.26.s:
adṛśyatvamavāpnoti daityatvamatha vā punaḥ ..
taṃtaṃ kāmamavāpnoti yaṃyaṃ vā manasecchati ..69..
2.26.d:
अदृश्यत्वमवाप्नोति दैत्यत्वमथ वा पुनः ॥
तंतं काममवाप्नोति यंयं वा मनसेच्छति ॥69॥
2.26.m: He attains invisibility, or indeed daitya-hood; / he attains whatever desire he wishes in his mind.

2.26.s:
sāmnastu devatāṃ jñātvā tena sāmnā tu devatām ..
ārādhayetsuprasannā sāmnā syātsaṃśayaṃ vinā..2.126.70..
2.26.d:
साम्नस्तु देवतां ज्ञात्वा तेन साम्ना तु देवताम् ॥
आराधयेत्सुप्रसन्ना साम्ना स्यात्संशयं विना॥2.126.70॥
2.26.m: Knowing the deity of the sāman, he should worship the deity with that sāman; / pleased by the sāman, she becomes well-disposed without a doubt.

2.26.s:
amūṣu pūrvaṃ tu sadā mantramāvartayecchuciḥ ..
candanenānuliptāṃgo jātipuṣpadharastathā .. 71 ..
2.26.d:
अमूषु पूर्वं तु सदा मन्त्रमावर्तयेच्छुचिः ॥
चन्दनेनानुलिप्तांगो जातिपुष्पधरस्तथा ॥ 71 ॥
2.26.m: Being pure, one should always recite the mantra beforehand on these [occasions], / his limbs anointed with sandalwood and wearing jasmine flowers,

2.26.s:
śvetoṣṇīṣaḥ śvetavāsāḥ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
evaṃ duduhaketyetatsopavāsastu yo japet .. 72 ..
2.26.d:

2.127
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शान्तातीतं गणं हुत्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति मानवः ॥
भैषज्यं च गणं हुत्वा सर्वान्रोगानपोहति ॥ 1 ॥
त्रिषस्तीयं गणं हुत्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
क्वचिन्नाप्नोति च भयं हुत्वा चैवाभयं गणम् ॥ 2 ॥
न क्वचिज्जायते राम गणं हुत्वा पराजयः ॥
आयुष्यं च गणं हुत्वा चापमृत्यून्व्यपोहति॥3॥
एते दशगुणाश्चैव होतव्याः स्युर्यथाक्रमम् ॥
अष्टादशसु धर्मज्ञ दशशान्तिषु भार्गव ॥ 4 ॥
वैष्णवी च तथा चैन्द्री ब्राह्मी रौद्री तथैव च ॥
वायव्या वारुणी चैव कौबेरी भार्गवी तथा ॥ 5 ॥
प्राजापत्या तथा त्वाष्ट्री कौमारी वह्निदेवता ॥
मारुद्गणी च गान्धारी शान्तिर्वै रुदती तथा॥6॥
2.26.m:
The ritual rule of the sāmans, an effective worker of acts, has been told to you in brief by me, O hero among men; / learn that of the Atharvan which I speak, having concentrated your mind, O person of noble soul.
Puṣkara said: / Having offered the Śāntātīta hymn-group, a person obtains peace; / and having offered the Bhaiṣajya hymn-group, he dispels all diseases.
Having offered the Triṣaṣtīya hymn-group, he is released from all sins; / and having offered the Abhaya hymn-group, he encounters no fear anywhere.
No defeat occurs anywhere, O Rāma, after offering the [Aparājita] hymn-group; / and having offered the Āyuṣya hymn-group, he dispels untimely deaths.
These should be offered tenfold in regular order, / O knower of dharma, descendant of Bhṛgu, in the eighteen peace rites and the ten peace rites:
Vaiṣṇavī and Aindrī, Brāhmī and Raudrī, / Vāyavyā, Vāruṇī, Kauberī, and Bhārgavī,
Prājāpatyā, Tvāṣṭrī, Kaumārī, Vahnidevatā, / Mārudgaṇī, Gāndhārī, Rudatī peace rite,

2.26.d:
शान्तिरांगिरसी याम्या पार्थिवी च भृगूत्तम ॥
एतास्तु शान्तयः प्रोक्ताः सर्वकर्महिताः सदा ॥ 7 ॥
यस्त्वामृत्युरितीत्येतज्जप्तं मृत्युविनाशनम् ॥
हुत्वा च मातृनामानि कामानेवमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 8 ॥
सुपर्णस्त्विति हुत्वा च भुजगैर्नैव बाध्यते ॥
यस्येदं भूमिमिति च भूमिकामो जपेत्सदा ॥ 9 ॥
पृथिव्यामुत्तमोसीति हुतं श्रैष्ठ्यप्रदं सदा ॥
औदुम्बरं यो न इति तथा वीर्यविवर्धनम् ॥ 2.127.10 ॥
इन्द्रेण दत्तमित्येतत्सर्वबाधाविनाशनम् ॥
हिरण्यवर्ण इति च स्नानं पापहरं भवेत् ॥ 11 ॥
असितस्येति सर्वाणि विषघ्नानि भृगूत्तम ॥
सारस्वतीति मन्त्रांश्च विषघ्नान्निर्विशेद्बुधः ॥12 ॥
शरभादीनि सर्वाणि पिशाचक्षपणानि च ॥
यमस्य लोकादित्येतद्दुःस्वप्नशमनं परम् ॥ 13 ॥
अग्नेर्व इति चाप्येतत्कथितं मन्युनाशनम् ॥
ऊर्ध्वो भवति विज्ञेयः कृत्वा स्थानकरः परः॥14॥
2.26.m:
the peace rite Āṅgirasī, Yāmyā, and Pārthivī, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / these peace rites are declared to be always beneficial for all actions.
This mantra 'yastvā mṛtyuḥ…', recited, destroys death; / and having offered with the names of the Mothers, one obtains desires in this manner.
Having offered with 'suparṇaḥ…', he is not troubled by serpents; / and one desiring land should always recite 'yasyedaṃ bhūmiḥ…'.
Offered with 'pṛthivyām uttamo 'si', it always bestows supremacy; / likewise, with 'audumbaraṃ yo naḥ', it increases vigor.
The mantra 'indreṇa dattam…' destroys all afflictions; / and bathing with 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ…' removes sin.
All the verses beginning with 'asitasya…' destroy poison, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / a wise man should employ the mantras beginning with 'sārasvatī…' as poison-destroying.
All those beginning with 'śarabha…' destroy piśācas; / this mantra 'yamasya lokāt…' is supreme for pacifying bad dreams.
'agner vaḥ' is also taught as destroying anger; / one should know that performing [rites with] 'ūrdhvo bhavati' is supreme, securing high station.

2.26.d:
इन्द्रं वयं वणिजमिति पण्यलाभकरं परम् ॥
कामो मे राज्ञीति हुतं स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनम्॥15॥
भद्राय कर्णमित्येतत्कर्णप्रस्यन्दने जपेत् ॥
भद्रासाक्षिवधे जाता कर्णप्रस्यन्दने तथा ॥ 16 ॥
तुभ्यमेवाजिरिति आयुष्यं तु हुतं भवेत् ॥
आयातु पितमित्येतन्मित्रलब्धिकरं हुतम् ॥ 17 ॥
आशासानमिदं जना मिश्रधान्येन होमयेत् ॥
आधिपत्यमवाप्नोति सर्वत्र मनुजोत्तम ॥18॥
अग्निरीशेभिरित्येतद्गवां वृद्धिकरं परम् ॥
द्वादशाहं तु जुहुयात्पराकेण विशेषतः ॥ 19 ॥
शातो हविरितीत्येतद्ग्रामस्वास्थ्यकरं भवेत् ॥
तस्माद्ग्रामान्मृदा कृत्वा वेदिसाम्यं समश्नुते ॥ 2.127.20 ॥
विधाय स्वेति सर्वाणि राष्ट्रस्वीकरणानि तु ॥
त्रिभ्यो भद्रेभ्य इत्येतद्वास्तोष्पतमुदाहृतम् ॥ 21 ॥
ध्रुवं ध्रुवेणेति हुतं स्थानलाभकरं भवेत् ॥
अच्युतापोस्तथा राम कथितं स्थानलाभदम् ॥22 ॥
2.26.m:
The mantra 'indraṃ vayaṃ vaṇijam…' brings supreme gain of merchandise; / offering with 'kāmo me rājñī…' increases the good fortune of women.
One should recite this 'bhadrāya karṇam…' for an ear discharge; / also 'bhadrāsākṣivadhe jātā…' for an ear discharge.
Offered with 'tubhyamevājir…', it bestows long life; / this offered with 'āyātu pītam…' brings the gaining of friends.
One should offer 'āśāsānam idaṃ janāḥ' into the fire with mixed grains; / thereby one attains sovereignty everywhere, O best of men.
This mantra 'agnirīśebhiḥ…' is supreme for increasing cattle; / one should offer it for twelve days, especially with the parāka penance.
This mantra 'śāto haviḥ…' brings well-being to a village; / having made a likeness of the altar with earth from that village, one obtains it.
All those beginning with 'vidhāya sva…' are for winning a kingdom; / this mantra 'tribhyo bhadrebhyaḥ…' is proclaimed as relating to Vāstoṣpati.
Offered with 'dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa…', it brings the gain of a position; / likewise 'acyutāpaḥ…', O Rāma, is declared to grant the gain of a position.

2.26.d:
पयो देवेष्विति हुतं रायस्पोषकरं परम् ॥
युनक्त सीरेति शुना कृषिलाभकरं भवेत् ॥ 23 ॥
अयं ते योनिरित्येतत्पुत्रलाभकरं भवेत् ॥
शुने वत्सा तथा ह्येतद्गवां वृद्धिकरं हुतम् ॥ 24 ॥
॥॥॥ मेति कथितं सर्वत्र श्रैष्ठ्यकारकम् ॥
यदग्न इति चाप्येतद्बन्धनान्मोक्षकारकम् ॥ 25 ॥
यो न स्व इति चाप्येतच्छत्रुनाशकरं परम् ॥
सवन्नहन्निति तथा नात्र कार्या विचारणा॥26॥
( त्वमत्वममितीत्येतद्यशसो वर्धनं परम् ॥
यथा वृषिमितीत्येतत्स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥ ॥ 27 ॥
आनो अग्न इत्येतच्च कथितं पतिलाभदम् ॥
येन वेहेति मां चैव गर्भलाभकरं भवेत् ॥ 28 ॥
इमं तपस्विन्निति तथा भवेत्सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥
यत्पृथिव्यामनावृत्तं हुतमेतद्यथाविधि ॥29 ॥
कृत्वा तु संशनं ज्ञेयं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
॥॥॥॥॥॥.2.127.30॥।)
2.26.m:
Offered with 'payo deveṣu…', it brings supreme increase of wealth; / 'yunakta sīrā…' with a ploughshare brings the gain of agriculture.
This mantra 'ayaṃ te yoniḥ…' brings the gain of a son; / and this offered with 'śune vatsā…' increases cattle.
The mantra '[…] mā…' is declared to produce pre-eminence everywhere; / and this 'yadagna…' brings release from bondage.
And this 'yo naḥ svaḥ…' is supreme for destroying enemies; / likewise 'savannahann…', no doubt should be entertained here.
This mantra 'tvamatvamam…' is the supreme increaser of fame; / this mantra 'yathā vṛṣim…' increases the good fortune of women.
And this 'ā no agna…' is declared to grant a husband; / and 'yena vā…' brings the obtaining of an embryo.
Likewise 'imaṃ tapasvin…' increases good fortune; / this mantra 'yatpṛthivyāmanāvṛttam…', offered according to rule,
having performed, should be known as pacification; no doubt should be entertained here. / […]

2.26.d:
शिवं शिवाभिरित्येतद्भवेच्छ्रेयस्करं परम् ॥
दूत्या दूषणमित्येतत्कृत्यादूषणमुच्यते ॥ 31 ॥
बृहस्पतिः परिपातु पथि स्वस्त्ययनं भवेत् ॥
मनो विवन्न भयदं पथि स्वस्त्ययनं भवेत् ॥ 32 ॥
अयन्नो अग्निरध्यक्षो भवेदग्निप्रसादतः ॥
संवत्सरं तु शिरसा धारयेद्यो हुताशनम् ॥ 33 ॥'
मन्त्रमेतज्जपेन्नित्यमाग्नेयाशामुखः स्थितः ॥
अनग्निज्वलनं कुर्याद्रामसंवत्सरे गते॥34॥
दूत्या दूतिरसीत्येतज्जपेन्मन्त्रमनुत्तमम् ॥
कुर्यात्प्रदिसराबन्धं सर्वदोषनिबर्हणम्॥35॥
प्राणसूक्तञ्च कथितं तथा प्राणविवर्धनम् ॥
मुञ्चामि त्वेति कथितमपमृत्युविमोक्षणम् ॥36॥
अथर्वशिरसोऽध्येता सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
परमं पावनं तद्धि सर्वकल्मषनाशनम्॥37॥
एवमेते शुभा मन्त्राः प्रतिवेदं मया तव ॥
समासात्कथिता राम समुद्धृत्य प्रधानतः ॥ 38 ॥
2.26.m:
This mantra 'śivaṃ śivābhiḥ…' brings supreme welfare; / this 'dūtyā dūṣaṇam…' is called the destroyer of black magic.
The mantra 'bṛhaspatiḥ paripātu…' provides an auspicious journey on the road; / 'mano vivat…' giving no fear provides an auspicious journey on the road.
The mantra 'ayaṃ no agniradhyakṣaḥ…' succeeds through the favour of Agni; / he who carries fire upon his head for a year,
should constantly recite this mantra, facing towards the south-eastern direction; / he can ignite fire without fuel, O Rāma, when a year has passed.
One should recite this unsurpassed mantra: 'dūtyā dūtirasī…'; / he should tie an amulet, which destroys all defects.
The Prāṇasūkta is taught as increasing life-force; / 'muñcāmi tvā' is taught as liberation from untimely death.
A student of the Atharvaśiras is freed from all sins; / for that is supremely purifying and the destroyer of all impurities.
Thus these auspicious mantras have been related to you by me for each Veda, / in summary, O Rāma, by extracting the principal ones.

कथिता भृगुशार्दूल पुराणैः सुमहात्मभिः ॥ 39 ॥
न ते शक्या महाभाग वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ॥

आज्यञ्च व्रीहयश्चैव तथा वै गौरसर्षपाः ॥ 42 ॥
अक्षतानि तिलाश्चैव दधि क्षीरञ्च भार्गव ॥
दर्भास्तथैव दूर्वाश्च बिल्वानि कमलानि च ॥ 43 ॥
शान्तिपुष्टिकराण्याहुर्द्रव्याण्येतानि भार्गव ॥
तैलेन्धनानि धर्मज्ञ राजिकां रुधिरं विषम् ॥ 44 ॥
समिधः कण्टकोपेता अभिचारेषु योजयेत् ॥
आर्षं वै दैवतं छन्दस्त्वविज्ञाय भृगूत्तम ॥ ॥ 45 ॥
2.26.m:
And the applications of each single mantra in their thousands / have been proclaimed, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, by the ancient high-souled sages.
They cannot be spoken, O fortunate one, even in hundreds of years; / nevertheless, through the pre-eminent mantras, some rituals have been taught to you.
Where no material for fire-oblation was specified by me to you previously, / I shall tell you the oblation materials for that; listen to me speak them.
Sacrificial firewood of sacrificial trees is the primary oblation material, / along with clarified butter, rice grains, and white mustard seeds;
Unbroken rice grains, sesame seeds, curds, and milk, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / darbha grass, dūrvā grass, bilva fruits, and lotuses,
they declare these substances to produce peace and prosperity, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Oil, firewood, O knower of dharma, mustard seeds, blood, and poison
One should employ thorny firewood in malevolent rites. / O foremost of the Bhṛgus, without knowing the seer, deity, and meter,

मन्त्रस्य तेन मन्त्रेण जप्यहोमौ न कारयेत् ॥
छन्दसि ब्राह्मणे सूक्ते यदव्यक्तं प्रदृश्यते ॥ 46 ॥
विद्वद्भि सह निश्चित्य तद्यज्ञमवतारयेत् ॥
सम्भारा ये यथा यत्र यानि द्रव्याणि यो विधिः ॥ 47 ॥
शाखां प्रति तथा तत्र तत्प्रमाणमिति स्थितिः ॥
यः स्वसूत्रमतिक्रम्य परसूत्रेण वर्तते ॥ 48 ॥
अप्रमाणमृषिं कृत्वा सोऽप्यधमेण युज्यते ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन स्वसूत्त्रं न विलंघयेत् ॥ 49 ॥
प्राक्तन्त्रोत्तरतन्त्रे द्वे स्वशाखाप्रत्यया द्विज ॥
सर्वकर्मसु कर्तव्ये मध्ये कर्म विधीयते ॥ 2.127.50 ॥
अथर्वणोऽयं कथितो विधिस्ते संक्षेपतो भार्गववंशमुख्य ॥
अतः परं किं कथयामि तुभ्यं तन्मे वदस्वायतलोहिताक्ष ॥ 51 ॥

2.26.m:
of a mantra, one should not perform recitation or oblations with that mantra. / Whatever is perceived as unmanifest in meter, Brāhmaṇa, or hymn,
one should determine together with the learned and then introduce into the sacrifice. / The materials that are prescribed, how and where, the substances, and the rite—
the established rule is that whatever is authoritative in that respect corresponds to each Vedic branch. / He who transgresses his own manual and acts according to another's manual,
treating the seer as unauthoritative, incurs demerit. / Therefore, with every effort, one should not transgress one's own manual.
The two rites, the preliminary framework and the concluding framework, based on one's own branch, O twice-born, / are to be performed in all rituals; the main ritual action is prescribed in between.
This procedure belonging to the Atharvan has been told to you in brief, O foremost of the Bhṛgu lineage. / What further shall I tell you after this? Speak that to me, O long- and red-eyed one!
2.128
Rāma said: / Declare a single mantra, O lord, that increases fortune / for each Veda, O lord of the world, son of the king of aquatic beings!

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
श्रीसूक्तं प्रतिवेदञ्च ज्ञेयं लक्ष्मीविवर्धनम् ॥
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके परे वापि यथाकामं द्विजस्य तु॥2॥
राम उवाच ॥
प्रतिवेदं समाचक्ष्व श्रीसूक्तं पुष्टिवर्धनम् ॥

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
हिरण्यवर्णा हरिणीमृचः पञ्चदश द्विज ॥
श्रीसूक्तं कथितं पुण्यमृग्वेदे पुष्टिवर्धनम् ॥4॥
रथे अक्षेषु वाजेति चतस्रस्तु तथा ऋचः ॥
श्रीसूक्तं तु यजुर्वेदे कथितं पुष्टिवर्धनम् 45॥
श्रायन्तीयं तथा मासं सामवेदे प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
श्रियं दातुर्मयि देहि प्रोक्तमाथर्वणे तथा ॥6॥
श्रीसूक्तं यो जपेद्भक्त्या तस्यालक्ष्मीर्विनश्यति ॥
जुहुयाद्यश्च धर्मज्ञ हविष्येण विशेषतः॥7॥
श्रीसूक्तेन तु पद्मानां घृताक्तानां भृगूत्तम ॥
अयुतं होमयेद्यस्तु वह्नौ भक्तियुतो नरः ॥8॥
2.26.m:
Puṣkara said: / The Śrīsūkta is to be understood for each Veda as increasing fortune, / in this world or in the next, according to the wish of a twice-born.
Rāma said: / Declare the Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity for each Veda, / and also the ritual of the Śrīsūkta, O best of all upholders of dharma!
Puṣkara said: / The fifteen verses beginning with 'hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hariṇīm,' O twice-born, / are proclaimed as the meritorious Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity in the Ṛgveda.
The four verses beginning with 'rathe akṣeṣu vājiṣu' / are proclaimed as the Śrīsūkta that increases prosperity in the Yajurveda.
The hymn beginning with 'śrāyantīyam' is proclaimed in the Sāmaveda, / and that beginning with 'śriyaṃ dātarmayi dehi' is declared in the Atharvaveda.
Misfortune is destroyed for him who recites the Śrīsūkta with devotion, / and who offers oblations, O knower of dharma, especially with sacrificial food.
He who offers ten thousand lotuses smeared with clarified butter / in fire with the Śrīsūkta, a man full of devotion, O foremost of the Bhṛgus—

पद्महस्तद्वया लक्ष्मीस्तं नरं तूपतिष्ठति ॥
दशायुतं तु पद्मानां जुहुयाद्यस्तथा जले ॥9॥
नापैति तत्कुलाल्लक्ष्मी विष्णोर्वक्षोगता यथा ॥
घृताक्तानान्तु बिल्वानां हुत्वा रामायुतं तथा ॥ 2.128.10 ॥

बिल्वानां लक्षहोमेन कुले लक्ष्मीमुपाश्नुते ॥11॥
पद्मानामथ बिल्वानां कोटिहोमं समाचरेत् ॥
श्रद्दधानः समाप्नोति देवेन्द्रत्वमपि ध्रुवम् ॥ 12 ॥
संपूज्य देवीं वरदां यथावत्पद्मैः सितैर्वा कुसुमैस्तथान्यैः ॥
क्षीरेण धूपैः परमान्नभक्ष्यैर्लक्ष्मीमवाप्नोति विधानतश्च ॥ 13 ॥

2.26.m:
Lakṣmī, holding lotuses in both hands, waits upon that man. / And he who offers one hundred thousand lotuses in water,
Lakṣmī does not depart from his family, just as she does not leave the chest of Viṣṇu. / Having offered ten thousand bilva fruits smeared with clarified butter, O Rāma,
he obtains abundant wealth, as much as his mind desires. / By offering one hundred thousand bilva fruits, he enjoys Lakṣmī in his family.
One should perform an offering of ten million lotuses or bilva fruits; / full of faith, he certainly attains even the lordship of the gods.
Having duly worshipped the boon-granting goddess with lotuses, white flowers, or other blooms, / with milk, incense, and choice edible offerings, he attains fortune according to rule.
2.129
Rāma said: / Declare a single auspicious mantra that accomplishes all deeds, / both of this world and of the next, O knower of all dharmas!
Puṣkara said: / The hymn remembered as the Pauruṣa for each Veda, O fortunate one, / is to be known as the accomplisher of all deeds, pure, related to the slayer of Madhu.

एकैकया ऋचा राम स्नातो दत्त्वा जलाञ्जलीः ॥
पौरुषेण च सूक्तेन मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥।
अन्तर्जलगतो जप्त्वा तथा सूक्तं तु पौरुषम् ॥
सर्वकल्मषनिर्मुक्तो यथेष्टां लभते गतिम् ॥ 4 ॥
एकैकया ऋचा स्नातः पुष्पं पुष्पं निवेदयेत ॥

एकैकया ऋचा स्नातो दत्त्वा राम फलंफलम् ॥
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति यान्कांश्चिन्मनसेच्छति ॥ 6 ॥
पौरुषेण च सूक्तेन प्राणायामो महाफलः ॥
जपहोमौ तथा राम सर्वकल्मषनाशनौ ॥7॥
सुरापो ब्रह्महा स्तेनस्तथैव गुरुतल्पगः ॥
पापेभ्यो विप्रमुच्येत जप्त्वा सूक्तं तु पौरुषम् ॥ 8 ॥
कृच्छैर्विशोधितः पूर्वं मध्याह्ने सलिलापगः ॥
स्नातस्तु पौरुषं सूक्तं जपेन्नित्यमतन्द्रितः ॥ 9 ॥
संवत्सरेण देवेशं वासुदेवं प्रपश्यति ॥
स्वयमेव महाभाग शाकमूलफलाशनः ॥2.129.10॥
2.26.m:
Having bathed and offered handfuls of water with each verse of the Pauruṣa hymn, O Rāma, / one is freed from all sins. / Having recited the Pauruṣa hymn while submerged in water, / freed from all defilements, one attains whatever destination one desires.
Having bathed, one should offer flowers one by one with each verse / to the Cosmic Person in water, O Rāma; one is freed from all sins.
Having bathed, offering fruits one by one with each verse, O Rāma, / one attains all desires, whatever one wishes in the mind.
Breath control accompanied by the Pauruṣa hymn yields great fruit; / likewise, recitation and oblations, O Rāma, destroy all defilements.
A drinker of liquor, a killer of a brahmin, a thief, and likewise a violator of the guru's bed / are freed from their sins by reciting the Pauruṣa hymn.
Previously purified by penances, having entered the waters at midday, / and having bathed, one should recite the Pauruṣa hymn constantly without slackness.
Within a year, he sees Vāsudeva, the lord of the gods, / in person, O fortunate one, while subsisting on vegetables, roots, and fruits.

यत्र कामावसायित्वं तस्मात्प्राप्नोति मानद ॥

2.26.m:
From him he obtains whatever desire he wishes in his mind, O Rāma: / foremost fortune, beauty, and long life,
the power of atomicity, lightness, reach, and greatness, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / lordship, subjugation, and irresistible will, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
He obtains from him the capacity to fulfill desires wherever they are, O giver of honor, / or whatever else is difficult to attain that he desires in his mind.
Having recited the Pauruṣa hymn constantly without slackness, free of desire, / he goes, O fortunate one, to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
This is taught to be supreme auspiciousness, pure, destroying the flood of worldly miseries, / bestowing happiness, granting dharma to men, and causing the attainment of all delightful things.
2.130
Rāma said: / The duties of the celibate student and the householder have been proclaimed previously; / speak also of the rites and the remaining two stages of life.
Depending on the duties of a householder, O best of gods, / speak to me of those optional rites that remain in the two stages of life.

2.26.m:
Puṣkara said: / Having dwelled happily in the householder stage of life, the twice-born who has duly concluded his studentship / should dwell in the forest, restrained and with his senses duly subdued.
When a householder sees wrinkles and grey hair on himself, / and sees the child of his child, he should then take refuge in the forest.
Abandoning food from the village and all household goods, / entrusting his wife to his sons, or together with her, he should go to the forest.
Taking the agnihotra fires and the domestic fire and utensils, / departing from the village to the forest, he should live with senses conquered.
With pure grains fit for sages of various kinds, or with greens, roots, and fruits, / he should offer all the great sacrifices according to the rule.
He should wear an animal skin or bark, and bathe in the evening and at dawn; / and he should always keep matted locks, a beard, body hair, and nails.
From whatever he has, he should offer bali and alms to the best of his ability; / he should honour those who come to the hermitage with gifts of alms of roots and fruits.

2.26.m:
He should constantly engage in recitation of the Veda, be self-restrained, friendly, composed, / ever a giver, never a receiver, compassionate toward all beings.
And he should offer the agnihotra with the sacrificial fires according to rule, / properly observing the new moon, full moon, and conjunction rites.
He should perform the sacrifice to the lunar mansions, the first-fruits offering, and the four-month sacrifices, / and duly the northern course of the sun and the southern course of the sun.
With pure sage-grains gathered in the spring and autumn, / he should duly offer sacrificial cakes and boiled rice portions separately.
Having offered to the deities that wild, most pure sacrificial oblation, / he should partake of the remainder for himself, as well as salt prepared by himself.
He should eat land-grown and water-grown vegetables, flowers, roots, and fruits / produced from trees, as well as oils extracted from fruits.
He should avoid honey and meat, ground-growing mushrooms, / and bhūstṛṇa grass, horse-radish tree, and bhallātaka fruits.

2.26.m:
In the month of Āśvayuja, he should discard previously gathered sage-grains, / worn-out garments, and flowers, roots, and fruits.
He should not eat what is grown by a ploughshare, even if cast away by someone; / nor food, flowers, and fruits produced in a village.
He may eat food cooked by fire, or he may consume only what is ripened by time; / he may grind with a stone, or use his teeth as a mortar.
He may wash his bowl immediately [having no store], or store for a month, / or store for six months, or store for a year.
He may eat food at night, having gathered it by day to the best of his ability; / or he may eat at every fourth mealtime, or at every eighth mealtime.
Or he may conduct himself according to the rules of the cāndrāyaṇa fast in the bright and dark fortnights; / or at the end of each fortnight he may eat boiled barley gruel once.
Or he may always subsist solely on flowers, roots, and fruits / ripened by time and fallen by themselves, steadfast on the path of the Vaikhānasa.
He may roll upon the ground or stand on the tips of his toes for the day; / he should move between standing and sitting, entering the water at the ritual ablutions.

2.26.m:
In summer he should be five-fire penance-performing; in the rainy season, exposed to the open sky; / and in the cold season, wearing wet clothes, steadily increasing his austerity.
Performing ablutions at the three daily sandhyās, he should satisfy the ancestors and the gods; / undertaking more severe austerity, he should dry up his body.
Having duly deposited the sacred fires within himself, / without fire and without a dwelling, a silent sage eating roots and fruits,
unattached to objects of pleasure, celibate, taking refuge on the bare earth, / indifferent to shelters, having the root of a tree as his abode,
he should collect alms just for sustenance from ascetic brahmins alone, / or from other twice-born householders residing in the forest.
Living in the forest, he should not eat eight mouthfuls brought from a village; / and [he should study] various Upaniṣads and Vedic texts for the purification of the self,
which were practiced by seers, brahmins, and householders, / for the increase of knowledge and austerity and for the purification of the body.
Or, setting out in the unconquered direction, he should walk straight ahead without swerving, / concentrated, subsisting on water and air until the collapse of the body.

2.26.d:
त्यक्त्वा तनुं सम्यगथोदितस्य विधेरथैकस्य वने निवासी ॥
प्राप्नोति लोकं स पितामहस्य त्यक्त्वा भयं नात्र विचारमस्ति ॥ 33 ॥
2.26.m: Having cast off his body by properly following one of the prescribed rules mentioned, a forest-dweller, / casting aside fear, reaches the world of the Grandfather; in this there is no doubt.
